definition_zh: 颅骨；头骨；脑袋；（比喻）头脑
definition_en: the bony framework of the head that encloses the brain, or informally the head itself
core_image: 一只空壳状的硬骨碗，扣住整颗脑袋
scene: 考察队在风化的沙地上挖出一具骨架，最完整的部分是一顶圆弧形的骨盖。The skull was so well preserved that its eye sockets still held sand.
sceneCN: 这里 skull 是「头骨、颅骨」（第 1 个义项：包住脑部的硬骨结构）；句意为头骨保存得很好，眼窝里还积着沙子。

pos.zh: 名词：颅骨；头骨；脑袋；头脑

derivatives.zh: 由 skull 与 cap 复合而成，义为「无檐便帽」
形似本词，义为「阴谋诡计」；只是拼写相近，词源不同
由 skull 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「满脑子的」

senses.title: The bony case that holds the brain
senses.definition: the bones that form the head and enclose the brain, especially in humans and animals
senses.definitionCN: 构成头部并包住脑的骨骼，尤指人与动物的
senses.example: The museum displays the skull of a woolly mammoth.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆里陈列着一只猛犸象的头骨。
senses.why: The Old Norse and Germanic word meant a shell or a bowl, and the rounded bony case is exactly that shape.
senses.whyCN: 古北欧语与日耳曼语中这个词意为「壳、钵」，而圆弧形的骨盒子正是这个形状。

senses.title: A death head as a symbol
senses.definition: a bare skull used as an image of death or danger
senses.definitionCN: 用作死亡或危险形象的光秃头骨
senses.example: The bottle carried a red skull on its label.
senses.exampleCN: 那个瓶子的标签上画着一个红色的骷髅头。
senses.why: A skull outlives the face around it, so it becomes the last visible part of a person and a natural emblem for death.
senses.whyCN: 头骨比脸面留得更久，成为一个人身上最后可见的部分，因此自然成了死亡的标志。

senses.title: The head, in informal talk
senses.definition: a person head, used in informal or humorous speech
senses.definitionCN: 人的脑袋，多用于口语或戏谑的说法
senses.example: Mind your skull, the door frame is low.
senses.exampleCN: 当心脑袋，门框很低。
senses.why: Once the word can mean the whole head, it drifts into casual talk about knocking or covering the head.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词可以指整个脑袋，它就滑进口语中关于撞头、裹头的说法里。

senses.title: The mind inside the head
senses.definition: a person mind, especially in fixed phrases about thinking slowly or stubbornly
senses.definitionCN: 人的头脑，尤用于表示迟钝或固执的固定说法
senses.example: He has a thick skull when it comes to advice.
senses.exampleCN: 一说到别人的建议，他脑子就转不过弯来。
senses.why: A hard skull that will not let a new idea in gives the phrase a thick skull, which then names the mind as well.
senses.whyCN: 坚硬得让新想法进不去的头骨，催生了 thick skull 的说法，进而用来指整个头脑。

intro.en: Skull comes from northern Germanic speech and is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, probably from a word for a shell or a bowl.
intro.cn: skull 来自北部日耳曼语，十四世纪起见于英语，一般认为原意是「壳、钵」。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning shell or hull lies behind the word, shown by the asterisk form.
items.cn: 重构出的词根意为壳、外壳，脚本中写作带星号的形态。

items.en: The Norse word skoltr names a shell or a husk, and northern English borrows from this group.
items.cn: 古北欧语 skoltr 指壳或外皮，英格兰北部英语从这一族词借入。

items.en: Skull is recorded meaning the bone of the head, probably after an earlier word for shell used of the head.
items.cn: skull 见于文献，意为头部的骨头，一般认为沿用了更早用「壳」指头部的说法。

items.en: The bare skull becomes a common emblem of death in art and on tombstones.
items.cn: 光秃的头骨在绘画与墓碑上成为常见的死亡标志。

items.en: Modern English adds phrases about the head and the mind, and compounds such as skullcap.
items.cn: 现代英语为其增添了关于头与脑的习语，以及 skullcap 等复合词。

note.en: Skull names the bone alone, and sits beside cranium, skullcap and, in the wider meaning family, head, brain and bone.
note.cn: skull 单指那块骨头，在形式上靠近 cranium、skullcap，在意义上与 head、brain、bone 同属一个义场。

entries.definition: trickery or dishonest behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 骗取；鬼祟行为；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a small oar, or a light rowing boat
entries.definitionCN: 短桨；单人划艇；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a small round cap fitting the top of the head
entries.definitionCN: 贴合头顶的无檐小帽

entries.definition: the part of the body above the neck
entries.definitionCN: 头

entries.definition: the soft organ inside the skull
entries.definitionCN: 脑

entries.definition: either of the bones that hold the teeth
entries.definitionCN: 颌骨；下巴

normalIntro.en: Skull is a shell word: the round bony case made to hold something soft and precious.
normalIntro.cn: skull 是一个「壳」字：圆形的骨盒子，专为装住柔软珍贵之物而造。

normal.en: Skull goes with skullcap, the cap that sits on the top of the skull.
normal.cn: skullcap 就是戴在头骨顶上的小帽。

normal.en: Skull and crossbones is the old sign for poison and piracy.
normal.cn: skull and crossbones 是从前表示毒物与海盗的老标志。

normal.en: A thick skull means a slow or stubborn head in informal English.
normal.cn: thick skull 在口语里指脑袋迟钝或固执。

normal.en: Compare cranium: cranium is the technical name, skull is the everyday one.
normal.cn: 对比 cranium：cranium 是学术叫法，skull 是日常叫法。

normal.en: Do not confuse skull with scull, the oar, or with skulduggery, the trickery.
normal.cn: 别把 skull 与 scull（短桨）、skulduggery（诡计）混为一词。

abstract.en: Picture a hard white bowl turned upside down on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只坚硬的白色碗倒扣在桌上。

abstract.en: Imagine a small skull sign on a bottle of cleaner.
abstract.cn: 想象清洁剂瓶上画着一个小小的骷髅标志。

abstract.en: Think of a helmet that looks like a bare head of bone.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶头盔，外形就像一颗光秃的骨制头颅。

examples.en: The fossil skull was found in a cave in the hills.
examples.cn: 化石头骨是在山间的一处洞穴里发现的。

examples.en: The label warns you with a skull and crossbones.
examples.cn: 标签上用一个骷髅交叉骨图案提醒你。

examples.en: He has a thick skull and never listens to advice.
examples.cn: 他这人死脑筋，从不听劝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死扣」——头骨是扣在脑子上的一层硬壳，像把盖子死扣上去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自古北欧语一系表示「壳、钵」的词（同源形式如古北欧语 skoltr），十四世纪进入英语，核心义为「包住脑部的硬壳」。

sensesIntro.en: Skull begins as the bony shell of the head, becomes the emblem of death, and then loosens informally into the head and the mind it holds.
sensesIntro.cn: skull 先是包住脑的骨壳，再成为死亡的象征，最后在口语中松弛地指脑袋乃至其中的头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard bowl of bone turned over the brain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只硬骨碗扣在脑上。

branches.en: The anatomical sense keeps the old shell image in bone.
branches.cn: 解剖义项把古老的壳意象留在骨骼上。

branches.en: A bare skull outlasts the face, so it stands for death.
branches.cn: 光秃的头骨比脸面留存更久，于是代表死亡。

branches.en: Informal speech stretches the part to name the whole head.
branches.cn: 口语把部分放大，用头骨来指整个脑袋。

branches.en: The hard case also names the mind that works inside it.
branches.cn: 坚硬的骨壳也用来指在里面运转的头脑。

branches.en: Anthropologists and painters both read a skull, one for age, one for death.
branches.cn: 人类学家与画家都读头骨，一个看年龄，一个看死亡。

intro.en: Skull has no living prefix or suffix of its own; its word family is made by compounding and a few late suffixes.
intro.cn: skull 本身没有仍在使用的前缀或后缀，它的词族主要靠复合与少量后加词缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Classical Latin has no direct relative of skull, so none is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 古典拉丁语没有与 skull 直接同源的词，因此这里不作列举。

items.meaning: the bony case of the head
items.example: Skull is the everyday noun for the bones of the head.
items.exampleCN: skull 是表示头骨的日常名词。

items.example: The ending -s forms skulls.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 skulls。

items.example: Skulls line the shadowed walls of the old chapel.
items.exampleCN: 头骨排列在古老小教堂阴暗的墙上。

items.meaningCN: 与头骨相关的构词成分
items.example: The element skull- joins cap to make a new noun.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 skull- 与 cap 组合成新名词。

items.example: Skullcap is built from skull and cap.
items.exampleCN: skullcap 由 skull 与 cap 复合而成。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms skullful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 skullful。

items.meaning: having a head full of something
items.example: Skullful is a playful, seldom used word.
items.exampleCN: skullful 是一个带有戏谑色彩、极少使用的词。

items.meaning: a mere spelling that looks like a prefix
items.meaningCN: 仅是拼写巧合，并非词缀
items.example: The letters ski- in skull are not a prefix at all.
items.exampleCN: skull 开头的 ski 并非前缀。

definition_zh: 价格、数量或水平迅速飙升；猛涨；暴涨
definition_en: to rise very quickly to a high level, especially of prices, costs, or numbers
core_image: 一支烟火弹「嗖」地从地面蹿上天，在夜空里炸开
scene: 加油站前的电子牌每隔一周就换一个更高的数字，开车的人看了直摇头。Fuel costs skyrocketed after two refineries were forced to close.
sceneCN: 这里 skyrocket 是「猛涨、飙升」（第 1 个义项：价格突然涨到很高）；句意为两家炼油厂被迫停产后，燃油成本猛涨。图中的电子牌与加油站雨棚是这一用法的典型场景。

pos.zh: 动词：价格、数量迅速飙升；猛涨

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「飙升的；暴涨的」，如「飙升的房价」
同一构词核心的动词，义为「飞速上升；猛增」，比 skyrocket 稍口语、语势稍弱
本词第一部分的名词，义为「天空」，与上半部分合成这一比喻

senses.title: Prices or costs rise very fast
senses.definition: to increase very quickly and steeply in price or cost, often beyond what people expect
senses.definitionCN: 价格或成本迅速而陡峭地上涨，常超出人们的预期
senses.example: House prices have skyrocketed in the last two years.
senses.exampleCN: 过去两年房价猛涨。
senses.why: The core image is a firework called a sky rocket shooting up into the sky, and the steep, sudden climb of prices looks exactly like that flight.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是名为「冲天炮」的烟火直冲夜空；物价那种又陡又突然的攀升，看起来正像这道飞升的轨迹。

senses.title: Numbers or statistics jump
senses.definition: of figures, sales, users, or similar data, to grow extremely rapidly
senses.definitionCN: 指数字、销量、用户数等数据极快地增长
senses.example: Online sales skyrocketed during the holiday season.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间线上销量激增。
senses.why: Anything counted can be drawn as a line on a chart, and a skyrocketing curve is a line that turns almost straight upward.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能计数的事物都能在统计图上画成一条线，而 skyrocketing 的曲线就是几乎竖直向上的那条线。

senses.title: Fame or popularity takes off
senses.definition: to become suddenly and extremely popular or successful
senses.definitionCN: 突然变得极受欢迎或极成功
senses.example: The band skyrocketed to fame after one video went viral.
senses.exampleCN: 这段视频走红后，这支乐队一夜成名。
senses.why: Fireworks burst in the sky where everyone can see them, so sudden fame is pictured as something exploding into public view.
senses.whyCN: 烟火在空中炸开，人人都能看见，于是骤然成名被描绘成某种东西在众目睽睽之下爆开。

senses.title: A level or rate races upward
senses.definition: of a level, rate, or temperature, to climb to an extreme point very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 指水平、比率或温度极快攀升到极端的程度
senses.example: Temperatures skyrocketed to forty degrees in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 城里的气温一路飙升到四十度。
senses.why: The noun rocket carried the general sense of anything that shoots up fast, and the height of the sky sets no visible limit on how far the climb can go.
senses.whyCN: rocket 一词本来就泛指任何飞快窜升之物，而「天」的高度让这种攀升几乎看不到尽头。

intro.en: Skyrocket joins the noun sky to rocket, a small firework that shoots into the air; English turned the compound into a verb for anything that rises explosively.
intro.cn: skyrocket 由 sky「天空」与 rocket（一种升空的烟火）合成；英语把这一合成词用作动词，指任何爆炸式上升的事物。

items.en: Rocket first names a small cylindrical firework launched by a guide stick, and a sky rocket is one that flies high into the air.
items.cn: rocket 最初指一种用导杆发射的圆筒形烟火，sky rocket 指飞得很高的那种炮仗。

items.en: Fireworks displays make the jumping firework a familiar picture of something shooting straight up.
items.cn: 烟火表演让这种蹿升的火光成为「直冲而上」的常见画面。

items.en: The compound sky rocket is written as one word and the idea of a sudden rise begins to colour it.
items.cn: sky rocket 合写成 skyrocket，词义中开始渗入「突然上升」的意思。

items.en: Skyrocketing becomes a standard word for prices and figures going up out of control.
items.cn: skyrocketing 成为表示物价与数字失控上涨的常用词。

items.en: Today the verb is mostly figurative: prices, costs, rates and fame are what skyrocket.
items.cn: 今天这个词作动词多为比喻用法，飙升的通常是价格、成本、比率与名气。

items.en: The rocket in this firework sense is generally traced to Italian rocchetta, a small spindle; the link to the space rocket is separate and later.
items.cn: 烟火义的 rocket 一般认为来自意大利语 rocchetta（小纺锤）；与后来指航天火箭的 rocket 是另一条线，年代也更晚。

note.en: Skyrocket is a compound of sky and the firework rocket; its look-alikes sit in the rocket family, while its near meanings are the ordinary verbs for a fast rise.
note.cn: skyrocket 是 sky 与烟火 rocket 的合成词：形近词都在 rocket 词族里，近义词则是普通的「快速上升」动词。

entries.definition: The second half of the compound, both the firework and the vehicle, and on its own a verb for rising very fast.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烟火；火箭」，是本词的后半部分；单独作动词时也表示「飞涨」。

entries.definition: A compound built on sky that means the outline of tall buildings against the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天际线」，同样由 sky 作前半部分构成，指高楼映在天上的轮廓。

entries.definition: An adjective or adverb meaning towards the sky, keeping the upward image of the first half.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「朝向天空的」，保留了前半部分「向上」的意象。

entries.definition: The lark that sings as it flies high; it is spelled like a sky compound but names a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「云雀」，指高飞鸣唱的百灵；虽同样是 sky 的合成词，指的却是一种鸟。

entries.definition: To rise quickly to a high level, often with an image of gliding; slightly more literary than skyrocket.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「猛增；翱翔」，带滑翔的画面，比 skyrocket 稍文雅。

entries.definition: To increase suddenly and strongly, often in a wave, used of prices, demand or power.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激增」，指像浪潮一样突然而有力地增长，多用于价格、需求和电力。

entries.definition: To rise or fall ever faster in a worsening cycle, as in spiralling costs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「螺旋式上升或恶化」，指在恶性循环中越来越快地变化，如成本螺旋上升。

entries.definition: To fall very sharply, the exact opposite of skyrocketing; it also comes from a weight on a line.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「暴跌」，与 skyrocket 正好相反；它同样源自垂线上的重锤。

normalIntro.en: The word is built out of two ordinary pieces, sky and the firework rocket, so the picture is already inside the spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两个普通部件拼成：sky 与烟火 rocket，画面本身就藏在拼写里。

normal.en: Sky plus rocket: the thing that shoots into the sky is exactly the shape of a price line going straight up.
normal.cn: sky 加 rocket：冲天而去的那个东西，形状正是一条竖直上升的价格线。

normal.en: The verb has no noun sense of its own; sky rockets are the noun, and skyrocket is the flight.
normal.cn: 这个动词本身没有名词义：名词是 sky rocket（冲天炮），而 skyrocket 指那一道飞行。

normal.en: Skyrocketing prices is the most common collocation, so where there is a price tag, there can be a skyrocket.
normal.cn: skyrocketing prices 是最常见的搭配：只要有标价的地方，就可能有 skyrocket。

normal.en: Remember the pair: skyrocket goes up, plummet comes down, and both began as objects that moved fast.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：skyrocket 往上窜，plummet 往下坠，两者原本都是快速移动的实物。

normal.en: In news writing, skyrocket is usually followed by an amount or a percentage, as in skyrocketed to eighteen percent.
normal.cn: 新闻写作中 skyrocket 后面常跟数值或百分比，例如 skyrocketed to eighteen percent。

abstract.en: Picture a chart on a desk, and a glowing firework is shooting up along the right edge of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的一张图表，一枚发光的烟火正沿着纸的右缘往上冲。

abstract.en: Watch a crowd below look upward all at once: a sky rocket makes every face tilt back.
abstract.cn: 看下面的人群同时抬头：一枚冲天炮让每一张脸都向后仰。

abstract.en: A skyrocket leaves nothing behind on the ground; a sudden rise changes the price, not the world underneath it.
abstract.cn: 冲天炮在地面什么也不留下；骤然的上涨改变的是价格，而不是它下面的世界。

examples.en: Food prices skyrocketed after the drought destroyed most of the harvest.
examples.cn: 旱灾毁掉大部分收成后，食品价格暴涨。

examples.en: The number of online learners skyrocketed during the first year of the course.
examples.cn: 课程第一年，在线学习的人数激增。

examples.en: Rents in the city centre are still skyrocketing, forcing young families to move away.
examples.cn: 市中心的租金仍在飞涨，逼得年轻家庭纷纷搬走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死盖罗凯特」——拆开是 sky 加 rocket，天上的火箭「嗖」地往上窜，像物价一夜飙高；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: sky「天空」+ rocket（烟火：冲天炮）→ skyrocket；rocket 的烟火义一般认为来自意大利语 rocchetta「小纺锤」，与指航天火箭的后起用法分属两条线索。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses all borrow the flight of a firework: prices climb steeply, figures jump, fame explodes into view, and any level races upward.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都借用了烟火的升空轨迹：价格陡升、数字激增、名气骤然爆开、任何水平急速攀升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a firework rockets off the ground and bursts high in the night sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚烟火弹从地面蹿起，在夜空中高处炸开。

branches.en: MONEY: a price line that rises as steeply as a launched firework.
branches.cn: 金钱线：像发射出去的烟火一样陡直上升的价格曲线。

branches.en: NUMBERS: counted things leave the page and shoot up on the chart.
branches.cn: 数字线：可计数的东西离开纸面，在图表上直冲而上。

branches.en: FAME: the burst in the sky is seen by everyone, so sudden success is visible to all.
branches.cn: 名气线：空中的爆开人人都看得见，于是骤然成功也就人人有目共睹。

branches.en: RATES: any measured level climbs without a visible ceiling.
branches.cn: 比率线：任何被测量的水平都能一路攀升，看不到天花板。

branches.en: Both a price and a rate have the same grammar: skyrocket plus to plus a figure.
branches.cn: 价格与比率语法相同：skyrocket 后接 to 再接一个具体数值。

intro.en: Skyrocket is an English compound, not a Latin word: sky sets the direction and rocket supplies the flying object.
intro.cn: skyrocket 是英语自身的合成词，不是拉丁语词：sky 定方向，rocket 提供那件飞行的东西。

latinIntro.en: Neither half comes from Latin: sky is a native English word, and rocket is generally traced to an Italian name for a spindle.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部件都不来自拉丁语：sky 是英语本族词，rocket 一般认为来自意大利语指「小纺锤」的词。

items.example: Sky sets the direction, from the ground upward.
items.exampleCN: sky 设定方向：从地面往上。

items.example: The firework sense is the older one.
items.exampleCN: 烟火义是较早的那个意思。

items.meaning: sky as the front part of compounds
items.meaningCN: 作复合词前半部分的「天空」
items.example: The same first part forms skyline and skyward.
items.exampleCN: 同一个前半部分还构成 skyline 与 skyward。

items.example: It appears in rocchetta, the probable source of rocket.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 rocchetta 里，后者是 rocket 可能的来源。

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词或形容词
items.example: It forms skyrocketing as in skyrocketing prices.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 skyrocketing，如 skyrocketing prices。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: It forms skyrocketed and skyrockets.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 skyrocketed 与 skyrockets。

items.meaning: noun joined to noun to make a new noun
items.meaningCN: 名词与名词合成新名词的构词方式
items.example: Sky plus rocket gives one word for a high firework.
items.exampleCN: sky 与 rocket 合成一个词，指飞得高的烟火。

items.meaning: a noun used as a verb with no ending added
items.meaningCN: 名词不加词尾直接用作动词
items.example: The noun rocket became the verb to rocket without any change.
items.exampleCN: 名词 rocket 不作任何改动就成了动词 to rocket。

items.meaning: a physical image applied to abstract things
items.meaningCN: 把具体形象用于抽象事物
items.example: The flight of the firework now describes prices.
items.exampleCN: 烟火的飞升如今用来描述价格。

definition_zh: 摩天大楼；超高层建筑
definition_en: a very tall building, especially one whose upper floors reach close to the clouds
core_image: 一栋玻璃高楼把顶楼伸到云层边上，仿佛能刮擦天空
scene: 傍晚从河对岸望去，一片玻璃墙面的高楼把天际线切成锯齿。The skyscrapers along the river turned gold as the sun went down.
sceneCN: 这里 skyscraper 是「摩天大楼」（第 1 个义项：极高的城市建筑）；句意为夕阳西下时，河岸边那些摩天大楼变成了金色。图中可辨识的是玻璃外墙与密集的窗格。

pos.zh: 名词：摩天大楼；超高层建筑

collocations.zh: 一座现代化的摩天大楼
摩天大楼区；高楼林立的街区

derivatives.zh: 同一 sky 词族的合成词，义为「天际线」，常与 skyscraper 搭配出现
本词后半部分的动词，义为「刮擦」，提供了这一形象的动作
由 scrape 加 -er 构成的名词，义为「刮擦器」，后接于 sky 组成本词

senses.title: A very tall building
senses.definition: a building with many floors, so tall that it dominates its city skyline
senses.definitionCN: 楼层极多、高得足以主宰一座城市天际线的建筑
senses.example: The new skyscraper has sixty floors and a rooftop garden.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋新摩天大楼有六十层，楼顶还有一座花园。
senses.why: The word is a compound of the verb to scrape and the noun sky: a building high enough that its top seems to graze the sky.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由动词 scrape「刮擦」与名词 sky「天空」合成：楼高到顶端似乎能蹭到天。

senses.title: A symbol of a modern city
senses.definition: a landmark high-rise that stands for a city identity, its wealth or its ambition
senses.definitionCN: 代表一座城市身份、财富或雄心的地标高建筑
senses.example: That skyscraper appears on every postcard of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 那座摩天大楼出现在这座城市的每一张明信片上。
senses.why: A sky-high building is visible from everywhere, so it easily becomes the face a city shows the world.
senses.whyCN: 高耸入云的建筑处处可见，于是很容易成为一座城市向世界展示的那张脸。

senses.title: A tower that broke height records
senses.titleCN: 不断刷新高度的超高层建筑
senses.definition: a structure designed to reach a new record height, especially in the era of steel frames and lifts
senses.definitionCN: 以刷新高度纪录为目标而设计的建筑，尤指钢框架与电梯时代的产物
senses.example: Each new skyscraper in the nineteen twenties tried to be taller than the last.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年代的每一座新摩天楼都想比前一座更高。
senses.why: The word labels buildings by the extreme of height, so it naturally gathers around records, elevation and the question of which building is tallest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词用「高度之极」来给建筑命名，因此往往围绕纪录、海拔以及「谁最高」这些话题。

intro.en: Skyscraper is an English compound formed in the late nineteenth century, putting a name for a tall ship onto a new kind of tall building.
intro.cn: skyscraper 是十九世纪后期形成的英语合成词：它把原本指高船桅杆的名称，套用到一种新的高层建筑上。

items.en: The sailor word skyscraper means a sky sail, a small sail set high above the topsail of a ship.
items.cn: 航海中的 skyscraper 指「高帆」，即挂在中桅帆上方高处的小帆。

items.en: Skyscraper is applied to anything very tall, from a tall hat to a high horse.
items.cn: skyscraper 被用来指任何很高的东西，从高帽子到高头大马。

items.en: With steel frames and safe lifts, buildings rise many storeys in American cities, and newspapers begin to call them skyscrapers.
items.cn: 有了钢框架与安全电梯，美国城市的楼房盖起许多层，报纸开始把它们叫作 skyscraper。

items.en: The word settles into meaning a very tall building, and is borrowed whole by many other languages.
items.cn: 这个词固定下来专指极高的建筑，并被许多其他语言整体借入。

items.en: Today skyscraper chiefly means an office or residential tower of exceptional height, in contrast with a mid-rise block.
items.cn: 今天 skyscraper 主要指高度异常突出的办公塔楼或住宅塔楼，与中层建筑形成对照。

note.en: Skyscraper is one member of the large sky family of compounds and informal names; its near meanings are the other words for very tall buildings.
note.cn: skyscraper 是庞大的 sky 合成词与俗称家族中的一员；近义词则是其他指「极高建筑」的说法。

entries.definition: The outline of buildings and other shapes seen against the sky, formed from the same first half of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天际线」，指映在天空上的建筑轮廓，与本词共用前半部分。

entries.definition: To hijack an aircraft, made by blending sky with hijack; a different compound with the same sky opener.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「劫机」，由 sky 与 hijack 混合而成；同样以 sky 开头，但意思完全不同。

entries.definition: A window set in a roof to let daylight in from the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天窗」，指开在屋顶上采光用的窗。

entries.definition: A view or picture of the sky itself, built on sky with the ending of landscape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天空景色」，以 sky 加上 landscape 的结尾构成。

entries.definition: A tall narrow structure, often standing alone; it stresses narrow height rather than many floors.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「塔」，多指独立的高而窄的建筑，强调窄高而非楼层众多。

entries.definition: A building with many floors; technical and neutral, without the dramatic picture of scraping the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「高层的、高层建筑」，属中性术语，不带「刮天」的形象。

entries.definition: A building of only a few floors; the modest opposite of a skyscraper in height.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「中低层建筑」，在高度上与摩天大楼形成朴素的对照。

entries.definition: In British English, a large building divided into flats or offices; plainer and much less emphatic than skyscraper.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语中义为「大楼、公寓楼」，比 skyscraper 朴素得多，语气平实。

normalIntro.en: The picture is written into the word itself: something that scrapes the sky, first a sail, then a building.
normalIntro.cn: 画面就写在这个词里：一样刮着天空的东西，先是帆，后是楼。

normal.en: Scrape means to rub against a surface; a skyscraper is the building that rubs up against the sky.
normal.cn: scrape 意为摩擦表面；skyscraper 就是一直蹭到天上去的那栋楼。

normal.en: The compound has a plural in -s only, because it is one noun: skyscrapers, and nothing else changes.
normal.cn: 这个词只有加 -s 的复数形式，因为它是一个名词：skyscrapers，不要在同一处再加塔楼一词重复。

normal.en: Remember the nautical start: a sky sail was the small sail set highest, above the topsail.
normal.cn: 记住它的航海出身：高帆是挂得最高、位于中桅帆之上的小帆。

normal.en: Compare skyline: skyscrapers make the skyline, and the two words share the same sky.
normal.cn: 对比 skyline：摩天大楼造出天际线，两个词共用同一个 sky。

normal.en: A mid-rise has a few floors, a high-rise has many, and a skyscraper is the one that dominates the sky above them all.
normal.cn: 中层楼只有几层，高层楼楼层很多，而摩天大楼是高出这一切、占满头顶天空的那一座。

abstract.en: Picture a child running a finger along the underside of the clouds, as if the solid roof could scrape them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子用指尖划过云层的底部，仿佛坚实的屋顶真能把它刮下一点来。

abstract.en: See a ship mast in open sea, then the same picture turned vertical and filled with windows.
abstract.cn: 先看开阔海面上的一根船桅，再把同一幅画面竖起来、填满窗格。

abstract.en: A skyscraper makes a city feel taller than its streets; stand on the pavement and look up until your neck aches.
abstract.cn: 摩天大楼让城市比街道本身更高；站在人行道上抬头仰望，直到脖子发酸。

examples.en: The glass skyscraper reflects the sunset so brightly that drivers slow down to look.
examples.cn: 那座玻璃摩天楼把落日映得极亮，司机们都放慢车速来看。

examples.en: Engineers designed the skyscraper so that it can sway in strong winds without cracking.
examples.cn: 工程师的设计让这座摩天大楼在强风中能够轻微摇摆而不开裂。

examples.en: Several skyscrapers now stand where the old market used to be.
examples.cn: 如今在旧市场的位置上矗立着好几座摩天大楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「刮天空」——sky 是天空，scrape 是刮擦，楼高得能刮到天，就是摩天大楼；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: sky「天空」+ scrape「刮擦」+-er 构成的名词 → skyscraper；字母次序上 scrape 需要换位成 scrap，再与 sky 合成。这个词最初是航海词，指「高帆」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses all grow from the same extreme of height: a very tall building itself, that building as a symbol of the city, and the record-breaking tower.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都从同一个「高度之极」长出：极高的建筑本体、作为城市象征的那栋楼，以及不断刷新纪录的塔楼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass tower whose top floors seem to graze the clouds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋玻璃高楼，顶楼仿佛蹭着云。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: many floors stacked so high that the roof sits near the weather.
branches.cn: 建筑线：楼层层层叠加，高到屋顶接近天气变化的高度。

branches.en: THE CITY FACE: what is tallest is what gets photographed, posted and drawn on banknotes.
branches.cn: 城市面孔线：最高的那一座最容易被拍下来、印在明信片上、画在纸币上。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a word built around an extreme raises the question of who is highest.
branches.cn: 纪录线：以「高度之极」造出的词，自然会引出「谁最高」这个问题。

branches.en: Both depend on the same engineering: steel frames and lifts let a building be taller than a stair can allow.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖同样的技术：钢框架与电梯让建筑高过楼梯所能达到的限度。

branches.en: A landmark and a record holder are often the same tower, and the second title becomes a selling point for the first.
branches.cn: 地标与纪录保持者常常是同一座塔，而第二个头衔又成了第一个头衔的卖点。

intro.en: Skyscraper is built from an ordinary English verb, an ordinary English noun, and an -er ending; there is no Latin part in it.
intro.cn: skyscraper 由一个普通英语动词、一个普通英语名词和词尾 -er 构成，其中没有拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native English words, so the family has no Latin ancestors to list here; sky has a very old Germanic origin.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部件都是英语本族词，因此这一词族没有可列为拉丁祖先的词；sky 有非常古老的日耳曼来源。

items.example: Sky is the object that the building seems to scrape.
items.exampleCN: 天空是这栋楼仿佛在刮擦的对象。

items.meaning: to rub against a hard surface
items.example: Branches can scrape against a window.
items.exampleCN: 树枝会刮擦窗玻璃。

items.meaning: the person or thing that does the action
items.example: The suffix turns scrape into scraper, the thing that scrapes.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 scrape 变成 scraper，即「刮擦的东西」。

items.meaning: sky as the front part of compounds
items.meaningCN: 作复合词前半部分的「天空」
items.example: It also builds skyline and skylight.
items.exampleCN: 它还构成 skyline 与 skylight。

items.meaning: a view or scene of a kind
items.example: With sky it forms skyscape, a view of the sky.
items.exampleCN: 与 sky 合成 skyscape，指「天空景色」。

items.example: High-rise is the plainer term for a tall building.
items.exampleCN: high-rise 是表示高楼的更朴素的说法。

items.example: Skyscrapers is the only form change the noun takes.
items.exampleCN: skyscrapers 是这个名词唯一的形态变化。

items.meaning: noun joined to noun to make a new noun
items.meaningCN: 名词与名词合成新名词的构词方式
items.example: Sky plus scraper produces a single new noun.
items.exampleCN: sky 与 scraper 合成一个全新的名词。

items.meaning: a compound copied whole into other languages
items.meaningCN: 整词被其他语言借入的方式
items.example: Languages such as German and Japanese carry their own version of this compound.
items.exampleCN: 德语、日语等语言都各有本语言的这一合成词版本。

definition_zh: 放松；松懈；（速度）减慢；使松弛
definition_en: to become or make something less tight, less quick, or less active
core_image: 绷紧的绳索被人一点点松开，绳面开始下垂
scene: 一匹拉着车的马跑到山坡上，赶车人松开缰绳，让它慢下来喘口气。The driver slackened the reins as the cart climbed the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 slacken 是「放松、松开」（第 1 个义项：把原本绷紧的东西放松）；句意为车子爬坡时，赶车人松开了缰绳。图中可辨识的是缰绳与被拉开的车辕。

pos.zh: 动词：放松、松开；松懈；减慢；使松弛

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础形容词，义为「松的；松弛的；懈怠的」，加 -en 后缀构成动词
由基础形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「松弛；松懈；萧条」
由基础形容词加 -er 构成，义为「偷懒的人、懈怠者」，口语色彩较强

senses.title: To make something less tight
senses.definition: to make or become less tight, as with a rope, a grip, or a belt
senses.definitionCN: 使绳索、握力或皮带等变得不那么紧或自行变松
senses.example: She slackened her grip on the rail and stepped down carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 她松开扶手，小心地走下台阶。
senses.why: The verb is the adjective slack, meaning not tight, plus the old verb ending -en that means to make or become.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由形容词 slack「松的、不紧的」加古动词词尾 -en 构成，-en 表示「使……或变得……」。

senses.title: To slow down
senses.definition: of a runner, a machine, or an activity, to become slower or less intense
senses.definitionCN: 指跑步的人、机器或某种活动变慢或强度降低
senses.example: The runners slackened their pace in the last kilometre.
senses.exampleCN: 跑者在最后一公里放慢了速度。
senses.why: A tight rhythm is a fist of effort; slackening the rope lets the pace loosen, so a slower rate is the same looseness applied to motion.
senses.whyCN: 紧绷的节奏像握紧的拳头；松开绳子，速度也就松了下来，于是「慢下来」就是把同一种松弛用到运动上。

senses.title: To become less strong or active
senses.definition: of a wind, a storm, rain, or demand, to lose force or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 指风、暴风雨、雨或需求等失去力量或强度
senses.example: The storm began to slacken soon after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜刚过不久，暴风雨就开始减弱。
senses.why: Force can be pictured as a taut cable; when the cable slackens, the force it carried loosens too, so a dying wind is a slackening grip.
senses.whyCN: 力量可以想象成一根绷紧的缆绳；缆绳一松，它承载的力量也随之松开，于是渐弱的风就是一只慢慢松开的握力。

senses.title: To stop trying as hard
senses.definition: to relax your effort or attention, often when it should not happen
senses.definitionCN: 放松努力或注意力，往往是在不该放松的时候
senses.example: Do not slacken your efforts in the final week of revision.
senses.exampleCN: 复习的最后一周不要松懈。
senses.why: A slack rope holds no load; when effort slackens, the will stops pulling tight, and the same word covers a relaxed body and a relaxed discipline.
senses.whyCN: 松掉的绳索承不住重量；努力一松懈，意志也不再绷紧，同一个词于是既能指放松的身体，也能指松弛的纪律。

intro.en: Slacken is formed inside English from the adjective slack plus a verb ending, and slack itself is very old and its earlier history is uncertain.
intro.cn: slacken 是在英语内部形成的：形容词 slack 加上动词词尾；而 slack 本身非常古老，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Slæc is recorded as an adjective meaning lazy, slow or loose.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 slæc 已有记载，义为「懒散的、迟缓的、松的」。

items.en: The deeper origin of slæc is uncertain; it is generally linked to Scandinavian words for loose and slow, but is not securely reconstructed.
items.cn: slæc 更早的来源不确定，一般与北欧语中表示「松、慢」的词相联系，但并无可靠的构拟。

items.en: Slack keeps the senses of loose, slow and careless, and begins to be used of rope, sails and gait.
items.cn: 中古英语的 slack 仍兼有「松、慢、懒」诸义，并开始用于绳索、帆与步态。

items.en: The verb slacken is formed with the old ending that means to make or become, as in lengthen and quicken.
items.cn: slacken 由表示「使……、变得……」的古词尾构成，如 lengthen 与 quicken 的构词方式。

items.en: The verbs slacken and slacken off spread from ropes and winds to pace, effort and demand.
items.cn: 动词 slacken 与 slacken off 的用法从绳索、风，扩展到速度、努力与需求。

note.en: Slacken belongs to a short English family built on slack, and its look-alikes are the words that share that stem; its near meanings are the other verbs for loosening or slowing.
note.cn: slacken 属于以 slack 为核心的小词族，形近词都是共享这个词干的词；近义词则是其他表示「放松或减速」的动词。

entries.definition: The base adjective and noun meaning not tight or not busy; slacken is formed directly from it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「松的；萧条的」，是本词的直接基础。

entries.definition: A person who avoids work, formed from slack with the ending that names a person who acts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「偷懒的人」，由 slack 加表示人的后缀构成。

entries.definition: The state of being loose, careless or quiet in business, from slack with the noun ending.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「松弛；懈怠；生意清淡」，由 slack 加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: The act of becoming looser or slower, or an adjective for something easing off.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「放松；放缓」，指变松或变慢的过程。

entries.definition: To make something less tight; built with the same verb ending and used of screws, belts and rules.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变松」，与 slacken 用同一类词尾，多用于螺丝、皮带与规则。

entries.definition: To become or make less tense; often used of muscles and people, and a calmer word than slacken.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放松」，多用于肌肉与人，比 slacken 语气更平和。

entries.definition: The comparative of slow, carrying the speed sense of sense two without the rope image.
entries.definitionCN: slow 的比较级，承接「放慢」这一义项，但没有绳索的画面。

entries.definition: To become or make less severe or less fast; an everyday verb for rain or traffic that lets up.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缓和、减弱」，常用于雨势或交通缓解，是日常说法。

entries.definition: To become or make firm and tight, the exact opposite of slackening a rope or a grip.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变硬、变紧」，与松开绳子和松手正好相反。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work from the base word slack and from the -en ending it shares with a whole group of verbs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子都从基础词 slack 出发，并利用它与一整组动词共有的 -en 词尾。

normal.en: Slack plus -en: the adjective becomes the verb of making loose, just as wide becomes widen.
normal.cn: slack 加 -en：形容词变成表示「使变松」的动词，如同 wide 变成 widen。

normal.en: Slacken off is the everyday phrasal form, so remember the pair: slacken a rope, slacken off at work.
normal.cn: slacken off 是日常的短语形式，记住这一对：松开绳子，工作上放慢松懈。

normal.en: Slacken the reins is the image at the heart of the word: you stop pulling, and the horse decides its own speed.
normal.cn: slacken the reins 正是这个词的核心画面：你不再拉紧，马自己决定速度。

normal.en: Watch the collocations: slacken the pace, slacken speed and slacken the reins all put a noun after the verb, while slacken off stands alone.
normal.cn: 注意这些搭配：slacken the pace、slacken speed、slacken the reins 都是动词后接名词，而 slacken off 则单独使用。

normal.en: English often uses the ending that makes verbs from adjectives, and slacken sits beside lengthen, quicken and stiffen.
normal.cn: 英语常用 -en 这类词尾由形容词造动词，slacken 正与 lengthen、quicken、stiffen 同列。

abstract.en: Watch a climbing rope hanging between two hands: fingers open, and the line drops into a curve.
abstract.cn: 看双手之间绷着的攀登绳：手指一松，绳子就垂成一道弧。

abstract.en: Now put a clock inside that rope: as it sags, the ticking slows, so looseness and slowness are one picture.
abstract.cn: 再往绳子里放一只钟：绳子越下垂，滴答声就越慢，于是「松」与「慢」成了同一幅画面。

abstract.en: Hold a heavy bag by the handle, then let the fingers relax one by one; the bag slides down without making any sound.
abstract.cn: 抓着沉重袋子的提手，再一根根手指松开；袋子悄无声息地滑下去。

examples.en: The doctor told him to slacken the bandage so that blood could flow freely.
examples.cn: 医生让他把绷带放松，好让血液流通。

examples.en: Rain slackened in the early morning, and the streets began to fill again.
examples.cn: 清晨雨势减弱，街上又渐渐有人了。

examples.en: Sales slackened in the winter, so the shop cut its opening hours.
examples.cn: 冬季销量放缓，于是这家店缩短了营业时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死来肯」——死拉着的绳子肯放开了，就是放松、松懈；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语形容词 slack「松的；懒散的；萧条的」+ 词尾 -en（使……、变得……）→ slacken；slack 可追溯至古英语 slæc，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are one image of a rope going loose, applied to a rope and a grip, to pace, to wind and rain, and finally to effort and attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都是「绳子变松」这一幅画面，分别用到绳索与握力、速度、风雨，最后落到努力与注意力上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut rope is let go, and the line begins to sag.
core.cn: 核心意象：绷紧的绳子被放开，绳面开始下垂。

branches.en: THE HANDS: a grip, a belt or a railway tension that is made less tight.
branches.cn: 双手线：握力、皮带或缆绳的张力被放松。

branches.en: THE SPEED: a machine or a runner works with less tension and therefore moves more slowly.
branches.cn: 速度线：机器或跑者的用力变松，速度随之变慢。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: a wind or a storm loses the pull it had on the air.
branches.cn: 天气线：风或暴风雨失去了对空气的那股拉拽力。

branches.en: THE WILL: a person stops pulling tight inside, so effort and attention slacken.
branches.cn: 意志线：人在内心里不再绷紧，于是努力与注意力随之松懈。

branches.en: All three describe a drop in tension, and in all three the thing that changes is speed-like: tightness, force and rate.
branches.cn: 三者都描述张力的下降，而三者里变化的东西都与快慢相关：紧度、力量与速率。

intro.en: Slacken is a purely English formation: an old adjective slack plus the verb ending -en, with the rest of the family built by ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: slacken 是纯英语构词：古老的形容词 slack 加上动词词尾 -en，词族其余成员由普通后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for this family, only an old English adjective whose own origin is uncertain, so no Latin same-root words appear here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族没有拉丁祖先，只有一个来源不确定的古英语形容词，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The base word already contains both looseness and laziness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根已经兼含「松」与「懒」两面。

items.example: The suffix turns slack into the verb slacken.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 slack 变成动词 slacken。

items.example: It forms slackness, the state of being slack.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 slackness，即「松弛的状态」。

items.meaning: a person who does the action
items.example: It forms slacker, a person who avoids work.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 slacker，即「偷懒的人」。

items.meaning: forming a participle or a noun of action
items.example: It forms slackening as in a slackening pace.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 slackening，如 a slackening pace。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: It forms slackened, as in the rope slackened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 slackened，如 the rope slackened。

items.meaning: away from a state or an activity
items.example: Slacken off is the phrasal verb for easing effort.
items.exampleCN: slacken off 是表示「松懈、放缓」的短语动词。

items.example: Slacken belongs with loosen, widen and stiffen in one verb pattern.
items.exampleCN: slacken 与 loosen、widen、stiffen 同属一种动词构词模式。

items.example: Stiffen is the opposite action built with the same ending.
items.exampleCN: stiffen 是用同一词尾构成的相反动作。

definition_zh: 诽谤；诽谤罪；造谣中伤；口头诋毁
definition_en: a false spoken statement that damages a person reputation, and the act or crime of making such statements
core_image: 绊人的绳：一句悄悄话被抛出，绊倒别人的好名声
scene: 小镇上有人到处传闲话，把一位老实店主说成骗子。The shopkeeper sued the gossip for slander after losing most of his customers.
sceneCN: 这里 slander 是「诽谤、口头诋毁」（第 1 个义项：用不实之言损毁他人名誉）；句意：店主在失去大半顾客之后，以诽谤为由起诉那个搬弄是非的人。

pos.zh: 诽谤；诋毁；诽谤罪
诽谤；口头中伤

derivatives.zh: 动词 slander 加 -er 构成，指「诽谤者」
slander 加 -ous 构成，义为「诽谤性的」
slanderous 再加 -ness 构成的抽象名词，义为「诽谤性」
动词加 -ing 用作动名词，义为「诽谤行为」

senses.title: A false spoken statement that harms a reputation
senses.titleCN: 诽谤之言；损人名誉的谣言
senses.definition: a false statement spoken about someone that damages his good name
senses.definitionCN: 当众说出的不实之词，用来损害他人的名声
senses.example: The rumour spread in the market was pure slander.
senses.exampleCN: 在市场里传开的那条谣言纯属诽谤。
senses.why: The Old French esclandre first meant a public scandal, and slander keeps that picture of words spread among people.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 esclandre 原指公开的丑闻，slander 保留了「闲话在人群中传开」这一画面，所以它是当众说出的毁人名节之言。

senses.title: The act or crime of defaming someone orally
senses.definition: the act, or in law the wrong, of making such false spoken statements
senses.definitionCN: 做出这类虚假口头陈述的行为，在法律上也指一种侵权行为
senses.example: He was found guilty of slander for naming her as a thief.
senses.exampleCN: 他因指称她是小偷而被判犯有诽谤罪。
senses.why: Once a false statement damages a person, the law gives the act a name of its own, so the word also names the wrong committed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不实之言真的伤害了人，法律就要给这个行为一个名称，于是 slander 从「话」延伸到「构成过错的行为」本身。

senses.title: To speak untruthfully about someone
senses.definition: to say false things about a person in order to damage his reputation
senses.definitionCN: 说某人的不实之言，以毁坏其名誉
senses.example: A rival was trying to slander him in front of every supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 一个对手正试图在每个供应商面前造谣中伤他。
senses.why: The noun and the verb share one core image, so turning the statement into an action needs no new word.
senses.whyCN: 名词和动词共用同一个核心意象，把「那句话」变成「去说那句话」，不需要另造新词。

senses.title: A cause of public disgrace
senses.definition: a thing or act that brings shame on a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 给个人或群体带来耻辱的事物或行为
senses.example: In Victorian England, unpaid debts were a slander on the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 在维多利亚时代的英国，欠债不还被视为整个家族的耻辱。
senses.why: Because the older French word meant scandal, the English word kept a second thread in which slander is the disgrace itself rather than talk about it.
senses.whyCN: 因为更早的法语词本义是「丑闻」，英语保留了一条副线：slander 也可以直接指耻辱本身，而不只是关于耻辱的闲话。

senses.title: False talk contrasted with libel
senses.titleCN: 口头诽谤与书面诽谤之别
senses.definition: false defamatory statements made by speech, in contrast with libel in permanent form
senses.definitionCN: 以言语形式作出的诽谤性陈述，与以永久形式作出的书面诽谤相对
senses.example: Radio and television broadcasts were once treated as slander, not libel.
senses.exampleCN: 电台和电视的播出内容曾经被当作口头诽谤，而不是书面诽谤。
senses.why: Law keeps the spoken and the written branches apart, so slander is defined by the mouth, libel by the page.
senses.whyCN: 法律把「说」和「写」分开处理，所以 slander 以嘴来界定，libel 以纸面来界定。

senses.title: Damaging talk used in a loose, describing way
senses.titleCN: 诽谤性的；中伤的（口语用法）
senses.definition: used loosely of words or reports that attack someone unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 泛指不公平地攻击他人的言论或报道
senses.example: Nothing in that slander-filled column was ever proved in court.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇满是诋毁的专栏文章，没有任何一句在法庭上得到证实。
senses.why: Writers stretch the noun into a describing role, so it can label anything spoken that unfairly wounds a name.
senses.whyCN: 写作者把名词拉伸到描述的位置，于是它可以标注任何不公平地伤害名声的口头内容。

intro.en: Slander comes into English from Old French esclandre, a scandal or false report, which goes back to Latin scandalum, a cause of offence, and ultimately to Greek skandalon, a trap or stumbling block.
intro.cn: slander 来自古法语 esclandre（丑闻、不实传闻），源于拉丁语 scandalum（令人跌倒的绊脚石、丑事），再往前是希腊语 skandalon（陷阱、绊索）。

items.en: Skandalon names the trigger of a trap, the stick that makes an animal stumble.
items.cn: skandalon 指陷阱的绊线或机关，即让猎物绊倒的那根木条。

items.en: Scandalum keeps the image as a cause of stumbling or offence, a snare for the soul.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scandalum 保留这一意象，指使人跌倒或受到冒犯的诱因，即灵魂的绊脚石。

items.en: Esclandre means a public scandal or a damaging false report.
items.cn: 古法语 esclandre 意为公开的丑闻或损害性的不实传闻。

items.en: Sclaundre enters English meaning the scandal itself and the talk that spreads it.
items.cn: sclaundre 进入英语，既指丑闻本身，也指散播丑闻的闲话。

items.en: The -d- appears in the spelling, giving slander beside the older forms.
items.cn: 拼写中出现字母 d，形成 slander，与更早的拼写并存。

items.en: Law fixes the modern split: slander is spoken, libel is written or printed.
items.cn: 法律固定了现代分工：slander 是口头诽谤，libel 是书面或印刷诽谤。

note.en: Slander shares a history with scandal, and it stands beside its legal partner libel and the plainer words of false talk.
note.cn: slander 与 scandal 同出一源，并与法律上的对应词 libel 以及更普通的「造谣」类词相邻。

entries.definition: a shameful event that causes public outrage
entries.definitionCN: 引起公众愤怒的丑闻——与 slander 同出于拉丁语 scandalum

entries.definition: containing or spreading false damaging statements
entries.definitionCN: 诽谤性的；含毁谤内容的——slander 加形容词后缀构成

entries.definition: a person who says false things about others
entries.definitionCN: 诽谤者——slander 加 -er 指人

entries.definition: a person who lives on an island
entries.definitionCN: 岛民——只是拼写里含有 slander 这一串字母，词源不同

entries.definition: a false written statement that damages a reputation
entries.definitionCN: 书面诽谤；文书诽谤——以永久形式发布，与口头传达相对

entries.definition: the general legal term for harming a reputation, spoken or written
entries.definitionCN: 诽谤（总称）——涵盖口头与书面两种形式的上位词

entries.definition: a false and malicious statement intended to injure a reputation
entries.definitionCN: 污蔑；中伤——书面语色彩更浓，指蓄意毁人名节的假话

normalIntro.en: Slander travels the same road as scandal: a stumbling stone thrown into a good name.
normalIntro.cn: slander 与 scandal 走在同一条路上：一颗绊脚石被扔进别人的好名声里。

normal.en: Scandal and slander both come from scandalum, a stumbling block, and the first letters still look alike.
normal.cn: scandal 与 slander 都出自 scand- 这一串字母，两者开头相近，可以捆在一起记。

normal.en: Slander goes through the mouth, libel goes onto the page.
normal.cn: slander 从嘴里出来，libel 落到纸面上。

normal.en: Slander + er gives the person, slander + ous gives the adjective.
normal.cn: slander 加 -er 得到「人」，加 -ous 得到形容词。

normal.en: A slander is a false story told behind a back, while a defamation can be written as well.
normal.cn: 诽谤是背后说的假话，而 defamation 也可以是写下来的。

normal.en: Sue for slander is the phrase to keep when the talk has already cost money.
normal.cn: 闲话已经造成金钱损失时，记住短语 sue for slander。

abstract.en: See a whisper leaving one mouth and entering many ears, turning into a mud ball as it travels.
abstract.cn: 想象一句耳语从一张嘴里出来，钻进许多只耳朵，一路滚成泥球。

abstract.en: See a court clerk handing the same words a legal label, so that talk becomes a wrong that can be fined.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭书记员在那句话上贴上一张法律标签，于是闲话变成可以处罚的过错。

abstract.en: See the same whisperer leaning in to speak it again, turning the word back into an action.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个搬弄是非的人再次凑近低声说话，于是名词又变回了动作。

examples.en: The actress refused to answer the slanders printed in the tabloids.
examples.cn: 那位女演员拒绝对小报上印出的那些诽谤作出回应。

examples.en: He sued the paper for slander after it named him as a cheat.
examples.cn: 报纸指称他作弊后，他以诽谤为由起诉了这家报纸。

examples.en: Slandering a colleague to win a promotion is both unfair and dishonest.
examples.cn: 为了赢得升职而中伤同事，既不公平也不诚实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死烂的」——把一个人的名声说成「死烂的」，就是口头诽谤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esclandre（丑闻、不实传闻）← 拉丁语 scandalum「使人跌倒的绊脚石、丑事」← 希腊语 skandalon「陷阱、绊索」。英文拼写里的 d 一般认为来自借入英语后所受的拉丁语形式影响，具体形成过程有不同的解释。核心义由「绊倒」引申为「用言词绊倒别人的名声」。

sensesIntro.en: Slander begins as the damaging false statement itself, extends to the legal wrong of making it, turns into the act of speaking it, and keeps an older thread in which it means disgrace.
sensesIntro.cn: slander 先指那句损人名誉的假话，再指做出这种话的法律过错，然后变成说这句话的动作，并保留了更早的一条支线：耻辱本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stumbling block is thrown into a good name, and the name trips.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗绊脚石被扔进别人的好名声里，名声被绊倒。

branches.en: A false statement is the trap itself: a stumbling block aimed at somebody else good name.
branches.cn: 假话本身就是那个陷阱：一块瞄准别人好名声的绊脚石。

branches.en: Once the stumbling becomes visible damage, law turns the act into a compensable wrong.
branches.cn: 一旦绊倒变成可见的损害，法律就把行为变成可索偿的过错。

branches.en: The speaker becomes the thrower, so the noun turns back into an action.
branches.cn: 说话的人变成扔石头的人，名词于是又回到了动作。

branches.en: The older French sense of scandal survives as the disgrace itself, not only talk about it.
branches.cn: 法语旧有的「丑闻」义残留为耻辱本身，而不只是关于耻辱的闲话。

branches.en: The mouth against the page, and the looseness of everyday speech, both sit at the edge of the legal sense.
branches.cn: 口与纸的对照，以及日常用语的宽泛拉伸，都挂在这个法律义项的边上。

intro.en: Slander has no modern English prefix or suffix of its own; its meaning comes from the French and Latin word body, and the derivations slanderer, slanderous and slandering are built with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: slander 本身不含现代英语的前缀或后缀，意义来自法语与拉丁语的词干，而 slanderer、slanderous、slandering 都是用常见后缀构成的派生。

latinIntro.en: The Latin scandalum means a stumbling block, from Greek skandalon, a trap or snare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandalum 意为绊脚石，源于希腊语 skandalon（陷阱、绊索）。

items.meaningCN: 绊脚石；使人跌倒的诱因
items.example: Scandalum supplies the Latin source of slander.
items.exampleCN: scandalum 提供 slander 的拉丁来源。

items.example: Esclandre carries the sense into French.
items.exampleCN: esclandre 把这一含义带入法语。

items.meaning: a false spoken statement about a person
items.example: Slander names the damaging talk.
items.exampleCN: slander 指那番毁人名节的言论。

items.example: The suffix -er forms slanderer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 slanderer。

items.example: Slanderer is the agent noun.
items.exampleCN: slanderer 是施动者名词。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms slanderous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 slanderous。

items.example: Slanderous describes the content of the talk.
items.exampleCN: slanderous 描述那番话的内容。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms slandering.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 slandering。

items.example: Slandering names the action as a whole.
items.exampleCN: slandering 把动作整体名词化。

definition_zh: 用刀猛砍；砍痕；斜杠；大幅削减；斜劈般划开
definition_en: to cut with a swift sweeping stroke of a blade, and the long cut, the diagonal mark, or the sharp reduction that such a stroke leaves behind
core_image: 刀口斜斜一划，留下一道长长的裂口
scene: 新办公室预算超支，管理层不得不砍掉一半差旅费用。During the meeting the manager announced a huge slash in training budgets.
sceneCN: 这里 slash 是「大幅削减」（第 4 个义项：把数额猛地砍掉一大块）；句意：会上经理宣布把培训预算大幅砍掉。

pos.zh: 猛砍；大幅削减；用斜杠分隔
砍伤；砍痕；斜杠；削减；斜劈状开口

collocations.zh: 刀耕火种；大刀阔斧地削减

derivatives.zh: slash 加 -er 构成，指「挥砍的人」「片状砍刀」或「恐怖片」
slash 加 -ing 用作形容词，义为「猛烈的、大幅的」
back 与 slash 复合，义为「反斜杠」
名词性短语复合而成，义为「刀耕火种的」

senses.title: To cut with a swift sweeping stroke
senses.definition: to cut something with a fast sideways stroke of a blade rather than a straight chop
senses.definitionCN: 不是直直劈下，而是用刀刃斜着迅猛一划，把东西砍开
senses.example: One of the men slashed the horse harness with a knife.
senses.exampleCN: 其中一人用刀割断了马的挽具。
senses.why: The French verb means to break or dash, and English keeps the force of a violent blow delivered sideways, so the cut is long rather than deep.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词本义是「打碎、猛烈撞击」，英语保留了「侧向一击」的力度，所以切出来的口子长而斜，而不是深而直。

senses.title: A long cut or wound left by a blade
senses.definition: a long, narrow cut or wound made by a blade
senses.definitionCN: 刀刃留下的一道又长又窄的伤口或切口
senses.example: The slash on his arm took three stitches.
senses.exampleCN: 他手臂上那道划伤缝了三针。
senses.why: Every stroke of a blade leaves its trace, so the word names both the act and the shape that remains.
senses.whyCN: 刀划过的动作总会留下痕迹，于是这个词既指「划」，也指划完之后留在物体上的那道形状。

senses.title: The diagonal mark used between words
senses.definition: the mark / used to separate words, show alternatives, or write dates
senses.definitionCN: 用来分隔词语、标注「或」或书写日期的斜线符号 /
senses.example: Write his job as teacher or coach with a slash between the words.
senses.exampleCN: 用斜杠把教师或教练这两个词隔开，写他的职务。
senses.why: The printer pen stroke that makes the mark travels in the same leaning direction as a cut, so the symbol took the name of the cut.
senses.whyCN: 笔尖画出这个符号时走过的方向，正是一道斜切的轨迹，所以这个标记继承了「砍」这个名字。

senses.title: A drastic cut in money, prices or jobs
senses.definition: to reduce an amount or a cost by a large and sudden degree
senses.definitionCN: 把数额或成本猛地砍掉一大块
senses.example: The company slashed its marketing budget by half.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把营销预算砍掉了一半。
senses.why: A slash of the sword is quick and wide, so the verb borrows that sweep for any number that is to be cut down enormously in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 一刀下去又快又宽，动词就把这一式用在任何要一次性砍掉一大截的数字上，于是数字也被「砍」了。

senses.title: A gaping opening made as if cut apart
senses.titleCN: 豁口；开襟；被割裂的开口
senses.definition: a long opening in a garment, a tent, or a surface, designed or torn as a cut
senses.definitionCN: 衣物、帐篷或表面上被切开、设计成开口的长条形缝隙
senses.example: The dress had a high slash at one side to allow easy walking.
senses.exampleCN: 这条连衣裙一侧开着高高的开衩，方便走路。
senses.why: When a slash is made deliberately instead of by accident, the same word names the opening that the cut leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 当这一刀不是为了伤害而是刻意为之，同一个词就转而指切开后留下的那个开口。

senses.title: A slashing blow drawn through the air
senses.definition: the sweeping motion or blow of a blade or a whip through the air
senses.definitionCN: 刀刃或鞭子在空中划过后落下的一记横扫
senses.example: With one slash of his stick he knocked the ball across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他随手一挥棍子，就把球击过了球场。
senses.why: Besides naming the cut and the cut mark, the word can name the swinging blow itself before any contact is made.
senses.whyCN: 除了指切口与切痕，这个词还可以指刀刃尚未碰到任何东西时的那一记挥砍动作本身。

senses.title: Ranked side by side in marks
senses.titleCN: 并列；以斜杠并列为同等地位
senses.definition: recorded or listed with a slash, as on a hit list or a chart
senses.definitionCN: 用斜杠记录或列出，如名录或图表中的并列登记
senses.example: Each wrong submission was slashed off the chart overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 每一份错误提交都在夜里被从图表上划掉了。
senses.why: Once the mark is used for keeping records, the verb also means putting a slash against an item, which becomes a way of counting or cancelling it.
senses.whyCN: 斜杠一旦被用来做记录，动词也就指在某条目上划一道杠，于是划杠既成了计数，也成了划掉。

intro.en: Slash comes from Old French esclachier, to break or burst, which may go back to a Germanic source; the spelling settles as slash in English and spreads out into cut, mark, and cut-down senses.
intro.cn: slash 来自古法语 esclachier（打碎、迸裂），更早来源一般认为可追溯到日耳曼语，词根细节存在不同说法；英语拼写固定为 slash 之后，词义扩展到切口、符号与削减。

items.en: The reconstructed source is usually related to words for tearing or slashing, though the exact Germanic form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为其来源与表示「撕裂、猛劈」的日耳曼语词相关，但确切的日耳曼语形式来源不确定。

items.en: Esclachier means to break, burst, or shatter, often with a blow.
items.cn: esclachier 意为打碎、迸裂，常指一击造成的破裂。

items.en: Slashen and sclashen name cutting something with a sweeping strike.
items.cn: 中古英语形式 slashen、sclashen 指用横扫的一击切砍某物。

items.en: The noun appears, naming a cut or a wound left by a blade.
items.cn: 名词形式出现，指刀刃留下的切口或伤口。

items.en: The mark / takes the name, and the verb grows a figurative sense of cutting budgets and prices.
items.cn: 斜线符号取得了这个名字，动词也长出了「削减预算与价格」的比喻义。

note.en: Slash is a cutting word first; the diagonal mark and the budget cut both borrow their image from the blade stroke.
note.cn: slash 首先是「切」的词；斜线符号与预算削减都从这一刀里借取了意象。

entries.definition: a person or thing that slashes
entries.definitionCN: 挥砍者；片状砍刀——slash 加 -er 构成

entries.definition: having been cut with a sweeping stroke
entries.definitionCN: 被砍开的；被大幅削减的——slash 的过去式与过去分词

entries.definition: the mark typed as a reverse diagonal
entries.definitionCN: 反斜杠——由 back 与 slash 复合，方向与斜杠相反

entries.definition: to scatter liquid noisily
entries.definitionCN: 泼溅——只是比 slash 多了一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: to divide or wound with a sharp edge
entries.definitionCN: 切；割——范围最广的上位词，不强调斜与猛

entries.definition: a long deep cut in flesh
entries.definitionCN: 深长的伤口——比 slash 更强调切口深

entries.definition: to cut roughly with repeated heavy blows
entries.definitionCN: 乱砍；反复猛劈——强调多次重重地砍

normalIntro.en: Slash is a blade word that grew a symbol and a budget meaning; a few real word pairs keep all three connected.
normalIntro.cn: slash 是一个「刀」的词，后来又长出了符号义和预算义；记住几个真实词组就能把三层意思串起来。

normal.en: Slash and splash differ by one letter, but splash is about water and slash is about a blade.
normal.cn: slash 与 splash 只差一个字母，但 splash 是泼水，slash 是动刀。

normal.en: The past tense slashed appears in news reports of budgets and prices, not only of injuries.
normal.cn: 过去式 slashed 不只出现在伤害新闻里，也常出现在预算与价格的报道中。

normal.en: Backslash is a compound, so the mark / and the mark \ are mirrored twins.
normal.cn: backslash 是复合词，所以斜杠 / 与反斜杠 \ 是一对镜像的双生子。

normal.en: Slash and burn names a farming method, and the phrase was later borrowed for harsh cost cutting.
normal.cn: slash and burn 原指刀耕火种的耕作方式，后来被借来形容严厉的削减。

normal.en: In writing, a slash between two words means one or the other, as in coach or teacher.
normal.cn: 书写里两个词之间的斜杠表示「任一」，比如教练或教师，写作 coach 斜杠 teacher。

abstract.en: See a sabre swing across a canvas, leaving one long diagonal scar from corner to corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一把弯刀横扫过画布，从一角到另一角留下一道长长的斜疤。

abstract.en: See the same long scar lifted off the canvas and set down on a page as the mark /.
abstract.cn: 想象那道长疤从画布上被取下来，放到纸面上，就成了斜杠符号。

abstract.en: See a column of numbers about to be cut, and one stroke wipes off the top half of every figure.
abstract.cn: 想象一列待砍的数字，一刀下去就把每个数字的上半截抹掉，这就是「大幅削减」。

examples.en: The thief slashed the straps of her bag and ran off.
examples.cn: 小偷割断了她背包的带子后跑掉了。

examples.en: Two slashes of red paint crossed the white wall.
examples.cn: 白墙上划过两道鲜红的漆痕。

examples.en: In the report, the shipping time is written as two days followed by a slash and then three.
examples.cn: 报告里运输时间写作两天斜杠三天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死拉」——用力死拉一刀，斜着划开一道长口子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esclachier（打碎、迸裂）→ 中古英语 slashen / sclashen（用横扫一击切开）→ 英语 slash。更早来源一般认为与日耳曼语族表示「撕裂、猛劈」的词相关，但确切的词根形式来源不确定；与 slander 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Slash starts with the sweeping cut of a blade, then names the cut mark, the diagonal symbol, and finally the drastic reduction of money and prices that copies the same motion.
sensesIntro.cn: slash 从刀刃横扫而过的「砍」开始，接着指砍出的口子、斜线符号，最后指仿照同一动作的「大幅削减数额与价格」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade sweeps across and leaves one long diagonal wound.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃横扫而过，留下一道长斜的伤口。

branches.en: The stroke itself: one fast sideways blow, whether it lands or is still in the air.
branches.cn: 动作线：一记快速的侧向挥砍，无论是否已经落下。

branches.en: The trace left behind: a long wound in flesh, or a deliberate opening in cloth.
branches.cn: 痕迹线：落在皮肉上的长伤口，或刻意留出的衣料开衩。

branches.en: The route of the pen turns the cut into the mark /.
branches.cn: 笔尖走过的轨迹，把那一刀变成了斜杠符号。

branches.en: A quick wide stroke is borrowed for amounts cut off in one go.
branches.cn: 又快又宽的一刀被借来形容一次性砍掉的数额。

branches.en: Marking an item with a slash becomes counting or crossing it out.
branches.cn: 在某条目上划一道杠，就成了计数或划掉它。

intro.en: Slash is a free root with no productive prefix of its own; English builds slasher, slashing and the compound backslash around it.
intro.cn: slash 是没有常用前缀的自由词根，英语围绕它构成 slasher、slashing 以及复合词 backslash。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word comes through Old French and is usually traced to Germanic words for tearing.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，它经由古法语进入英语，一般认为可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「撕裂」的词。

items.example: Esclachier supplies the verb source.
items.exampleCN: esclachier 提供动词来源。

items.meaning: to cut with a sweeping stroke
items.example: Slash keeps the cutting force.
items.exampleCN: slash 保留了切割的力度。

items.example: The noun names the trace.
items.exampleCN: 名词形式指留下的痕迹。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms slasher.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 slasher。

items.meaning: a person or blade that slashes
items.example: Slasher is the agent noun.
items.exampleCN: slasher 是施动者名词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms slashing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 slashing。

items.example: Slashing describes a severe cut.
items.exampleCN: slashing 形容削减幅度猛烈。

items.example: The prefix back- makes backslash.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 back- 构成 backslash。

items.example: Backslash points the other way.
items.exampleCN: 反斜杠指向相反的方向。

definition_zh: 板条；条板；（以板条）猛打；条板制构件
definition_en: a long narrow flat piece of wood, metal or plastic, used in rows to make shutters, blinds, fences or furniture
core_image: 一排又长又薄的窄木条，像百叶窗那样并排钉在一起
scene: 夏日午后，百叶窗的板条歪了一根，阳光斜斜照进屋里。The old wooden slat of the blind had warped and would not close.
sceneCN: 这里 slat 是「板条」（第 1 个义项：长而窄的薄木条或薄金属条）；句意：百叶窗上那根旧板条已经翘曲变形，关不上了。

pos.zh: 板条；条板；（百叶、栅栏的）叶片
（用板条或扁物）猛打；猛拍

derivatives.zh: slat 双写 t 加 -ed 构成，义为「由板条制成的」
slat 加 -ing 构成，义为「板条材料；用板条装成的东西」
板岩；石板，与 slat 拼写相近，但一般认为不是同源派生

senses.title: A long narrow flat strip of wood
senses.definition: a thin flat strip of wood, used in rows as part of a larger structure
senses.definitionCN: 又长又薄又平的木条，成排拼在同一结构里使用
senses.example: He nailed the last slat to the fence before dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 他在天黑前把最后一块板条钉到了栅栏上。
senses.why: The word is a by-form of slate, the thin flat stone, and the thin flat shape is what carries over to the wooden strip.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 slate（薄石板）的一种变体，继承了「又薄又平」的形状，于是转指同样薄而平的木条。

senses.title: One leaf of a blind or shutter
senses.definition: one of the narrow boards that can be tilted to control light in a blind or shutter
senses.definitionCN: 百叶窗或遮板上可以翻转以调节光线的那一片窄板
senses.example: Dust had gathered on every slat of the window blind.
senses.exampleCN: 窗上百叶的每片叶片上都积了灰。
senses.why: Once strips are set side by side and made to move, each strip becomes the smallest unit of the whole, and this is the most common modern use.
senses.whyCN: 当一排薄条并排安装并且可以转动时，每一条都成了整体的最小单位，这也是今天最常见的用法。

senses.title: A strip of metal, plastic or fabric in the same shape
senses.definition: a strip of metal, plastic or fabric shaped like a wooden slat and used in the same way
senses.definitionCN: 形状像木条、用法相同的金属、塑料或织物窄条
senses.example: The car seats are cooled by flexible plastic slats under the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车座椅靠布面下的柔性塑料条来散热。
senses.why: The shape rather than the material defines the word, so replacing wood with metal or plastic does not change the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由形状而不是材料来界定，所以把木头换成金属或塑料，名称并不改变。

senses.title: A strip used as a seat or mattress support
senses.definition: one of the narrow strips forming the base of a bed or a chair seat
senses.definitionCN: 构成床架或椅面底部的那一根根窄条
senses.example: One of the bed slats had cracked under the heavy mattress.
senses.exampleCN: 沉重的床垫把床架上的一根板条压裂了。
senses.why: Furniture makers set the same strips under a bed or a seat, where each one takes the weight of a body.
senses.whyCN: 家具匠把同样的窄条铺在床或椅面下面，每一根各自承受一部分身体的重量。

senses.title: The structural pattern made by such strips
senses.definition: a surface or frame built from parallel slats, such as a slatted floor or a slatted door
senses.definitionCN: 由平行板条拼成的表面或框架，如条板地板或条板门
senses.example: The slats in the old door let the air move through the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 旧门上的一条条板条让空气穿过了谷仓。
senses.why: When the individual strips are viewed together, they name a way of building, which is why the adjective slatted describes whole floors and doors.
senses.whyCN: 把单根条子放在一起看，它们就成了一种建造方式，所以形容词 slatted 可以形容整块地板或门。

senses.title: To strike sharply with a flat object
senses.definition: to hit something hard with a flat strip or a wide flat object
senses.definitionCN: 用板条或扁宽的物件狠狠地打一下
senses.example: The farmer slatted the wet sack against the fence to empty it.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把湿麻袋在栅栏上猛拍，把里面的东西倒空。
senses.why: A strip is also a stick, so the noun turns into a verb that names hitting with something long, narrow and flat.
senses.whyCN: 板条本身也是根棍子，名词于是转为动词，指用又长又窄又扁的东西击打。

senses.title: A strip built into a vehicle body
senses.definition: a narrow shaped strip fixed to a vehicle or aircraft body to guide air or protect a surface
senses.definitionCN: 固定在车身或机体上，用来导流或护住表面的窄条构件
senses.example: The mechanic replaced the damaged slat on the car grille.
senses.exampleCN: 修车工换掉了汽车格栅上那根受损的导流条。
senses.why: Engineers take the same thin shaped strip and place it where the air flows, so the vehicle sense is the shape applied to a new job.
senses.whyCN: 工程师把同样的薄形条子放到气流经过的地方，所以交通工具中的义项只是把这一形状用到新工作上。

intro.en: Slat cannot be traced to Latin or Greek; it is generally thought to be a by-form of the English word slate, the thin flat stone, and the sense of a wooden strip is recorded from the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: slat 一般不能追溯到拉丁语或希腊语，一般认为它是英语本土词 slate（薄石板）的变体；从十七世纪开始，它被用来指木质的窄板条。

items.en: The word is related in form to slate, which names a flat thin stone used for roofing and writing.
items.cn: 这个词在形式上与 slate 相关，后者指用于盖顶和书写的薄而平的石头。

items.en: Sclat and sclate are recorded as names for the thin roofing stone in northern and western English.
items.cn: 中古英语中，sclat、sclate 等拼写在英格兰北部与西部指薄薄的屋顶石板。

items.en: Slat takes on a wooden sense, naming a thin narrow board used in fences and doors.
items.cn: slat 获得木质含义，指用于栅栏与门的薄窄木板。

items.en: The verb slat appears, meaning to hit with a strip or a wide flat object.
items.cn: 动词用法出现，意为用条状或扁宽之物击打。

items.en: Slats become standard in blinds, bed bases and vehicle bodies; the adjective slatted is formed.
items.cn: 板条成为百叶窗、床架与车身的标准构件，并构成形容词 slatted。

note.en: Slat is a thin flat strip word, often confused in shape with slate; the near-meaning group gathers the other strip and board words used for the same jobs.
note.cn: slat 是「薄而平的窄条」，在外形上常与 slate 混淆；近义组汇集的是做同样工作的其他「条」与「板」类词。

entries.definition: a thin flat stone used for roofing
entries.definitionCN: 板岩；石板——一般认为 slat 是它的变体，但今天指石而非木

entries.definition: more than one strip, or the third-person verb
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式的板条，也作动词第三人称单数——比 slat 多一个字母 s

entries.definition: made of or fitted with parallel slats
entries.definitionCN: 条板制成的——slat 双写 t 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: of a dull grey-blue shade like slate
entries.definitionCN: 石板灰的——由 slate 与颜色词复合，与 slat 只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a long thick piece of timber
entries.definitionCN: 木板；厚板——比 slat 更厚更宽，常用于地板与船身

entries.definition: a thin narrow strip of wood used as a base for plaster
entries.definitionCN: 板条；灰泥底条——建筑术语，专指抹灰时作底用的细木条

entries.definition: a long narrow strip of wood fixed across others to strengthen or hold them
entries.definitionCN: 压条；木条——横跨固定在其他木料上起加固作用

normalIntro.en: Slat is a shape word: thin, flat, narrow and long, and it is the shape that decides whether the strip is called wooden, plastic or metal.
normalIntro.cn: slat 是一个形状词：薄、平、窄、长，正是这个形状决定了它是木的、塑料的还是金属的。

normal.en: Slat and slate look almost the same, but slate is thin stone and a slat is a thin wooden strip.
normal.cn: slat 与 slate 长得几乎一样，但 slate 是薄石头，slat 是薄木条。

normal.en: The adjective slatted doubles the t, so it is spelled slatted, not slated.
normal.cn: 形容词 slatted 要双写字母 t，不能写成 slated。

normal.en: Slats are counted in strips: one slat of a blind, two slats of a bed base.
normal.cn: 板条按根计数：百叶窗的一片 slat，床架的几根 slats。

normal.en: In building English, slat is close to lath, the thin strip under plaster.
normal.cn: 建筑英语里，slat 与 lath（抹灰时用的细木条）意思相近。

normal.en: A wooden slat is flat and light; a plank is thick, and a beam is deep and heavy.
normal.cn: slat 薄而轻，plank 厚，beam 又深又重，三者按尺寸分层。

abstract.en: See a carpenter taking one long shaving from a board, straight and thin, and nailing that shaving into a fence.
abstract.cn: 想象木匠从一块木板上刨下一条又长又直的薄片，再把这条薄片钉进栅栏。

abstract.en: See a row of slats all tilting together, so that the light slides in between them instead of through them.
abstract.cn: 想象一排板条一起翻转，于是光线从条与条之间的缝隙滑进来，而不是穿过板条本身。

abstract.en: See the whole floor built of parallel strips, every gap the width of one finger.
abstract.cn: 想象整块地板都由平行的窄条拼成，每条缝隙都只有一根手指那么宽。

examples.en: Rain drummed on the wooden slats of the veranda roof.
examples.cn: 雨点敲在凉台屋顶的木条上。

examples.en: They replaced the broken slats of the shutters before the storm arrived.
examples.cn: 他们在暴风雨来临前换掉了百叶窗上断裂的板条。

examples.en: The garden bench had a slatted back and a polished seat.
examples.cn: 花园长椅有一个条板靠背和一张磨得发亮的椅面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撕啦」——撕啦一声削下一条薄木片，就是板条；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为 slat 是英语本土词 slate（薄石板）的变体，两者都来自表示「薄而平的片状石材」的日耳曼语词，更早的印欧语来源不确定。由「薄平片」转指「木质窄条」的用法见于十七世纪，核心义始终是「又薄又平的窄条」。它不是拉丁语借词。

sensesIntro.en: Slat stays on one shape throughout: first a thin wooden strip, then the single leaf of a blind, then strips in other materials and in furniture, then the pattern they make, and finally a verb that names striking with such a strip.
sensesIntro.cn: slat 始终围绕同一个形状：先是薄木条，再是百叶窗的单独一片，然后是其他材料与家具中的窄条，接着是由它们拼成的结构，最后引申为用扁条击打的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thin flat strip lies beside many of its twins, all nailed in a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条又薄又平的窄条与许多同伴并排，被钉成一整排。

branches.en: The single strip is the base sense, a thin flat piece of wood.
branches.cn: 单根窄条是基础义项，即薄木条。

branches.en: Set side by side in a frame and made to turn, each strip becomes one blind leaf.
branches.cn: 在框架里并排安装并可翻转时，每根窄条就成了百叶窗的一片叶片。

branches.en: Material changes do not matter: metal, plastic or a bed base still uses the same strip.
branches.cn: 材料替换不影响词义：金属、塑料或床架用的仍是同一种窄条。

branches.en: Viewed together, the strips become a way of building floors, doors and vehicle bodies.
branches.cn: 把窄条合起来看，它们就成了一种建造地板、门与车身的做法。

branches.en: Because a strip is also a stick, the noun turns into a verb of striking.
branches.cn: 因为窄条本身也是根棍子，名词就变成了表示击打的动词。

intro.en: Slat is a short native stem with no prefix or suffix of its own; English builds the past form slatted, the adjective slatted and the noun slatting around it.
intro.cn: slat 是简短的本土词干，本身不含前缀或后缀；英语围绕它构成过去式 slatted、形容词 slatted 与名词 slatting。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for slat; it is a native English word, generally taken as a by-form of slate.
latinIntro.cn: slat 没有拉丁语来源，它是英语本土词，一般认为与 slate 同形而异体。

items.example: Slat is the bare stem.
items.exampleCN: slat 是这个词干本身。

items.example: Slate is the oldest recorded relative.
items.exampleCN: slate 是有记录的最早亲缘词。

items.meaningCN: 过去式或过去分词结尾
items.example: The ending -ted after doubling gives slatted.
items.exampleCN: 双写后再加结尾构成 slatted。

items.example: Slatted builds on the past participle.
items.exampleCN: slatted 由过去分词转化而来。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms slatting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 slatting。

items.meaningCN: 板条材料；用板条装成的东西
items.example: Slatting names the material as a whole.
items.exampleCN: slatting 把材料作为整体来命名。

items.example: Slats keeps the countable plural.
items.exampleCN: slats 保留可数复数。

items.example: Lath is the builder cousin of slat.
items.exampleCN: lath 是 slat 在营造业的表亲。

items.example: Batten holds other strips in place.
items.exampleCN: batten 用来把其他条木固定住。

definition_zh: 板岩；石板；石板瓦；候选人名单；预定安排；严厉批评；提名
definition_en: a fine-grained grey rock that splits into thin flat sheets, used for roofs and floors, or to plan or criticize something in advance
core_image: 岩石被一凿劈成薄而平的一片片，像书页一样叠起来盖在屋顶上
scene: 老城街上的屋顶铺满灰蓝色的石板，雨水顺着层层叠瓦流下。Rain ran down the grey tiles of every roof on the old street. The piece then moves to the idiom wipe the slate clean, which means forgetting past wrongs and starting again.
sceneCN: 这里 slate 是「石板」（第 2 个义项：劈成薄片用于铺屋顶或擦写字的石板）；句意：雨水顺着老街上每片灰蓝色石板瓦流下。随后出现习语 wipe the slate clean，意思是抹去旧怨、重新开始，对应第 2 个义项里石板可擦写的意象。

pos.zh: 板岩；石板；石板瓦；候选人名单；预定安排
严厉批评；预定安排；提名

collocations.zh: 既往不咎；一切从头开始

derivatives.zh: slate 加 -ed 构成，指「铺了石板瓦的」，也指「被预定、被安排的」
slate 加 -er 构成，指铺石板瓦的工人
slate 改 y 尾构成，指「板岩般的；石板灰色的」

senses.title: Fine-grained rock that splits into flat sheets
senses.definition: a dark grey rock with very fine grains that can be split easily into thin flat sheets
senses.definitionCN: 一种深灰色、颗粒极细、容易劈成薄片的岩石
senses.example: The quarry produces slate that splits into sheets as thin as a finger.
senses.exampleCN: 这座采石场出产的板岩能劈得像手指一样薄。
senses.why: Old French esclat named a splinter, a piece broken off, and the rock took the name from the way it breaks into thin flat pieces.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 esclat 意为木片、碎片，这种岩石因为一劈就成薄片而得名，名字本身记录的就是它裂开的样子。

senses.title: A flat tile or board for writing on
senses.definition: a thin flat piece of slate used as a roof tile, a paving stone, or a small board for writing with chalk
senses.definitionCN: 薄而平的石板，用作屋顶瓦、铺石，或让孩子用粉笔写字的小板
senses.example: Each child in the class wrote the sum on a slate with chalk.
senses.exampleCN: 班上的每个孩子都用粉笔把算式写在石板上。
senses.why: The rock is cut into thin waterproof tiles for roofs and into small writing boards, so the material name became the name of the object.
senses.whyCN: 这种岩石被切成薄而防水的瓦铺屋顶，也被切成小书写板，于是材料名直接变成了物品名，可写可擦的画面正是 wipe the slate clean 的来源。

senses.title: A list of people put forward for office
senses.definition: a list of candidates or people chosen for a position or an event
senses.definitionCN: 为某个职位或活动选出的候选人名单
senses.example: The party announced a full slate of candidates for the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 该党公布了市议会的整份候选人名单。
senses.why: American politics wrote the names of a whole group on one flat board, and the written list took the name of the board it was chalked on.
senses.whyCN: 美国政治把一整组人的名字写在一块平板上，于是「写在板上的名单」沿用了板本身的名称，这就是名单义的来历。

senses.title: A plan or schedule fixed in advance
senses.definition: a plan or schedule that has been arranged for a future time
senses.definitionCN: 事先安排好的计划或日程
senses.example: The film is on the slate for release in early summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影预定在初夏上映。
senses.why: A slate was used as a board on which work and dates were written up, and even a writing surface for daily menus, so the word came to mean what is written down as arranged.
senses.whyCN: 石板曾用作写工作与日期的板子，英国人甚至把酒馆写在板上的当日菜单叫作 slate，于是这个词就表示被写下来的安排。

senses.title: To criticize very severely
senses.definition: to criticize someone or something very severely, especially in public
senses.definitionCN: 严厉地、公开地批评某人或某事
senses.example: Critics slated the new play for its empty dialogue and thin plot.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家严厉批评这部新剧对白空洞、情节单薄。
senses.why: The British verb slates, literally to throw stones or beat with a flat slab, gave the sense of attacking a work with hard flat blows of words.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语的动词本来有「扔石头、用平板拍打」的意思，把批评者想象成用一块块硬石板拍打作品，便有了「猛烈抨击」。

senses.title: To schedule for a future time
senses.definition: to plan or arrange an event for a particular future time, or to nominate someone for a position
senses.definitionCN: 把某事安排到将来某个时间，或提名某人担任某职
senses.example: The bridge is slated to open in October after long delays.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥在长期延误之后预定于十月通车。
senses.why: Keeping a written diary on a slate grew into recording planned dates, and being written on the slate of candidates came to mean being nominated.
senses.whyCN: 在石板上记日程的习惯发展成「把日期写进计划」，而名字被写进候选人名单就表示「被提名」。

intro.en: Slate comes from Old French esclat, a splinter or broken piece, itself probably from a Germanic word for splitting; the sense of a writing board, a list of candidates and a schedule all grew from the flat sheet of stone.
intro.cn: slate 来自古法语 esclat（碎片、裂片），一般认为再上溯到日耳曼语中表示「劈开」的词；书写板、候选人名单与日程等义都由那块平整的石板长出来。

items.en: The base is usually reconstructed from a Germanic verb meaning to split or burst, though the exact form is a reconstruction and not attested.
items.cn: 一般认为其词基是日耳曼语中表示劈开、爆裂的动词，但确切形式属重构，没有文献佐证。

items.en: Old French esclat meant a splinter or a piece broken off, and similar forms are used for shards and chips.
items.cn: 古法语 esclat 意为碎片、裂下的薄片，同类词形也用来指陶片与木屑。

items.en: English takes sclate and slate for the rock and for a thin flat roofing tile, because the stone breaks naturally into flat sheets.
items.cn: 中古英语以 sclate、slate 指这种岩石与薄平的屋顶瓦，因为这种石头天然裂成薄片。

items.en: A small slate board served for writing with chalk, and the word is recorded for a list of names and for a written record of accounts.
items.cn: 小块石板被用来以粉笔写字，这个词也开始指名册与账目记录。

items.en: American politics named the whole list of candidates on a ballot a slate, and papers added the verb slate for nominating or scheduling.
items.cn: 美国政治把选票上的整份候选人名单叫作 slate，报刊又用动词 slate 表示提名或排定时间。

items.en: British usage develops a verb slate meaning to criticize severely, probably from the idea of striking or stoning, and keeps a clean slate for a fresh start.
items.cn: 二十世纪的英式英语发展出动词 slate，表示严厉批评，一般认为源于「打击、扔石头」，并沿用 a clean slate 表示重新开始。

note.en: Slate is compared with thin flat materials of the same look, and with words for rock, for a list of names, and for harsh criticism.
note.cn: 把 slate 与形近的薄平材料、表示岩石的词、表示名单的词以及表示严厉批评的词作比较。

entries.definition: a thin narrow strip of wood, metal or plastic fixed in a row
entries.definitionCN: 细长的木条、金属条或塑料条，成排固定；与 slate 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a thick flat piece of stone, concrete or similar hard material
entries.definitionCN: 石板块、混凝土板等厚平板；与 slate 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: rain and snow falling together, or ice pellets
entries.definitionCN: 雨雪交加或冰粒；与 slate 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a fine-grained rock that splits into thin layers, often containing clay
entries.definitionCN: 一种能裂成薄层的细粒岩石，多为泥质

entries.definition: a list of names showing who is on duty or available
entries.definitionCN: 名单；值班表

entries.definition: to say what is wrong with something
entries.definitionCN: 批评；指责

normalIntro.en: Slate is a flat grey stone that splits into sheets and, because it was once a board for writing, it also means a list and a schedule.
normalIntro.cn: slate 是一种能劈成薄片的扁平灰石；因为它曾是写字的板子，也引申出名单与日程。

normal.en: Old French esclat meant a splinter, and a slate breaks into flat splinters.
normal.cn: 古法语 esclat 意为碎片，而 slate 正是裂成一片片薄片的石头。

normal.en: A clean slate starts a new chapter, and wipe the slate clean forgives the past.
normal.cn: a clean slate 表示翻开新的一页，wipe the slate clean 表示既往不咎。

normal.en: A slate of candidates is a whole list chosen together.
normal.cn: a slate of candidates 就是一起选出的整份候选人名单。

normal.en: The verb slate means to criticize severely or to schedule.
normal.cn: 动词 slate 表示严厉批评或预定安排。

normal.en: Compare slab and slat: a slab is thick stone, a slat is a thin strip, and slate names both the stone and the writing board.
normal.cn: 对比 slab 与 slat：slab 是厚石板，slat 是细长条，而 slate 兼指岩石与书写板。

abstract.en: Picture a roof covered with grey sheets that look like fish scales.
abstract.cn: 想象一片屋顶铺满灰石板，层层叠叠像鱼鳞。

abstract.en: The past is chalk marks on a board; a wet cloth makes it slate again.
abstract.cn: 过去是一块黑板上的粉笔字，湿布一抹，一切又回到干净的板面。

abstract.en: Imagine a page where the whole list of names is already written.
abstract.cn: 想象一页已经写好整组名字的名单。

examples.en: The old farmhouse has a heavy slate roof that has lasted a century.
examples.cn: 那座老农舍的石板屋顶厚重结实，已经用了一个世纪。

examples.en: The two teams agreed to wipe the slate clean and start the negotiations again.
examples.cn: 两队同意抛开旧怨，重新开始谈判。

examples.en: Papers slated the politician for breaking his promise.
examples.cn: 报纸严厉批评那位政治家违背承诺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「slate」读来像「死累特」，可以联想工人扛着又重又平的石板累得不行；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esclat（碎片、裂片）← 一般认为日耳曼语中表示「劈开」的动词；核心义「一劈就裂成薄片的平整石料」，再由写字板引申出名单与日程。

sensesIntro.en: Slate begins with the flat grey rock itself, moves to the thin sheets cut from it for roofs and writing, and travels through three written uses: a list of candidates, a fixed schedule, and the two verbs for scheduling or criticizing.
sensesIntro.cn: slate 从扁平的灰石本身开始，转到用它切成的薄瓦与书写板，再沿「写在板上的东西」延伸到候选人名单与日程，最后是两个动词：安排与严厉批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat grey stone that splits into thin sheets, like the pages of a book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块能劈成薄片的灰色平石，像一叠书页。

branches.en: The rock itself is the oldest sense, named for the way it splits.
branches.cn: 岩石本身是最早的义项，名字记录的是它裂开的样子。

branches.en: Cut into thin sheets, the stone becomes roof tiles and chalk boards.
branches.cn: 切成薄片后，这种石头成为屋顶瓦与粉笔板。

branches.en: A list chalked on the board inherits the name of the board.
branches.cn: 写在板上的名单沿用了板本身的名称。

branches.en: What is written down as arranged becomes a schedule, and the verb records that plan.
branches.cn: 把安排写在板上就成了日程，动词则记录这一计划动作。

branches.en: The British verb adds two directions: striking with hard flat words, and writing a date on the slate.
branches.cn: 英式动词添上两个方向：用硬而平的话语打击，以及在石板上写下日期。

intro.en: Slate came from a French splinter word, borrowed whole into English; the family is built with -ed, -er and -y rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: slate 来自法语中表示「碎片」的词，整体借入英语；同族词主要靠 -ed、-er、-y 构成，而不是拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: Slate has no Latin ancestry; the French source comes from a Germanic splitting word, so the Latin entries are left empty. The linked material word schist comes from Greek, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: slate 没有拉丁语来源，法语中介词来自日耳曼语中表示「劈开」的词，因此拉丁同源词留空；与之相关的岩石词 schist 来自希腊语，也不是拉丁语。

items.example: Esclat names a piece broken off from a hard material.
items.exampleCN: esclat 指从硬物上裂下来的一片。

items.example: Slate names the rock before it names anything else.
items.exampleCN: slate 最先指的就是这种岩石。

items.example: The suffix forms slates for many tiles.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 slates，表示多块石板。

items.meaningCN: 表示被动或过去时的词尾
items.example: The suffix forms slated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 slated。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix forms slating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 slating。

items.example: The suffix forms slater for a roofer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 slater，指铺石板瓦的工人。

items.example: The suffix forms slaty for a stone colour.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 slaty，表示石板色。

items.meaning: a roof covered with flat stone tiles
items.example: The farmhouse kept its slate roof after the repairs.
items.exampleCN: 农舍修葺之后仍保留着石板屋顶。

items.example: The new manager began with a clean slate.
items.exampleCN: 新经理一开始就展现出一张白纸的形象。

definition_zh: 屠宰；屠杀；宰杀；惨败；彻底击败
definition_en: to kill animals for food, or to kill human beings in large numbers and cruelly; as a noun, the act of such killing or a heavy defeat
core_image: 屠宰场里牲畜被成排放倒，血流成片
scene: 清晨的屠宰场里，工人按顺序把牲畜宰杀，再把肉挂上铁钩。At dawn the workers slaughtered the animals in the order written on the chalk board. The word then jumps to a match in which one side is beaten without mercy.
sceneCN: 这里 slaughter 是「屠宰」（第 1 个义项：为食用而宰杀牲畜）；句意：天刚亮，工人们按黑板上写好的顺序宰杀牲畜。后半句把画面转到一场比赛里，一方被毫不留情地击败，对应第 3 个义项。

pos.zh: 屠宰；屠杀；宰杀；惨败
屠宰；屠杀；彻底击败

derivatives.zh: slaughter 与 house 复合构成，义为「屠宰场」
slaughter 加 -er 构成，义为「屠宰者；行凶屠杀者」
slaughter 与 man 复合构成，义为「屠宰工」，英式用法
过去分词作形容词，义为「被宰杀、被屠杀的」

senses.title: To kill animals for food
senses.definition: to kill an animal, especially for its meat
senses.definitionCN: 宰杀动物，尤指为取肉而宰杀
senses.example: Farmers slaughter pigs in the cooler months of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在较冷的月份宰猪。
senses.why: The Old Norse verb slatra meant to butcher, and the word began in the world of food rather than warfare.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语动词 slatra 意为屠宰，这个词从一开始就属于食物处理的场景，而不是战场的场景。

senses.title: To kill people in cold blood
senses.definition: to kill a large number of people cruelly and without mercy
senses.definitionCN: 残忍无情地杀害大批人
