senses.example: The invaders slaughtered whole families in a single night.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵者一夜之间屠杀了整户整户的家庭。
senses.why: The butchery of animals became a picture of human killing, because the word already carried the image of a helpless mass being cut down.
senses.whyCN: 宰杀牲畜的画面被搬到杀人上，因为这个词本来就带着「一群无力反抗者被成批放倒」的意象。

senses.title: A very easy win over a rival
senses.definition: a defeat that is so heavy that the losing side has no chance at all
senses.definitionCN: 悬殊到失败一方毫无机会的惨败
senses.example: The final ended in a six nil slaughter for the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛以客队零比六惨败收场。
senses.why: The killing sense supplies the image of an opponent wiped out, and sport uses the word lightly for a one-sided game.
senses.whyCN: 屠杀义提供了「一方被全部扫掉」的画面，体育报道便借来轻描淡写地形容一边倒的比赛。

senses.title: The act of killing, as a noun
senses.definition: the killing of animals for food or the brutal killing of people, viewed as an act or an event
senses.definitionCN: 为食用而宰杀牲畜，或残忍杀害人群，作为行为或事件本身
senses.example: The report counted the slaughter of more than a thousand cattle.
senses.exampleCN: 报告统计了上千头牛的宰杀数量。
senses.why: English uses the same form for the act and its name, so the noun stands for the whole butchery as one thing observed.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式把整个宰杀或屠杀当作一件可观察的事来命名，因此同一个词形既是动作也是那件事本身。

senses.title: To beat an opponent heavily
senses.definition: to defeat an opponent by a very large margin in a game or contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或较量中以极大差距击败对手
senses.example: The champions slaughtered their rivals in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军球队在下半场彻底击败了对手。
senses.why: Once the noun named a one-sided result, the verb simply described beating the other side in that same deadening way.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词已指悬殊的结果，动词自然就用来描述以同样的狠劲把对手打倒。

senses.title: To criticize without mercy
senses.titleCN: 猛烈抨击；不加保留地批评
senses.definition: to criticize someone or something very harshly, as if cutting them down
senses.definitionCN: 极为严厉地批评某人或某事，语气如同把人砍倒
senses.example: The reviewers slaughtered the film for its empty story.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人因故事空洞把这部电影批得体无完肤。
senses.why: From the same image of a victim cut down, talk describes a piece of writing or a film as slaughtered by criticism.
senses.whyCN: 延续「被砍倒的受害者」这一画面，人们便把一篇作品被批评批得体无完肤也说成被 slaughter。

intro.en: Slaughter comes from Old Norse slatra, to butcher; English borrowed it from the Danes and passed it through French slaughter and the modern spelling, keeping the butchery image for both animals and people.
intro.cn: slaughter 来自古诺斯语 slatra（屠宰），英语从北欧移民那里借入，再经法语形式的传递形成今天的拼写，屠宰的画面一直被用来指牲畜，也用来指人。

items.en: The Old Norse verb sla means to strike or to smash, and forms of it appear in English as slay and in the name of the hammer Mjolnir.
items.cn: 古诺斯语动词 sla 意为击打、砸碎，它的词形以 sley 一类的方式出现在英语中，也是锤子名字的构成成分。

items.en: Slatra means to butcher an animal for meat, and it is the direct source of the English word; the Norse form was recorded in Iceland from the eleventh century.
items.cn: slatra 意为把牲畜宰杀取肉，是英语这个词的直接来源；北欧的这个词形在冰岛文献中从十一世纪起有记录。

items.en: English first writes the word as slathtre for the killing of animals, and the form soon spreads to human killing as well.
items.cn: 中古英语最先把它写作 slathtre，指宰杀动物，随后这一形式很快就延伸到指杀人。

items.en: French influence from words such as esclandre reshapes the spelling into slaughtre, and the written form settles toward the modern one.
items.cn: 受法语词形（如 esclandre）的影响，拼写被改造成 slaughtre，书写形式逐渐稳定到现代的样子。

items.en: The spelling slaughter becomes fixed in printing, and slaughterhouse appears for a building where animals are killed.
items.cn: printing 中的拼写固定为 slaughter，同时出现 slaughterhouse 一词，指宰杀牲畜的场所。

items.en: Sport reporting gives the word an easy win sense, and criticism gives it a sense of severely attacking a work.
items.cn: 二十世纪，体育报道赋予它「大胜」义，批评语境则让它表示把一部作品批得很惨。

note.en: Slaughter is compared with look-alike words that begin the same way, and with words for killing, for a market where meat is cut, and for naming the place.
note.cn: 把 slaughter 与开头相同的形近词、表示杀人的词、表示切肉市场的词以及表示屠宰场所的词作比较。

entries.definition: the act or sound of laughing
entries.definitionCN: 笑；笑声；与 slaughter 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person who roofs buildings with stone tiles
entries.definitionCN: 铺石板瓦的工人；与 slaughter 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to kill, especially in a literary or dramatic way
entries.definitionCN: 杀死；杀戮；偏书面或戏剧色彩

entries.definition: to kill animals for meat, or to kill people brutally
entries.definitionCN: 宰杀牲畜；残杀

entries.definition: the cruel killing of many helpless people
entries.definitionCN: 屠杀；强调受害者是无力自保的群体

entries.definition: a place where animals were once cut up for selling meat
entries.definitionCN: 旧时的屠宰场；也引申为混乱场面

normalIntro.en: Slaughter begins as a butcher word borrowed from Old Norse and grows into a word for mass killing, for a heavy defeat, and for merciless criticism.
normalIntro.cn: slaughter 最初是从古诺斯语借来的屠宰用语，后来长成表示大批杀戮、惨败和无情批评的词。

normal.en: Old Norse slatra means to butcher, and the verb began in the kitchen rather than the battlefield.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 slatra 意为屠宰，这个动词出身于厨房而非战场。

normal.en: Slaughterhouse joins slaughter and house for the building where animals are killed.
normal.cn: slaughterhouse 由 slaughter 与 house 组合，指宰杀牲畜的场所。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one form, as in a slaughter of cattle and to slaughter cattle.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，如 a slaughter of cattle 与 to slaughter cattle。

normal.en: Sport reports say the team slaughtered the opposition when the score is one-sided.
normal.cn: 比分悬殊时，体育报道说这支球队把对手彻底击败。

normal.en: Compare butcher: butcher works mostly in the meat trade, while slaughter reaches into killing people and into sport.
normal.cn: 对比 butcher：butcher 多用于肉类行业，slaughter 则扩展到杀害人和体育语境。

abstract.en: Picture a row of cattle waiting in a line no one can step out of.
abstract.cn: 想象一排牲畜站在无法离队的队列里。

abstract.en: Hear the two words slaughter and laughter, and see how one dead silence follows the other.
abstract.cn: 把 slaughter 与 laughter 放在一起听，一个之后是一片死寂。

abstract.en: Think of a scoreboard showing six goals against none, and call that night a slaughter.
abstract.cn: 想象比分牌上六比零，把那一夜称为一场惨败。

examples.en: The new rules require animals to be stunned before they are slaughtered.
examples.cn: 新规定要求牲畜在被宰杀前先使其昏迷。

examples.en: Villagers still remember the slaughter of that autumn and hold a service every year.
examples.cn: 村民仍记得那年秋天的那场屠杀，并每年举行追思仪式。

examples.en: The home team was slaughtered in front of a full stadium.
examples.cn: 主队在满场观众面前被彻底击败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「slaughter」读来像「死喽特」，可以联想屠宰场里牲畜倒下的样子；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺斯语 slatra（屠宰）← 同族动词 sla（击打、砸碎），与 slay 同源；核心义「成批地砍倒宰杀」，再由牲畜转到人、到比赛与批评。

sensesIntro.en: Slaughter starts with butchering animals, widens to the killing of people, becomes a noun for such an act, and then weakens into a heavy defeat and a harsh criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: slaughter 从宰杀牲畜开始，扩展到杀害人群，又作名词指这种行为本身，最后在体育与批评语境里弱化成「惨败」与「猛烈抨击」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a helpless group cut down in a row, without a chance to escape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群无力反抗者被成排砍倒，没有逃走的机会。

branches.en: Butchering animals for food is the oldest sense, and the noun names the same act.
branches.cn: 为食用宰杀牲畜是最早的义项，名词则给同一行为命名。

branches.en: The killing of people keeps the same form and the same noun.
branches.cn: 杀人沿用同一词形与同一名词形式。

branches.en: A one-sided match borrows the image of a side being wiped out, as noun and as verb.
branches.cn: 一边倒的比赛借用了「一方被扫掉」的画面，名词与动词都是如此。

branches.en: Both senses share the picture of many lives ended without resistance.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「许多生命毫无反抗地被终结」的画面。

branches.en: Being cut down passes from war to sport and to a work being torn apart by critics.
branches.cn: 「被砍倒」从战场传到球场，再传到被批评拆解得粉碎的作品。

intro.en: Slaughter was borrowed whole from Old Norse and builds its family with compounds such as slaughterhouse and man, and with the ordinary English endings -ed, -er and -ing.
intro.cn: slaughter 整体借自古诺斯语，它的同族词靠 slaughterhouse、slaughterman 这类复合与 -ed、-er、-ing 这类英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Slaughter has no Latin ancestry; its Old Norse root is Germanic, so the Latin entries are left empty and only its English family is listed above.
latinIntro.cn: slaughter 没有拉丁语来源，其古诺斯语词根属日耳曼语，因此拉丁同源词留空，上文只列出英语的同族词。

items.example: Slatra is the Norse verb behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: slatra 是英语这个词背后的诺斯语动词。

items.example: Slay shares the Norse striking root.
items.exampleCN: slay 共享诺斯语「击打」的词根。

items.meaning: the killing of animals or people
items.example: Slaughter names the act and the event.
items.exampleCN: slaughter 既指行为也指事件。

items.meaningCN: 动词第三人称单数词尾
items.example: The suffix forms slaughters.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 slaughters。

items.example: The suffix forms slaughtered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 slaughtered。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix forms slaughtering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 slaughtering。

items.example: The suffix forms slaughterer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 slaughterer。

items.meaning: a building where animals are killed
items.example: The cattle were driven to the slaughterhouse by noon.
items.exampleCN: 中午前牛群被赶到了屠宰场。

items.meaning: a person whose job is to kill animals
items.example: A slaughterman must follow strict hygiene rules.
items.exampleCN: 屠宰工必须遵守严格的卫生规定。

definition_zh: 雪橇；用雪橇运送；大锤；重击；猛烈抨击
definition_en: a vehicle with runners for travelling over snow, or to carry something on such a vehicle; also a heavy hammer
core_image: 两条铁滑刃在雪面上飞速滑行，后面的货或人跟着飞驰
scene: 雪后的山路上，一辆木制雪橇载着木柴顺着坡道滑下去，留下两道长长的滑痕。Two dogs pulled the loaded sledge up the frozen path. The word in the idiom sledgehammer then turns to the world of hammers and blows.
sceneCN: 这里 sledge 是「雪橇」（第 1 个义项：装滑刃、用来在雪地上运送东西的器具）；句意：两条狗拉着装满东西的雪橇沿结冰的小路上坡。后半句的 sledgehammer 把画面转向锤子与重击，对应第 4 个义项。

pos.zh: 雪橇；大锤
用雪橇运送；用大锤敲击；猛烈抨击
乘雪橇滑行

derivatives.zh: sledge 与大锤旧词 hammer 复合构成，义为「大锤」，也指「沉重的打击」
sledge 加 -ing 构成，义为「乘雪橇滑行」，在板球中指「场上嘲讽对方」
sledge 加 -er 构成，义为「乘雪橇的人」

senses.title: A vehicle with runners for snow
senses.definition: a low vehicle with two long runners that slides over snow and ice, used to carry people or goods
senses.definitionCN: 装有两条长滑刃、可在冰雪上滑行、用来运送人或货物的低矮载具
senses.example: They loaded the sledge with firewood and pulled it through the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把木柴装上雪橇，把它拖过雪地。
senses.why: The word comes from a Germanic family of sliding sledges, and the plain name for the runner vehicle is the oldest and most central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自日耳曼语中一族的滑行器具名称，指装滑刃的载具，这是最早也最核心的义项。

senses.title: To travel or carry by sledge
senses.titleCN: 乘雪橇滑行；用雪橇运送
senses.definition: to ride on a sledge, or to move goods by sledge over snow and ice
senses.definitionCN: 乘坐雪橇滑行，或用雪橇把货物运过冰雪
senses.example: Supplies were sledged across the frozen lake to the research station.
senses.exampleCN: 补给被用雪橇运过冰湖送到研究站。
senses.why: The noun was turned into a verb so that the journey of the vehicle could be described as an action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词后，这件器具的行程就可以用一个动作来描述。

senses.title: The British verb for taunting rivals
senses.definition: in British cricket, to make rude remarks to an opposing player in order to upset them
senses.definitionCN: 英国板球中指用难听的话讥讽对方球员，好让对方乱了阵脚
senses.example: The captain warned his team against sledging the young batsman.
senses.exampleCN: 队长告诫队员不要讥讽那位年轻击球手。
senses.why: Australian cricket slang borrowed the sledge as a heavy hammer: a taunt is used as a blunt blow against the other player.
senses.whyCN: 澳大利亚板球俚语借用「大锤」这一形象：讥讽就像笨重的一锤，砸在对方球员身上。

senses.title: A heavy hammer
senses.definition: a large heavy hammer with a long handle, used with both hands for striking hard
senses.definitionCN: 带长柄、需双手挥动的大锤，用于重击
senses.example: He lifted the sledge and broke the old wall with two blows.
senses.exampleCN: 他举起大锤，两下就把旧墙砸开了。
senses.why: The word sledge is a shortened form of sledgehammer, an old name for the heavy hammer, and it survives as a bare noun in tools and smithing.
senses.whyCN: sledge 是 sledgehammer 的缩略形式，本来就是这种重锤的旧名，在工具与铁匠用语中保留下来，成为独立的名词义。

senses.title: To strike with a sledgehammer
senses.definition: to hit something hard with a sledgehammer or to deliver a heavy blow
senses.definitionCN: 用大锤用力敲击，或给予沉重的一击
senses.example: The workers sledged the concrete blocks until they split.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们用大锤猛砸混凝土块，直到它们裂开。
senses.why: The heavy hammer was used as a verb, and the verb keeps the feeling of a big flat blunt blow.
senses.whyCN: 这种重锤被用作动词，保留了笨重、沉闷的一记重击的感觉。

senses.title: To attack a plan or idea harshly
senses.definition: to criticize or attack something severely, as though breaking it apart with a heavy hammer
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈批评或攻击某事，仿佛用重锤把它砸碎
senses.example: The editor sledged the proposal in a long front-page article.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在头版长文中猛烈抨击了那份提案。
senses.why: The picture of a heavy hammer falling on a flat surface easily shifts from wood and stone to an argument that is pounded flat.
senses.whyCN: 重锤落在平整表面上的画面很容易从木头、石头转到被砸得扁平的论点，于是有了「痛批」。

intro.en: Sledge is a shortened form of sledgehammer, a word borrowed from Middle Dutch slegge, the sliding vehicle and the heavy hammer sharing the same source; the snow sense and the hammer sense have grown apart even though they share one origin.
intro.cn: sledge 是 sledgehammer 的缩略形式，借自中古荷兰语 slegge；滑行的载具与重锤出于同一来源，尽管雪橇义与锤子义在今天已经相去很远。

items.en: The family goes back to a Germanic base for a hammer or an implement used for striking and driving, reconstructed and not directly attested.
items.cn: 这一族词可上溯到日耳曼语中表示锤子或用来击打的工具的词基，属重构形式，没有直接文献。

items.en: The Old English verb slean means to strike, and the verb slay comes from the same striking root.
items.cn: 古英语动词 slean 意为击打，动词 slay 就出自同一个表示击打的词根。

items.en: Slegge names a sledgehammer, and this Dutch word supplies sledgehammer to English in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: slegge 是大锤的名称，这个荷兰语词在十三、十四世纪把 sledgehammer 给了英语。

items.en: English sledgehammer is a compound of sledge and hammer, and the short form sledge also names the hammer on its own.
items.cn: 英语 sledgehammer 由 sledge 与 hammer 复合而成，单用短形式 sledge 也指大锤。

items.en: In Britain the sliding runner vehicle for snow is called a sledge, while American usage prefers sled.
items.cn: 十九世纪的英国把在雪上滑行的载具称为 sledge，美式用法则多用 sled。

items.en: Australian cricket slang gives sledge the sense of taunting an opponent, and British journalism adds a verb for harsh criticism.
items.cn: 二十世纪的澳大利亚板球俚语让 sledge 有讥讽对手之义，英国新闻用语又添上「猛烈抨击」的动词义。

note.en: Sledge is compared with words that begin the same way, and with other winter vehicles and with words for hammering and harsh criticism.
note.cn: 把 sledge 与开头相同的词、其他冬季载具、表示锤击的词以及表示猛烈批评的词作比较。

entries.definition: a narrow flat shelf of rock or a surface sticking out of a wall
entries.definitionCN: 突出的岩架、窗台；与 sledge 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a serious promise, or to promise formally
entries.definitionCN: 承诺；保证；与 sledge 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a piece of wood or metal with a narrow edge used to split or hold
entries.definitionCN: 楔子；三角木；与 sledge 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a small vehicle with runners for snow, the usual American word
entries.definitionCN: 雪橇；美式常用词

entries.definition: a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer, often for passengers
entries.definitionCN: 马拉或驯鹿拉的载人雪橇

entries.definition: a heavy hammer used for breaking stone and driving posts
entries.definitionCN: 大锤；用于砸石与打桩的重锤

normalIntro.en: Sledge has two lives: the runner vehicle borrowed from Dutch and the heavy hammer that shortened into the bare word, with later slang for taunting and criticizing.
normalIntro.cn: sledge 有两条命：一条是从荷兰语借来的滑行载具，一条是缩略成独立词形的重锤，后来又有讥讽与抨击的俚语义。

normal.en: Sledgehammer joins sledge and hammer, and the short form sledge keeps the hammer meaning alone.
normal.cn: sledgehammer 由 sledge 与 hammer 组合，短形式 sledge 也单指大锤。

normal.en: Old English slean means to strike, and the striking root ties the sledge family to blows.
normal.cn: 古英语 slean 意为击打，这个击打的词根把 sledge 一族与「敲打」连在一起。

normal.en: In Britain the snow vehicle is a sledge, in America it is a sled.
normal.cn: 雪上载具在英式英语里是 sledge，在美式英语里是 sled。

normal.en: A sledgehammer blow can break a wall or sink a proposal at a meeting.
normal.cn: 一记重锤既能砸开一堵墙，也能在会议上砸掉一份提案。

normal.en: Compare sleigh: a sleigh is drawn by horses or reindeer for passengers, while a sledge also hauls loads.
normal.cn: 对比 sleigh：sleigh 多为马拉、载人，而 sledge 也用来运货。

abstract.en: Picture two steel runners cutting a straight line across fresh snow.
abstract.cn: 想象两条铁滑刃在新雪上划出一条笔直的线。

abstract.en: Feel a heavy hammer swing up and come down flat on a stone block.
abstract.cn: 感受一把重锤抡起后平直地砸在石块上。

abstract.en: Hear a rough remark across the cricket pitch, a blow made of words.
abstract.cn: 想象板球场上传来一句讥讽的话，那是用语言打出的一锤。

examples.en: The children took turns sliding down the hill on a wooden sledge.
examples.cn: 孩子们轮流坐上木雪橇从山坡滑下去。

examples.en: He sledged the old paving stones into pieces in under an hour.
examples.cn: 不到一小时，他就用大锤把旧石板砸成了碎块。

examples.en: The plan was sledged by every newspaper in the country.
examples.cn: 这份计划遭到全国每一家报纸的猛烈抨击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sledge」读来像「死来夹」，可以联想雪橇两侧的滑刃把路面死死夹住向下冲；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古荷兰语 slegge（大锤）→ 英语 sledgehammer，缩略为 sledge；与古英语 slean（击打）同属日耳曼语击打的词根。滑行载具义与锤子义在英语里汇到同一个词形，雪橇义的来源细节存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Sledge splits into two groups: the winter vehicle and its own verb, and the heavy hammer with its verbs of striking, taunting and criticizing.
sensesIntro.cn: sledge 分成两组：冬季载具以及它自己的动词用法；重锤以及敲击、嘲讽、抨击这组动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy object that slams forward, thick and blunt, across a flat white surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件厚重、钝拙的东西贴着白色平面猛冲向前。

branches.en: The runner vehicle and its own verb are the winter pair.
branches.cn: 滑行载具与它的动词构成冬季这一对义项。

branches.en: Cricket slang makes the sledge a verbal blow against a rival.
branches.cn: 板球俚语把雪橇变成挥向对手的语言一锤。

branches.en: The heavy hammer and its striking verb come from the shortened sledgehammer.
branches.cn: 重锤与它对应的敲击动词来自缩略词 sledgehammer。

branches.en: The blow of the hammer easily becomes an attack on a plan in words.
branches.cn: 锤子的一击很容易变成以言语对一份计划的攻击。

branches.en: Both the sledge and the hammer are long, heavy and built to go forward in a straight line.
branches.cn: 雪橇与大锤都是长而重、适合直线前冲的东西。

intro.en: Sledge builds compounds such as sledgehammer and takes the ordinary English endings -s, -ed, -er and -ing; its Dutch origin supplies no living prefix.
intro.cn: sledge 能构成 sledgehammer 这样的复合词，并接上 -s、-ed、-er、-ing 等英语词尾；其荷兰语来源没有留下仍在使用的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Sledge has no Latin ancestry; its source is Middle Dutch slegge within the Germanic hammer family, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: sledge 没有拉丁语来源，其源头是中古荷兰语 slegge，属日耳曼语中表示锤子的一族词，因此拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Slegge is the Dutch word for a heavy hammer.
items.exampleCN: slegge 是荷兰语中表示重锤的词。

items.example: Slean gives the striking root to slay and to sledge.
items.exampleCN: slean 为 slay 与 sledge 提供「击打」的词根。

items.example: Hammer joins sledge in the compound sledgehammer.
items.exampleCN: hammer 与 sledge 在 sledgehammer 中组合。

items.example: He broke the stone with a sledgehammer.
items.exampleCN: 他用大锤把石头砸开了。

items.meaningCN: 复数或第三人称单数词尾
items.example: The suffix forms sledges.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 sledges。

items.example: The suffix forms sledged.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 sledged。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix forms sledging.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 sledging。

items.example: The suffix forms sledger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 sledger。

items.example: A dog sledge carried the doctor through the blizzard.
items.exampleCN: 一辆狗拉雪橇把医生送过了暴风雪。

definition_zh: （毛发、外表）光滑的；溜光发亮的；（设计、外形）线条流畅的；（人）油滑的；使光滑；使平整
definition_en: smooth and shiny, often in a way that looks well cared for or stylishly streamlined
core_image: 一只手顺着动物光亮的背脊摸过去，不留一丝阻力
scene: 展台上最新款跑车的车身像被水冲过一样发亮，设计师正指着那条顺滑的弧线。The designer stroked the sleek body of the new sports car.
sceneCN: 这里 sleek 是「线条流畅、表面光滑」（第 3 个义项：形容设计或外形流畅光滑）；句意：设计师用手沿着那辆新跑车流畅光滑的车身摸过去。

pos.zh: 光滑的；油亮的；线条流畅的；油滑的
使光滑；使平整（较罕用，见于旧式或文雅表达）

derivatives.zh: 光滑地；流畅地
光滑；油亮；线条流畅
光亮顺滑的（较少见）

senses.title: Smooth and glossy hair or fur
senses.definition: smooth, soft, and shiny, especially of hair or an animal coat
senses.definitionCN: 光滑、柔软而有光泽的，多指毛发或动物皮毛
senses.example: The dog had a coat of sleek black fur.
senses.exampleCN: 那只狗长着一身光滑乌亮的黑毛。
senses.why: The word began in animal description, so its oldest image is a well-groomed coat that light slides down.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早用于描写动物，所以最原始的画面是一身梳理得极好的毛，光一照就顺势滑下去。

senses.title: Well-fed and healthy in appearance
senses.definition: looking plump, healthy, and well cared for
senses.definitionCN: 看上去丰满、健康、照料得当
senses.example: The horses in the stable were sleek and strong.
senses.exampleCN: 马厩里的马匹体态丰润又健壮。
senses.why: A shiny coat was a sign of good feeding, so a sleek animal came to mean a well-kept one.
senses.whyCN: 发亮的皮毛是喂养得好的标志，于是光滑的动物就引申为被照料得很好、体态健康。

senses.title: Smoothly shaped and beautifully streamlined
senses.definition: having a smooth, elegant, and flowing shape or design
senses.definitionCN: 外形或设计平滑、优美而流畅
senses.example: The phone has a sleek metal body.
senses.exampleCN: 这款手机的金属机身线条流畅。
senses.why: The image of a smooth surface moved from fur to manufactured objects that look equally polished.
senses.whyCN: 光滑表面的意象从皮毛移到人造器物上，形容同样被打磨得毫不拖泥带水的设计。

senses.title: Dishonestly smooth in manner
senses.definition: speaking or behaving in a way that is too smooth and seems insincere
senses.definitionCN: 言行过于圆通流畅而显得不真诚
senses.example: Nobody believed the sleek young salesman.
senses.exampleCN: 没人相信那个油嘴滑舌的年轻推销员。
senses.why: When the smoothness belongs to a person rather than a surface, it hints at a polished manner that hides something.
senses.whyCN: 当这种「光滑」用来说人而不是说表面，就暗示话术中打磨过的圆滑，像是在遮掩什么。

senses.title: To make something smooth and neat
senses.definition: to make something smooth or tidy by rubbing or combing it
senses.definitionCN: 通过抚摸或梳理使某物光滑整齐
senses.example: She sleeked her hair back behind her ears.
senses.exampleCN: 她把头发往耳后捋得服服帖帖。
senses.why: The adjective gave a verb, so the quality becomes the action of pressing a rough surface into smoothness.
senses.whyCN: 形容词派生出动词，于是「光滑」这一属性变成了把粗糙表面按压平整的动作。

intro.en: Sleek is usually traced to a northern root meaning smooth, via a form in Old Norse or Old French.
intro.cn: sleek 一般认为源自表示「光滑」的北方语源，经由古诺尔斯语或古法语的形式进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed form related to slik suggests a smooth surface.
items.cn: 与 slik 相关的重构形式暗示「光滑的表面」。

items.en: A cognate form means smooth or even; some scholars point to this source.
items.cn: 同源形式意为「平滑、平坦」，部分学者认为英语由此传入。

items.en: Another proposal is a French adjective meaning smooth, now lost.
items.cn: 另一种说法认为来自现已消失的法语形容词，意为光滑。

items.en: Sleek first describes the smooth, glossy coats of animals.
items.cn: sleek 最初描写动物光滑发亮的皮毛。

items.en: The sense widened to streamlined design, polished style, and smooth talk.
items.cn: 词义扩展到流畅的外形设计、打磨过的风格以及圆滑的言辞。

note.en: Sleek sits between glossy and smooth, and also covers a stylish shape and a slippery manner.
note.cn: sleek 处于「油亮」与「平滑」之间，还能用来形容时髦的外形和滑不留手的言行。

entries.definition: in a smooth and glossy way
entries.definitionCN: 光滑地；流畅地

entries.definition: the quality of being smooth and shiny
entries.definitionCN: 光滑；油亮

entries.definition: to satisfy thirst or a desire
entries.definitionCN: 解渴；满足（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: having an even surface without bumps
entries.definitionCN: 平滑的；没有凹凸的

entries.definition: bright and shiny on the surface
entries.definitionCN: 光亮而有光泽的

entries.definition: shaped to move easily through air or water
entries.definitionCN: 流线型的

normalIntro.en: Sleek is a word you can feel with your fingers: everything about it slides the same way.
normalIntro.cn: sleek 是一个能用手指感觉的词：它涉及的一切都朝同一个方向顺滑地滑过去。

normal.en: A sleek coat shines, so sleek pairs well with hair and fur.
normal.cn: sleek 的皮毛会发亮，所以它常与头发、毛发搭配。

normal.en: A sleek design looks clean because every curve is continuous.
normal.cn: sleek design 显得干净，因为每一段弧度都是连续不断的。

normal.en: Call a person sleek and you mean smooth, practiced, and possibly sly.
normal.cn: 说某人 sleek，意思是圆熟流利，还可能带点狡猾。

normal.en: Sleek as a verb shows the action: sleek your hair, sleek a surface.
normal.cn: sleek 作动词时表示动作：把头发捋顺，把表面弄平。

normal.en: Compare glossy and smooth: glossy is about shine, smooth is about evenness, sleek is both plus style.
normal.cn: 对比 glossy 与 smooth：glossy 讲光泽，smooth 讲平整，sleek 兼具二者并多了风格感。

abstract.en: Run a hand down an otter back and feel the light glide.
abstract.cn: 顺着水獭的背脊摸下去，感受光在皮毛上滑走。

abstract.en: Imagine a stallion brushed until it seems to glow.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹被反复刷洗得几乎发光的公马。

abstract.en: See a car body with no gaps, only one long curve.
abstract.cn: 想象一具没有缝隙、只有一道长弧线的车身。

examples.en: The cat licked its sleek fur in the afternoon sun.
examples.cn: 猫在午后的阳光里舔着光滑的皮毛。

examples.en: The sleek glass tower dominates the skyline.
examples.cn: 那座线条流畅的玻璃大厦占据了天际线的主位。

examples.en: He combed his hair down and made it perfectly sleek.
examples.cn: 他把头发梳下来，弄得一丝不乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四里可」顺：一路光滑，走四里都没遇到一处磕碰；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为经古诺尔斯语或古法语中表示「光滑、平坦」的形式进入英语，核心义「表面顺滑、毫无阻滞」。

sensesIntro.en: Sleek starts with glossy animal coats, then the healthy look they signal, then streamlined design, and finally a too-smooth manner.
sensesIntro.cn: sleek 从动物油亮的皮毛开始，进而指皮毛所透露的健康体态，再到流畅的设计，最后指过于圆滑的言行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sliding without any resistance over a glossy surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在光亮的表面上毫无阻力地滑过。

branches.en: The glossy coat is the oldest and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 油亮皮毛是最古老、最字面的义项。

branches.en: A glossy coat signals good feeding and health.
branches.cn: 油亮皮毛暗示喂养得当、体态健康。

branches.en: Streamlined objects carry the same smoothness into design.
branches.cn: 流线型器物把同一种光滑带进了设计。

branches.en: Hair and car bodies are both judged by how smoothly they flow.
branches.cn: 头发与车身的评价依据都是它顺滑流动的程度。

branches.en: Polished design and polished talk share the idea of surface without friction.
branches.cn: 打磨过的设计与打磨过的言辞共享「表面毫无摩擦」这一概念。

intro.en: Sleek is a complete Germanic word, so its family is built with English endings rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: sleek 本身是完整的日耳曼词，所以它的词族靠英语词尾构成，而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no direct Latin ancestor for sleek; this section lists the closely related Germanic forms.
latinIntro.cn: sleek 没有直接对应的拉丁语祖先，这里列出关系密切的日耳曼语形式。

items.example: Sleek describes coats, cars, and curves.
items.exampleCN: sleek 可描写皮毛、汽车与曲线。

items.example: The verb sleek means to flatten hair or cloth.
items.exampleCN: 动词 sleek 意为把头发或布料弄平。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sleekly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 sleekly。

items.example: The cat moved sleekly through the grass.
items.exampleCN: 猫滑顺地穿过草丛。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms sleekness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 sleekness。

items.example: The sleekness of the seal skin surprised the visitors.
items.exampleCN: 海豹皮的光滑程度让游客们惊讶。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the rare sleeky.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成较少见的 sleeky。

items.example: Sleeky is a rare variant of sleek.
items.exampleCN: sleeky 是 sleek 的少见变体。

items.example: Sleek-haired breeds need little grooming.
items.exampleCN: 短毛光滑的品种几乎不用打理。

items.example: A well-kempt coat looks sleek.
items.exampleCN: 梳理得整齐的皮毛看起来就光滑。

definition_zh: 睡眠者；睡得很熟的人；（列车）卧铺；卧铺车厢；（建筑）枕木；爆冷门的作品或选手；无人察觉的潜伏者
definition_en: a person who sleeps, or anything that lies quiet and unnoticed until it suddenly matters
core_image: 铁轨下面静静躺着的木梁，上面跑着呼啸而过的火车
scene: 老式夜行列车开进站台，车厢里的小隔间铺好了被子，乘客们提着行李等着上车休息。Comfortable padded sleepers fill the overnight train to Glasgow.
sceneCN: 这里 sleeper 是「卧铺车厢」（第 2 个义项：列车中带床铺的车厢）；句意：开往格拉斯哥的夜班列车设有舒适的软卧车厢。

pos.zh: 睡眠者；熟睡的人
卧铺；卧铺车厢
枕木
爆冷门的作品或选手；潜伏者

derivatives.zh: 睡觉（sleeper 的基础动词）
困倦的（sleep 加 -y 构成）
睡眠中的（如 sleeping car）
失眠的；无法入睡的

senses.title: A person who is asleep
senses.definition: someone who is sleeping, or someone who sleeps in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 正在睡觉的人，或睡得如何的某种人
senses.example: She is a light sleeper and wakes at every sound.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡觉很浅，一有声音就醒。
senses.why: The ending -er adds a doer to the verb sleep, so a sleeper is simply the person who performs the action.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 在动词 sleep 后加上「做事的人」，所以 sleeper 就是做出「睡」这个动作的人。

senses.title: A carriage with beds on a train
senses.definition: a coach on a train with beds for passengers who travel overnight
senses.definitionCN: 夜间列车上设有床铺的车厢
senses.example: We booked two seats in the sleeper to Edinburgh.
senses.exampleCN: 我们订了两个去爱丁堡的卧铺。
senses.why: The person who sleeps and the place where one sleeps met in the word, so a carriage built for sleep took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 「睡的人」与「睡觉的地方」在这个词里合一，于是专为睡觉设计的车厢也叫 sleeper。

senses.title: A heavy beam under a railway track
senses.definition: a long timber or concrete beam that lies under the rails and supports them
senses.definitionCN: 铺在铁轨下方、起承托作用的长条木梁或混凝土梁
senses.example: Workers replaced the rotten sleepers on the old line.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们更换了旧线路上的朽坏枕木。
senses.why: The beam lies quietly flat on the ground, like a body sleeping, so the builders reused the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 这根横梁平平地躺在地上，像一具熟睡的身子，于是修路的人借用了同一个词。

senses.title: Something unexpectedly successful
senses.definition: a film, book, player, or team that attracts little notice at first and then becomes very successful
senses.definitionCN: 起初不受注意，后来却大获成功的电影、书、选手或球队
senses.example: The small film became a sleeper hit at the box office.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小成本电影在票房上意外爆红。
senses.why: It stayed unnoticed while it slept, and the surprise is exactly what makes the later success feel like a sleeper waking up.
senses.whyCN: 它「睡着」时无人留意，而正是这份被忽视让后来的成功显得像黑马突然苏醒。

senses.title: A hidden agent who waits
senses.definition: a spy or member of a group who lives an ordinary life for years before being activated
senses.definitionCN: 长期隐居在平常生活中、待命后才行动的间谍或组织成员
senses.example: The police arrested a sleeper who had lived in the town for years.
senses.exampleCN: 警方逮捕了一名在小镇生活多年的潜伏者。
senses.why: The central image is dormancy, so a person planted and left to sleep fits the word perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「蛰伏」，一个被安插后长期沉睡般不动的人，正好套进这个词。

intro.en: Sleeper is the Old English verb sleep, a Germanic word, with the agent ending -er added.
intro.cn: sleeper 由古英语动词 sleep（日耳曼语词）加上表示施事者的词尾 -er 构成。

items.en: A reconstructed verb meant to sleep, with close relatives in Dutch and German.
items.cn: 重构动词意为「睡觉」，在荷兰语和德语中有近亲。

items.en: Slæpan and the noun slæp name sleep and sleeping.
items.cn: slæpan 与名词 slæp 表示睡觉与睡眠。

items.en: The ending -er creates sleepers, a word for the person who sleeps.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 造出 sleepers 一词，指睡觉的人。

items.en: The word spreads to objects that rest low and quiet, such as beams.
items.cn: 词义扩展到低伏静置的物件，例如横梁。

items.en: Rail travel gives sleepers to the railway and to the coach with beds.
items.cn: 铁路旅行使 sleeper 同时成为铁轨枕木与卧铺车厢的名称。

items.en: The dormant image yields the unexpected hit and the hidden agent.
items.cn: 「潜伏」的意象又生出意外的爆款与隐藏的特工。

note.en: Sleeper belongs to the sleep family and also to the railway, entertainment, and spy fields, where dormancy is the link.
note.cn: sleeper 属于「睡」词族，也出现在铁路、娱乐和间谍等场景中，把它们连起来的正是「沉睡潜伏」这一层意思。

entries.definition: to rest with your eyes closed and your mind inactive
entries.definitionCN: 睡觉；休息

entries.definition: tired and ready to sleep
entries.definitionCN: 困倦的

entries.definition: unable to sleep
entries.definitionCN: 失眠的；无法入睡的

entries.definition: a simple fold-down bed on a night train
entries.definitionCN: 夜间列车上的简易折叠铺位

entries.definition: a narrow bed in a train or on a ship
entries.definitionCN: 火车或船上的窄铺

entries.definition: the raised surface beside a railway track
entries.definitionCN: 铁路站台

normalIntro.en: Sleeper is built from sleep plus -er, so every sense keeps the image of something at rest.
normalIntro.cn: sleeper 由 sleep 加 -er 构成，所以每个义项都保留着「静止休憩」的画面。

normal.en: A heavy sleeper does not notice alarm clocks.
normal.cn: a heavy sleeper 指睡得很沉、闹钟都吵不醒的人。

normal.en: The -er ending marks the person, as in teacher and worker.
normal.cn: 词尾 -er 标记做事的人，就像 teacher 和 worker 一样。

normal.en: The sleeper coach is the car built for sleeping.
normal.cn: sleeper coach 就是专为睡觉造的车厢。

normal.en: Railway sleepers are the beams the rails lie on.
normal.cn: 铁路枕木就是铁轨躺在上面的那根横梁。

normal.en: Sleeper hit describes a work that succeeds without early noise.
normal.cn: sleeper hit 形容起初无人问津却意外成功的作品。

abstract.en: See a person curled in a bunk while the train sways.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人蜷在铺位上，列车左右轻摇。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket laid over a flat bed in a small cabin.
abstract.cn: 想象小隔间里一张铺好被子的平铺铺位。

abstract.en: Watch a heavy timber lying still under two steel rails.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粗木梁静静躺在两根钢轨下方。

examples.en: My father is a heavy sleeper, so the storm did not wake him.
examples.cn: 我父亲睡得很沉，那场暴风雨也没把他吵醒。

examples.en: They took the sleeper from London to Inverness.
examples.cn: 他们搭乘卧铺列车从伦敦去因弗内斯。

examples.en: The novel was a sleeper that sold millions after a slow start.
examples.cn: 这本小说起初销量平平，后来却成了热卖的黑马。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯哩珀」——斯文地躺着、呼呼入睡的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 slæpan（睡觉）+ 施事后缀 -er → sleeper（睡觉的人）；后引申为供人睡觉的车厢、躺在地上的枕木，以及「蛰伏未动」的人与作品。

sensesIntro.en: Sleeper moves from the person who sleeps, to the carriage made for sleep, to the beam that lies flat, and finally to anything dormant that later surprises.
sensesIntro.cn: sleeper 从「睡觉的人」出发，再到「供人睡觉的车厢」，再到「平躺的枕木」，最后指「蛰伏许久才突然显眼」的人或物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy beam lying calm and quiet under the running rails.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根粗壮横梁静静躺在奔驰的铁轨之下。

branches.en: The person who sleeps is the root sense of the agent noun.
branches.cn: 睡觉的人是这个施事名词的根本义项。

branches.en: The train carriage is the place where the sleeper sleeps.
branches.cn: 列车车厢是睡觉的人睡觉的地方。

branches.en: The railway beam borrows the image of something lying flat.
branches.cn: 铁轨下的横梁借用了「平躺之物」的意象。

branches.en: Both the coach and the beam are low, supporting, and unnoticed.
branches.cn: 车厢与枕木都低伏在下、起承托作用、不惹人注意。

branches.en: The unexpected hit and the hidden agent both lie dormant before they act.
branches.cn: 意外的黑马与潜伏者都在行动前先蛰伏不动。

intro.en: Sleeper is a Germanic root with the native English ending -er, and its family is built with -y and -less.
intro.cn: sleeper 由日耳曼词根加上英语本族词尾 -er 构成，它的词族又靠 -y 与 -less 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Sleep has no Latin ancestor; the related Latin idea of rest appears only in learned borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: sleep 没有拉丁语祖先，拉丁语中「休息」的概念只出现在学术借词里。

items.meaning: to rest in a state of sleep
items.example: The base verb is sleep.
items.exampleCN: 基础动词是 sleep。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 做某事的人或物（施事后缀）
items.example: The suffix -er forms sleeper from sleep.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 由 sleep 构成 sleeper。

items.example: Sleeper keeps the agent meaning.
items.exampleCN: sleeper 保留施事含义。

items.example: The suffix -y forms sleepy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 sleepy。

items.example: Sleepy describes a nodding child.
items.exampleCN: sleepy 形容一个直打瞌睡的孩子。

items.example: The suffix -less forms sleepless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 sleepless。

items.example: A sleepless night leaves you tired.
items.exampleCN: 一夜无眠会让你疲惫。

items.example: Sleeping car is the older name for a sleeper coach.
items.exampleCN: sleeping car 是卧铺车厢的旧称。

items.example: The prefix over- forms oversleep.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 构成 oversleep。

items.meaning: a hidden group waiting to act
items.example: Sleeper cell uses the dormant image.
items.exampleCN: sleeper cell 借用「潜伏」的意象。

definition_zh: 口号；标语；广告语；（旧）苏格兰高地氏族的战斗呐喊
definition_en: a short catchy phrase used to advertise something or to rally people behind a cause
core_image: 一群人齐声喊出的短促一声，把所有人拧成一股劲
scene: 大选前夜，街角的广告牌换上了新横幅，志愿者举着纸板箱在路口向路过的行人发传单。The slogan promised lower prices for every family.
sceneCN: 这里 slogan 是「口号、标语」（第 1 个义项：宣传时反复使用的一句短话）；句意：新标语承诺让每个家庭都享受更低的物价。

pos.zh: 口号；标语；广告语；战斗呐喊（旧义）

derivatives.zh: 爱用口号的人；口号作者
口号式宣传；堆砌口号
把……编成口号（较少见）

senses.title: A short memorable phrase in advertising
senses.definition: a short phrase used in advertising that is easy to remember and repeat
senses.definitionCN: 广告中使用的简短、易记、易复述的句子
senses.example: The brand changed its slogan after thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌在三十年后更换了广告语。
senses.why: The old battle cry was a single shout that everyone knew, so commerce took that form for its memorable lines.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的战斗呐喊是一声人人都懂的短喊，商业于是把这种形式借来做易记的广告语。

senses.title: A phrase summing up a cause
senses.definition: a short phrase that states the aim of a political or social movement
senses.definitionCN: 概括某个政治或社会运动目标的短句
senses.example: Freedom and bread became the rallying slogan of the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 「自由与面包」成了那场罢工的号召口号。
senses.why: A rally slogan gathers people in the same way a clan cry once gathered warriors under one voice.
senses.whyCN: 集会口号聚拢人群的方式，正和当年氏族呐喊把战士聚到一声之下一样。

senses.title: The old Highland battle cry
senses.titleCN: 苏格兰氏族的战斗呐喊
senses.definition: the war cry of a Scottish Highland clan, shouted as its members charged
senses.definitionCN: 苏格兰高地氏族冲锋时齐声喊出的战斗呐喊
senses.example: Each clan had its own slogan called out before battle.
senses.exampleCN: 每个氏族都有自己开战前喊出的呐喊词。
senses.why: This is where the word started: a shout shared by a whole kin group at the moment of attack.
senses.whyCN: 词义的起点就在这里：整个宗族在进攻那一刻共同喊出的一声。

senses.title: A stock phrase repeated without thought
senses.definition: a phrase used so often that it becomes a thoughtless formula
senses.definitionCN: 被用得太多、成了不加思索的套话的短语
senses.example: We are all in this together has become a slogan in his speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 「我们同舟共济」已经成了他演讲里的套话。
senses.why: Anything shouted by many voices can end up worn thin, so a slogan can also be a ready-made line with no weight left.
senses.whyCN: 被许多人齐声喊过的话最终会被磨薄，所以 slogan 也能指一句毫无分量的现成套语。

intro.en: Slogan comes from Scottish Gaelic sluagh-ghairm, the war cry of a Highland clan, through English spelling.
intro.cn: slogan 源自苏格兰盖尔语 sluagh-ghairm，即高地氏族的战斗呐喊，经英语拼写改造而成。

items.en: Sluagh means host or army, and gairm means a call or cry.
items.cn: sluagh 意为「人群、军队」，gairm 意为「呼喊」。

items.en: Sluagh-ghairm is the collective shout of a clan going into battle.
items.cn: sluagh-ghairm 就是氏族出战时齐声的呼喊。

items.en: The spelling slogan appears in Scottish writing for this clan cry.
items.cn: 十六世纪苏格兰英语写作中以 slogan 这一拼写记录这种氏族呐喊。

items.en: The word travels south and gradually loses its purely military sense.
items.cn: 这个词向南传播并逐渐失去纯军事含义。

items.en: Printed campaigns and newspapers give slogan its modern advertising use.
items.cn: 印刷宣传与报纸让 slogan 获得现代广告用语的用法。

note.en: Slogan is a Gaelic word for a clan shout, and it now sits among words for mottoes, catchlines, and repeated phrases.
note.cn: slogan 原是盖尔语中氏族呐喊的词，如今与格言、标题句、重复短语等词同处一个语义圈。

entries.definition: a person who invents or repeats slogans
entries.definitionCN: 编口号或爱喊口号的人

entries.definition: the use of slogans instead of real argument
entries.definitionCN: 以口号代替真正论点的做法

entries.definition: to turn something into a slogan
entries.definitionCN: 把某事编成口号

entries.definition: a short phrase expressing the aim of a group
entries.definitionCN: 座右铭；格言

entries.definition: a phrase made famous by repeated use
entries.definitionCN: 流行语；标志性口头禅

entries.definition: words shouted together in a rhythm
entries.definitionCN: 有节奏地齐声喊叫

normalIntro.en: Slogan is a battle cry that became a sales pitch, so every sense keeps the idea of one short phrase spoken for many.
normalIntro.cn: slogan 是变成推销话术的战斗呐喊，所以每个义项都保留着「一句短话替众人发声」的意思。

normal.en: A commercial slogan is short so that people can repeat it.
normal.cn: 商业口号要短，才方便人们复述。

normal.en: A campaign slogan names a goal in a few words.
normal.cn: 竞选口号用几个词点明目标。

normal.en: Chant a slogan and you hear the clan cry behind it.
normal.cn: chant a slogan 时，背后就是氏族的呐喊声。

normal.en: Sloganeering is empty slogan labour, all voice and no thought.
normal.cn: sloganeering 指空洞的口号工程，只有喊声没有思考。

normal.en: Compare motto and slogan: a motto is a group creed, a slogan is aimed at buyers or voters.
normal.cn: 对比 motto 与 slogan：motto 是团体的信条，slogan 面向买家或选民。

abstract.en: Picture a supermarket aisle where one line hangs over every shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象超市货架上方悬着同一句话，统管整条过道。

abstract.en: See a crowd holding placards with the same few words.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人手举标语牌，牌上是同样的几个词。

abstract.en: Hear warriors roar one name as they charge downhill.
abstract.cn: 想象战士们冲下山坡时齐声吼出同一个名号。

examples.en: The slogan on the poster was printed in huge red letters.
examples.cn: 海报上的标语印成了巨大的红字。

examples.en: Every election brings a new set of slogans.
examples.cn: 每次选举都会带来一批新口号。

examples.en: Their slogan promised a cleaner, quieter city.
examples.cn: 他们的口号承诺要建一座更干净、更安静的城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯罗梗」——一句话里藏个梗，喊出来人人都记得；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 苏格兰盖尔语 sluagh-ghairm（sluagh「人群、军队」+ gairm「呼喊」）→ 苏格兰英语 slogan（氏族战斗呐喊）→ 英语 slogan（口号、标语、广告语）。

sensesIntro.en: Slogan goes from the Highland clan cry to commercial and political catchlines, and ends with the worn-out phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: slogan 从高地氏族的呐喊出发，走向商业与政治的短句，最后落到被喊旧的套话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many voices roaring one short call at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多声音在同一刻吼出同一句短短的呼喊。

branches.en: Advertising borrows the shout and trims it to a memorable line.
branches.cn: 广告借用了这声呼喊，把它削成一句易记的话。

branches.en: A movement turns the shout into a shared aim.
branches.cn: 社会运动把呼喊变成共同的目标。

branches.en: The clan battle cry is the source sense.
branches.cn: 氏族战斗呐喊是词义的源头。

branches.en: A rally and a clan charge both need one voice to unite the group.
branches.cn: 集会与氏族冲锋都靠同一个声音把众人连成一体。

branches.en: What sells first as a fresh line can fade into an empty formula.
branches.cn: 一句新鲜的话先能推销，也可能褪色成空洞的套话。

intro.en: Slogan is a compound from Gaelic, not from Latin, so its parts are Gaelic words and its derivatives are English.
intro.cn: slogan 是盖尔语的复合词而非拉丁语来源，所以它的构件是两个盖尔语词，派生词则由英语构成。

latinIntro.en: Slogan has no Latin ancestor; the related Latin words below belong only to the idea of a call or shout.
latinIntro.cn: slogan 没有拉丁语祖先，下方列出的相关拉丁词只与「呼喊」这一概念同属一个语义场。

items.example: Sluagh supplies the crowd of the cry.
items.exampleCN: sluagh 提供「众人」这一半含义。

items.example: Gairm supplies the act of shouting.
items.exampleCN: gairm 提供「呼喊」这一半含义。

items.meaning: the war cry of a clan
items.example: The compound is the direct source of slogan.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是 slogan 的直接来源。

items.example: Slogan keeps the cry but changes its purpose.
items.exampleCN: slogan 保留了呼喊，却换了用途。

items.example: The suffix -eer forms sloganeer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eer 构成 sloganeer。

items.example: A sloganeer works with words and volume.
items.exampleCN: sloganeer 与词句和声量打交道。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms sloganeering.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 sloganeering。

items.example: Sloganeering often hides weak policy.
items.exampleCN: 口号式宣传常常掩盖薄弱的政策。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms sloganize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 sloganize。

items.example: Sloganize turns an idea into a line.
items.exampleCN: sloganize 把一个想法变成一句话。

definition_zh: 马虎的；草率的；邋遢的；宽松肥大的；湿软的
definition_en: careless and untidy in the way something is done, kept, or dressed
core_image: 一碗稀泥被打翻，黏糊糊地摊了一桌子
scene: 室友总把湿毛巾和脏碗堆在水槽边，房间一团糟。My roommate leaves wet towels and dirty bowls by the sink, and his sloppy habits drive me crazy.
sceneCN: 这里 sloppy 是「邋遢的」（第 3 个义项：人做事不整洁、随随便便）；句意：室友总把湿毛巾脏碗堆在水槽边，他邋遢的习惯让我受不了。

pos.zh: 马虎的；草率的；邋遢的；宽松肥大的；湿软的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly，义为「马虎地；邋遢地」
基础词加名词后缀 -ness，义为「马虎；邋遢」
同源动词 slop 的过去分词，义为「被泼洒得湿漉漉的」，多用于口语

senses.title: Doing something carelessly
senses.definition: done quickly and without care, so that mistakes are likely
senses.definitionCN: 做得快又不仔细，容易出错
senses.example: His report was full of sloppy mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 他的报告里到处是马虎造成的错误。
senses.why: If water is slopped about, it spills everywhere, and sloppiness of hand becomes sloppiness of mind.
senses.whyCN: 水被随意泼洒就会弄得到处都是，手上的糊弄就变成了脑子里的马虎。

senses.title: Untidy and loose in dress
senses.definition: loose-fitting and untidy clothes worn with little attention to appearance
senses.definitionCN: 衣服宽松肥大、穿得不讲究，不修边幅
senses.example: He showed up in a sloppy T-shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着一件松垮垮的T恤就来了。
senses.why: Baggy clothes hang on the body the way spilled water spreads on a floor, so untidy dress is a sloppy mess worn on the person.
senses.whyCN: 宽松衣服松垮地挂身上，就像泼在地上的水四处摊开，于是不整洁的穿着就是穿在身上的「糊成一团」。

senses.title: Being untidy in habits
senses.titleCN: 邋遢的；生活习惯松散的
senses.definition: habitually disorderly in personal habits or surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 个人习惯或生活环境习惯性脏乱
senses.example: My roommate is sloppy and never cleans his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 我室友很邋遢，从不收拾他的桌子。
senses.why: The wet, messy image easily moves from things to people who keep things that way.
senses.whyCN: 湿漉漉、乱糟糟的画面很容易从物品转向那些把生活过成这样的人。

senses.title: Wet and soft
senses.definition: wet, soft, and unpleasantly mushy, especially of food or ground
senses.definitionCN: 湿软、稀糊糊令人不适的，多指食物或地面
senses.example: The rain turned the path into sloppy mud.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水把小径变成了稀泥。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: slop is liquid waste, so sloppy means literally wet like slop.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：slop 指泔水般的液体垃圾，sloppy 字面上就是「像泔水一样湿」。

senses.title: Overly emotional
senses.definition: excessively sentimental or gushing, especially in a public way
senses.definitionCN: 感情表达过度、黏黏糊糊的
senses.example: The ending of the film felt too sloppy for me.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的结尾在我看来太煽情了。
senses.why: A slurping, wet kiss is physically sloppy, and a scene that pours out feelings has the same sticky excess.
senses.whyCN: 吧唧一口的湿吻是身体上的湿软，而把感情一股脑倒出来的场面有着同一种黏腻的过度。

senses.title: Loose and careless in speech or writing
senses.definition: using vague, careless, or inaccurate language
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作含糊、不准确、不严谨
senses.example: Sloppy language makes a strong argument weak.
senses.exampleCN: 含糊的语言会让有力的论点变弱。
senses.why: Words thrown down like wet food on a plate leave stains without shape, which is exactly what careless writing looks like.
senses.whyCN: 词句像湿软的食物泼在盘子上，只留下没有形状的污渍，这正是草率写出来的文字的样子。

senses.title: Boiled soft or runny
senses.definition: cooked until soft and watery, especially of eggs or vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 煮到软烂出水，多指蛋或蔬菜
senses.example: She likes sloppy scrambled eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢炒得稀软的鸡蛋。
senses.why: Food cooks until it slumps and runs, which is the mushy core of the word in the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 食物煮到塌软流汁，这就是这个词在厨房里那团软烂的核心意象。

senses.title: Carelessly warm behavior
senses.definition: friendly in an informal, unpolished, and touchy way
senses.definitionCN: 友好但不讲究、爱搂搂抱抱的
senses.example: He gave me a sloppy hug at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他在门口给了我一个黏糊糊的随意拥抱。
senses.why: Physical sloppiness turns into affection: a loose, messy, unguarded friendliness.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的松垮黏糊转化为感情：一种松散、凌乱、不设防的亲切。

intro.en: Sloppy belongs to the noun slop, liquid waste from a kitchen, and developed its careless sense around the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: sloppy 来自名词 slop（厨房里的泔水、液体垃圾），约在十九世纪发展出「马虎」之义。

items.en: The noun slop means mud, slush, or liquid waste, probably from a Low German source related to a verb meaning to slop or splash.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 slop 指泥浆、雪水或液体垃圾，一般认为来自低地德语，与表示「泼洒」的动词同源。

items.en: The adjective sloppy first means wet and slushy, following slop directly.
items.cn: 形容词 sloppy 首见于十七世纪，意思是湿软、泥泞，直接由 slop 而来。

items.en: Sloppy extends to loose clothing and soft, watery food.
items.cn: sloppy 扩展到指宽大的衣物和软烂出水的食物。

items.en: The figurative sense of careless and untidy appears in writing about soldiers, sailors, and sloppy work.
items.cn: 十九世纪，「马虎、邋遢」的比喻义出现在关于士兵、水手和草率工作的文字中。

items.en: Modern English keeps sloppy for careless habits, loose dress, sloppy language, and sloppy joes.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 sloppy 表示马虎的习惯、宽松衣着、含糊语言以及软面包三明治。

note.en: Sloppy looks alike slop and slip, and near in meaning to careless words that stress speed, neglect, or dirt.
note.cn: sloppy 形近 slop 与 slip，在意义上靠近强调快速、疏忽或脏乱的「粗心」类词。

entries.definition: liquid waste or wet mud
entries.definitionCN: 泔水；稀泥

entries.definition: done quickly and carelessly
entries.definitionCN: 草率匆忙的，与 sloppy 的「马虎」义直接相邻

entries.definition: careless in work or method
entries.definitionCN: 马虎敷衍的；只是拼写与 sloppy 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: not paying enough attention
entries.definitionCN: 粗心大意的

entries.definition: not neat or orderly
entries.definitionCN: 不整洁的

entries.definition: neat and orderly
entries.definitionCN: 整洁的；有条理的，与 sloppy 的邋遢义相反

normalIntro.en: Sloppy is slop made into an adjective: a wet, spilling, careless mess.
normalIntro.cn: sloppy 是由名词 slop 变来的形容词：湿乎乎、泼洒一地、杂乱无章。

normal.en: Slop is wet kitchen waste, and sloppy describes the same mess spread across a person or a job.
normal.cn: slop 指厨房湿垃圾，sloppy 则描述同样的杂乱铺展到人身上或工作里。

normal.en: A sloppy job is a quick job with mistakes left in it.
normal.cn: a sloppy job 就是干得快、把错误留在里面的活。

normal.en: Sloppy clothes hang loose, like liquid spreading out.
normal.cn: sloppy 的衣着宽松下垂，像液体摊开一样。

normal.en: Sloppily and sloppiness keep the careless meaning; the adverb shows how, the noun names the habit.
normal.cn: sloppily 和 sloppiness 都保留「马虎」义：前者说明怎么做，后者指这种习性。

normal.en: Compare sloppy with careless: careless is about attention, sloppy adds dirt, looseness, and mess.
normal.cn: 对比 careless：它侧重注意力，sloppy 则多了脏、松垮、凌乱的感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl of porridge tipped over, grey and spreading over the edge of the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗粥被打翻，灰白黏稠地从桌沿摊下来。

abstract.en: Imagine putting on a sweater three sizes too large and never tucking it in.
abstract.cn: 想象套上一件大了好几个号的毛衣，从来不往裤子里塞。

abstract.en: Think of a sticky fingerprint left on a clean glass door.
abstract.cn: 想象干净玻璃门上留下一个黏黏的指印。

examples.en: The hotel manager criticised the sloppy service in the review.
examples.cn: 酒店经理在点评里批评了马虎的服务。

examples.en: Mud made the trail sloppy after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后，泥水让小路变得泥泞。

examples.en: Students who submit sloppy notes often lose marks in the exam.
examples.cn: 交上来字迹潦草、条理马虎笔记的学生常常在考试中丢分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死捞皮」—— 菜皮死命往身上捞，捞得满身黏糊糊，干活也马虎了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 低地德语的 slop（泥浆、泔水，一般认为）→ 中古英语 slop（泥浆；液体垃圾）→ sloppy（湿软的）→ 「松垮、马虎、邋遢」的比喻义；-y 是形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: From wet and messy, sloppy spreads to loose clothes, careless work, vague language, and sticky emotion.
sensesIntro.cn: sloppy 从「湿软杂乱」出发，扩展到宽松衣着、马虎的工作、含糊的语言和黏糊的情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl of thin porridge spilling over the edge of a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一碗稀粥从桌沿溢出来。

branches.en: Careless work is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 马虎草率的工作是现代最主要义项。

branches.en: Loose clothes and messy habits both wear the spill on the person.
branches.cn: 宽松衣着和邋遢习惯都是把「泼洒」穿在了人身上。

branches.en: Wet ground and soft food keep the literal mush.
branches.cn: 泥泞地面与软烂食物保留字面意义上的「糊软」。

branches.en: Sticky emotion and touchy warmth share the wet excess.
branches.cn: 黏腻的情感和黏糊的亲昵共享同一种湿软的过度。

branches.en: Vague writing and careless work are the same mess across a page or a desk.
branches.cn: 含糊的文字与马虎的工作，都是同一摊乱在纸上或桌上。

intro.en: Sloppy is the noun slop plus the adjective suffix -y, with sloppily and sloppiness built on the same stem.
intro.cn: sloppy 由名词 slop 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，sloppily 与 sloppiness 都建在同一个词干上。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is recorded; slop is generally traced to a Low German word for mud or liquid waste.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语祖词；slop 一般追溯到低地德语中表示泥浆或液体垃圾的词。

items.example: Slop gives the wet core of sloppy.
items.exampleCN: slop 提供 sloppy 的湿软核心。

items.meaning: to spill or splash a liquid
items.example: He slopped water on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 他把水泼到了地板上。

items.example: The suffix -y turns slop into sloppy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 slop 变成 sloppy。

items.example: Sloppily is the adverb form.
items.exampleCN: sloppily 是副词形式。

items.example: Sloppiness names the habit.
items.exampleCN: sloppiness 指这种习性。

items.example: The slop bucket was full again.
items.exampleCN: 泔水桶又满了。

items.meaning: a soft sandwich of minced meat
items.example: Sloppy joes were on the school menu.
items.exampleCN: 学校菜单上有软面包夹肉末。

items.example: A slapdash repair soon broke again.
items.exampleCN: 草率的修理很快又坏了。

items.example: Slipshod work costs money.
items.exampleCN: 马虎的活是要花钱的。

definition_zh: 狭槽；投币口；时段；位置；职位；安排时间
definition_en: a long narrow opening, or a position, time, or place that is kept free for something
core_image: 一个尺寸刚好的细长凹槽，正好能放下一样东西
scene: 邮局柜台贴着告示，提醒顾客把硬币投进机子上那条窄缝。A note at the post office counter asked customers to drop the coins into the narrow slot.
sceneCN: 这里 slot 是「投币口」（第 2 个义项：供投币或塞入东西的狭缝）；句意：邮局柜台贴着告示，请顾客把硬币投进那条窄缝。

pos.zh: 狭槽；投币口；时段；位置；职位
把……放进凹槽；安排时间；把……归入某类

derivatives.zh: slot 加过去分词后缀 -ed，义为「有狭槽的；被安排好的」
slot 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「开槽；排入」，见于 slotting fee（上架费）
slot 加表示施动者的 -er，义为「开槽机；开槽工」

senses.title: A narrow opening
senses.definition: a long, narrow hole or groove cut into a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上开出的细长孔或凹槽
senses.example: He pushed the letter through the slot in the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信从门上的投信口塞了进去。
senses.why: The Middle French root esclot means the hollow between ribs, so slot begins as a long hollow cut into a surface.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 esclot 指肋骨之间的凹陷，所以 slot 最初就是刻在表面上的长条凹槽。

senses.title: A coin slot
senses.definition: a small opening in a machine where coins or cards are inserted
senses.definitionCN: 机器上用来投入硬币或卡片的小口
senses.example: The machine ate my coin because the slot was blocked.
senses.exampleCN: 因为投币口堵住了，机器把我的硬币吞了。
senses.why: The groove becomes a mouth for the machine, and anything shaped to accept things follows the same opening.
senses.whyCN: 凹槽变成了机器的嘴巴，凡是按形状接收东西的口子都沿着同一意象延伸。

senses.title: A time slot
senses.definition: a fixed period of time reserved for an activity, broadcast, or booking
senses.definitionCN: 为某个活动、播出或预约预留的固定时间段
senses.example: The talk show was given the best slot of the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这档脱口秀拿到了晚上的黄金时段。
senses.why: Time is cut into narrow slots the way a card is cut into a shape, and only one thing fits in each.
senses.whyCN: 时间被切成一个个细长的槽位，就像卡片被剪成某一形状，每个槽位只放一样东西。

senses.title: A position in a list or system
senses.definition: an assigned position in an order, list, or series
senses.definitionCN: 在次序、清单或系列中被分配的位置
senses.example: His name took the last slot on the team list.
senses.exampleCN: 他的名字排在队伍名单的最后一个位置。
senses.why: A slot holds exactly one item, so any reserved place in a list is a slot.
senses.whyCN: 一个槽位恰好容纳一件东西，所以名单里任何一个预留的位置都是 slot。

senses.title: A job vacancy
senses.definition: an available position in an organization or team
senses.definitionCN: 组织或团队中空缺的岗位
senses.example: There is still one slot open on the course.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程还剩一个名额。
senses.why: Institutions are imagined as racks with numbered slots, and an empty slot is a vacancy waiting to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 机构被想象成一排带编号的槽架，空着的槽就是一个等待填补的空缺。

senses.title: To fit something into place
senses.definition: to put something into a slot or narrow space, often easily
senses.definitionCN: 把东西放进凹槽或狭窄空间，常指轻松地放入
senses.example: Slot the card into the reader and wait for the beep.
senses.exampleCN: 把卡插进读卡器，等提示音响起。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to give something its place inside the groove.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词：把某物放进它该在的凹槽里。

senses.title: To schedule or reserve
senses.definition: to arrange someone or something into a particular time or place
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某事安排进特定时间或位置
senses.example: Could you slot me in on Friday morning?
senses.exampleCN: 能把我安排到周五上午吗？
senses.why: To slot someone in is to drop them into the empty time slot on the timetable.
senses.whyCN: 把某人 slot in，就是把人放进时间表上那个空着的槽位。

senses.title: To classify
senses.definition: to place someone or something into a category or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物归入某一类别或模式
senses.example: The critic slotted the novel into the thriller tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家把这部小说归入惊悚小说的传统。
senses.why: Categorising is sorting objects into labelled grooves, which is the abstract form of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 分类就是把东西分进贴好标签的槽里，这是同一意象的抽象化形式。

intro.en: Slot comes through Old French esclot, the hollow between the ribs, and later hollowed surfaces of all kinds.
intro.cn: slot 经由古法语 esclot（肋骨间的凹陷）传入，后来泛指各种被挖空的表面。

items.en: Esclot means the hollow between the ribs or breast of a person or animal.
items.cn: esclot 指人或动物肋骨或胸前的凹陷。

items.en: Slot appears in English as a word for a hollow or depression.
items.cn: 十四世纪 slot 进入英语，指凹陷或窝。

items.en: Slot develops the sense of a narrow opening or groove in wood or metal.
items.cn: 十五世纪 slot 发展出「木头或金属上的狭缝、凹槽」之义。

items.en: With machines and vending, slot shifts to coin slots and slot machines.
items.cn: 随着机器和自动售卖的出现，slot 转向投币口和老虎机。

items.en: Broadcasting and offices give slot the abstract senses of time slot, job slot, and to slot in.
items.cn: 广播电视与办公场景赋予 slot「时段、岗位、安排插入」等抽象义。

note.en: Slot looks alike slit, slat, and sot, and is near in meaning to words for openings, periods, and free places.
note.cn: slot 与 slit、slat、sot 形近，意义上靠近表示开口、时间段和空位的词。

entries.definition: a long narrow cut
entries.definitionCN: 细长的切口；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a thin flat strip of wood or metal
entries.definitionCN: 板条；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a drunkard
entries.definitionCN: 醉鬼；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a long narrow cut in a surface
entries.definitionCN: 沟槽

entries.definition: a hole or gap in something
entries.definitionCN: 开口；缺口

entries.definition: an available job or room
entries.definitionCN: 空缺；空房

normalIntro.en: Slot is a groove cut to size, and its abstract senses all keep the idea of exactly one thing per groove.
normalIntro.cn: slot 是按尺寸开的槽，它的抽象义都保留着「一槽只放一物」的想法。

normal.en: A slot machine drops balls into slots, and the word became the name of the game.
normal.cn: 老虎机让球落进槽里，这个词于是成了游戏的名字。

normal.en: Time slot shows that hours can be cut into narrow openings too.
normal.cn: time slot 说明时间也能被切成一条条窄口。

normal.en: Slot in is to squeeze someone into the timetable like a card into a reader.
normal.cn: slot in 就是把某人像卡片一样塞进时间表的读卡器里。

normal.en: Slotting is a noun in retail, where slotting fee means money paid for shelf space.
normal.cn: slotting 在零售业中是名词，slotting fee 指为上架货架位置付的钱。

normal.en: Compare slot with hole: a hole can be round, a slot is always long and narrow.
normal.cn: 对比 hole：洞可以是圆的，而 slot 一定是狭长的。

abstract.en: Picture a key going into a groove that fits only its own shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙插进只有它这个形状才能进的槽。

abstract.en: Think of a timetable with little empty boxes, each holding one meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一张时间表上画着小空格，每格只放一场会议。

abstract.en: Imagine a coin sliding down a narrow rail into a tray.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币沿狭窄的滑道滑进托盘。

examples.en: Please put your boarding pass into the slot at the gate.
examples.cn: 请把登机牌放进登机口的插槽里。

examples.en: The radio station moved its news programme to a later slot.
examples.cn: 电台把新闻节目挪到了更晚的时段。

examples.en: The coach slotted the young player into the defence.
examples.cn: 教练把年轻球员安排进了后防线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死搂他」—— 硬币死命搂进那条缝里，槽口就是它的家；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esclot（肋骨间的凹陷）→ 中古英语 slot（凹陷；窝）→ slot（狭缝、凹槽）→ 引申为「时段、岗位、插入」；词根来源存疑，一般认为与古北欧语 slota 有松散关联。

sensesIntro.en: A long hollow is the base; the opening takes coins, periods, positions, and finally any place where something is fitted in.
sensesIntro.cn: 狭长的凹槽是基础；开口先是投币口，再变成时段、位置，最后成为一切「把东西放进去」的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a groove cut to the exact width of one thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：按一样东西的宽度开出的凹槽。

branches.en: Hollows in a surface and machine openings are the concrete senses.
branches.cn: 表面上的凹槽和机器上的口子是具体义项。

branches.en: A time slot cuts the day into reserved shapes.
branches.cn: 时段把一天切成预留好的形状。

branches.en: A place in a list and a job vacancy are reserved slots.
branches.cn: 名单里的位置和空缺岗位都是预留的槽位。

branches.en: The verb puts things inside grooves and timetables.
branches.cn: 动词形式把东西放进凹槽和时间表里。

branches.en: Sorting into categories is the most abstract groove.
branches.cn: 分类归入是最抽象的凹槽。

intro.en: Slot has only one syllable, and its English family grows with -ed, -ing, and -er: slotted, slotting, slotter.
intro.cn: slot 只有一个音节，英语词族靠 -ed、-ing 和 -er 扩展：slotted、slotting、slotter。

latinIntro.en: Slot arrived through Old French esclot from a Germanic source; there is no direct Latin ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: slot 经古法语 esclot 来自日耳曼语，没有直接的拉丁语祖词。

items.example: The slot accepts coins only.
items.exampleCN: 这个槽只收硬币。

items.example: Slot the tray back into place.
items.exampleCN: 把托盘放回原位。

items.example: Slotted screens are common on boxes.
items.exampleCN: 带槽的纸板箱很常见。

items.example: Slotting fees are paid to shops.
items.exampleCN: 上架费是付给商店的。

items.example: A slotter cuts grooves in metal.
items.exampleCN: 开槽机在金属上切槽。

items.example: The coin slot was taped shut.
items.exampleCN: 投币口被胶带封住了。

items.example: Book a time slot online.
items.exampleCN: 在网上预约一个时段。

items.example: She slotted in a quick call.
items.exampleCN: 她挤时间打了一个短电话。

items.example: The pieces slot into a clear pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这些碎片归入一个清晰的模式。

definition_zh: 懒惰；怠惰；树懒
definition_en: a dislike of work and effort, or the slow tree-dwelling animal of Central and South America
core_image: 一只树懒吊在树枝上，半晌才挪动一下爪子
scene: 复习周到了，室友却整天躺着刷手机，说忙了一学期总要歇一歇。With exams a week away, my roommate spent the whole day in bed, calling it a well-earned sloth.
sceneCN: 这里 sloth 是「懒惰」（第 1 个义项：不愿干活、不愿用力的习性）；句意：复习周到了，室友却整天躺着刷手机，说忙了一学期总要歇一歇。

pos.zh: 懒惰；怠惰；树懒（不可数，指习性时形式不变）

derivatives.zh: sloth 加形容词后缀 -ful，义为「懒惰的」，多用于书面
slothful 加 -ly，义为「懒散地」
slothful 加 -ness，义为「懒散」

senses.title: Habitual laziness
senses.definition: a strong unwillingness to work or make an effort
senses.definitionCN: 不愿工作、不愿用力气
senses.example: His sloth kept him in bed past noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他的懒惰让他在床上赖过了中午。
senses.why: The suffix -th turns the adjective slow into a noun for the state of being slow, and a slow person is a lazy one.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -th 把形容词 slow 变成表示「慢」这一状态的名词，而慢吞吞的人就是懒人。

senses.title: One of the deadly sins
senses.definition: in Christian teaching, the sin of neglect toward duty or of spiritual apathy
senses.definitionCN: 基督教教义中，对职责的怠慢或精神上的麻木
senses.example: Medieval monks feared sloth more than hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的修士害怕怠惰甚于饥饿。
senses.why: Once church writers took sloth as a moral failing, the everyday slowness became a sin with a name.
senses.whyCN: 当教会作家把慵懒视为道德过失之后，日常的慢吞吞就变成了有名有姓的罪。

senses.title: The slow tree animal
senses.definition: a slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal of Central and South America with long curved claws
senses.definitionCN: 中南美洲的长爪树栖哺乳动物，行动极慢
senses.example: A sloth can sleep for well over half the day.
senses.exampleCN: 树懒一天要睡一大半以上的时间。
senses.why: The animal was named for its slowness, so the abstract vice and the furry creature share one label.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物因慢而得名，抽象的恶习与毛茸茸的动物共用一个名字。

senses.title: Slow, idle movement
senses.definition: a literally slow and hesitant way of moving or behaving
senses.definitionCN: 字面意义上动作缓慢、拖沓的状态
senses.example: The meeting settled into an unproductive sloth.
senses.exampleCN: 会议陷入了毫无产出的拖沓。
senses.why: Because the word sums up slowness, any dragging, idle stretch of time can be called sloth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本就概括了「慢」，所以任何拖沓、空转的一段时间都可以叫 sloth。

senses.title: A group of the animals
senses.definition: a collective noun for a group of sloths
senses.definitionCN: 表示一群树懒的集合名词
senses.example: A sloth of sloths hung in the branches.
senses.exampleCN: 一群树懒挂在树枝上。
senses.why: English gives many animals group nouns, and the slow creature gets one that reuses its own name.
senses.whyCN: 英语给许多动物都有集合名词，这种慢吞吞的动物也得到了一个直接复用自己名字的群体量词。

intro.en: Sloth is Middle English slowth: slow plus the old suffix -th that also gives truth and warmth.
intro.cn: sloth 是中古英语 slowth：slow 加上古老的 -th 后缀，和 truth、warmth 同一种构词方式。

items.en: The adjective slaw means slow or inactive, with an abstract noun slæwþ meaning slothfulness.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 slaw 意为缓慢、不活跃，对应的抽象名词 slæwþ 意为懒惰。

items.en: The form slowth combines slow with the suffix -th to name the state of being slow.
items.cn: 中古英语中 slowth 由 slow 加后缀 -th 构成，指「慢」的状态。

items.en: Sloth takes on the moral sense of idleness and appears in lists of the deadly sins.
items.cn: sloth 取得「怠惰」的道德义，出现在七大罪的名单里。

items.en: Sloth is used for the slow-moving treedwelling animal of the Americas, filling a gap after the word ai was dropped.
items.cn: 十六世纪 sloth 被用来称呼美洲行动极慢的树栖动物，填补了 ai 一词弃用后的空缺。

items.en: Modern English keeps sloth for laziness, the deadly sin, and the animal, with the adjective slothful beside it.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 sloth 表示懒惰、七大罪之一以及树懒，并有形容词 slothful 相伴。

note.en: Sloth is the noun of slow, next to the -th family truth and warmth, and near in meaning to laziness, idleness, and lethargy.
note.cn: sloth 是 slow 的名词，与 -th 词族 truth、warmth 相邻，意义上靠近 laziness、idleness 与 lethargy。

entries.definition: not moving or working quickly
entries.definitionCN: 慢的；迟的

entries.definition: the quality of being true
entries.definitionCN: 真实；真相，与 sloth 共享 -th 抽象名词后缀

entries.definition: the quality of being warm
entries.definitionCN: 温暖，与 sloth 共享 -th 抽象名词后缀

entries.definition: the state of not wanting to work
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰

entries.definition: the state of doing nothing
entries.definitionCN: 闲散；无所事事

entries.definition: hard work and diligence
entries.definitionCN: 勤劳；勤奋，与 sloth 的懒惰义相反

normalIntro.en: Sloth is slow turned into a thing: the same -th that builds truth and warmth builds a word for being slow.
normalIntro.cn: sloth 是把 slow 变成的东西化名词：造出 truth 和 warmth 的那个 -th 也造出了「慢」。

normal.en: Slow plus -th gives sloth, a noun for the quality of being slow.
normal.cn: slow 加 -th 就是 sloth，表示「慢」这一性质的名词。

normal.en: Slothful is the adjective; a slothful afternoon is one wasted in bed.
normal.cn: slothful 是形容词，slothful 的下午就是浪费在床上度过。

normal.en: In church lists sloth sits among the seven deadly sins.
normal.cn: 在教会的名单里，sloth 坐落在七大罪之中。

normal.en: The animal got its name from the vice, which is why a slow tree animal is a sloth.
normal.cn: 这种动物因慢得像懒人而得名，所以行动缓慢的树栖动物就叫树懒。

normal.en: Compare sloth with slow: slow describes speed, sloth names the unwillingness that stays.
normal.cn: 对比 slow：slow 说的是速度，sloth 说的是那种持续不愿用力的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a furry animal hanging from a branch, one claw moving in an hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一只毛茸茸的动物挂在树枝上，一个钟头才动一下爪子。

abstract.en: Think of an alarm clock ringing for the fifth time while a hand switches it off again.
abstract.cn: 想象闹钟响了第五遍，一只手又把它按掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a desk with a closed book, a cold cup, and dust on the keyboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌上，书合着、茶杯凉了、键盘落了灰。

examples.en: Sloth is the enemy of every good plan.
examples.cn: 懒惰是一切好计划的敌人。

examples.en: The zookeeper explained that a sloth moves less than a few metres a day.
examples.cn: 饲养员解释说，树懒一天挪动不到几米。

examples.en: The poem blames sloth for the ruined garden.
examples.cn: 这首诗把荒废的花园归咎于懒惰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死懒」加个 th 的音—— 死懒到底，就是懒到极点；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 slaw（缓慢的）→ 中古英语 slæwþ／slowth（缓慢；懒惰）→ sloth（懒惰）→ 引申为「怠惰之罪」→ 十六世纪起指行动极慢的树懒；核心是 slow 加 -th。

sensesIntro.en: Slow turned into a noun gives sloth: a quality, then a sin, then a slow animal, then an idle mood and a group word.
sensesIntro.cn: slow 名词化后成为 sloth：先是一种性质，然后是一种罪，再是一种慢动物，最后是拖沓的状态和群体量词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a creature hanging from a branch that takes an hour to move one claw.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只挂在树枝上的动物，一个钟头才挪动一下爪子。

branches.en: Habitual laziness is the main everyday sense.
branches.cn: 习惯性的懒惰是日常主要义项。

branches.en: Church teaching lifts laziness into a named sin.
branches.cn: 教会教义让懒惰升格为一种有名字的罪。

branches.en: The animal borrows the name of the vice.
branches.cn: 动物借用了这一恶习的名字。

branches.en: Any dragging, idle stretch of time is called sloth.
branches.cn: 任何拖沓空转的一段时间都可以称作 sloth。

branches.en: The collective noun keeps the animal sense alive in field guides.
branches.cn: 群体量词让动物义在野外图鉴中延续。

intro.en: Sloth is a Germanic abstract noun: slow plus -th, with slothful, slothfully, and slothfulness built on the same stem.
intro.cn: sloth 是日耳曼语系的抽象名词：slow 加 -th 构成，slothful、slothfully、slothfulness 建在同一词干上。

latinIntro.en: Sloth has no Latin ancestor; its oldest form slæwþ is native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: sloth 没有拉丁语祖词，最古老的形式 slæwþ 是本土古英语词。

items.example: Sloth ruled the whole household.
items.exampleCN: 懒散支配着这整个家。

items.example: The suffix -th turns slow into sloth.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -th 把 slow 变成 sloth。

items.example: Truth shares the -th ending.
items.exampleCN: truth 共享 -th 词尾。

items.example: Warmth shows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: warmth 显示同样的构词方式。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms slothful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 slothful。

items.example: A slothful week passed quickly.
items.exampleCN: 懒散的一周很快就过去了。

items.example: Slothfully describes how someone acts.
items.exampleCN: slothfully 描述一个人做事的方式。

items.example: Slothfulness names the state.
items.exampleCN: slothfulness 指这种状态。

items.meaning: a shaggy bear of South Asia
items.example: The sloth bear eats termites.
items.exampleCN: 懒熊吃白蚁。

definition_zh: 懒惰的；疏懒的；懒散的；行动迟缓的
definition_en: lazy and unwilling to work or make any effort
core_image: 一只树懒挂在树上一整天，伸出的前爪懒得再动一下
scene: 小组作业交了半截报告，负责人只说下周再说，另两个人干脆交了空白页。With such a slothful team, even a simple report was never finished on time.
sceneCN: 这里 slothful 是「懒散的、不愿花力气」（第 1 个义项：不愿做事）；句意：碰上这样一支懒散的队伍，连一份简单的报告都没能按时完成。

pos.zh: 懒惰的；疏懒的；懒散的；行动迟缓的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「懒散地」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「懒惰；懒散」
基础名词，义为「懒惰；树懒」，也是 slothful 的词干

senses.title: Unwilling to work
senses.definition: lazy and unwilling to do the work that should be done
senses.definitionCN: 懒散、不愿做分内之事的
senses.example: The slothful clerk left the paperwork for others to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 那个懒散的职员把文书工作留给别人去完成。
senses.why: Sloth is a deadly sin in old English, and the adjective keeps that moral weight: someone slothful simply declines to work.
senses.whyCN: sloth 在古英语传统里是七宗罪之一，形容词保留了这种道德色彩，所以 slothful 的人是主动不肯干活。

senses.title: Habitually inactive
senses.definition: describing a person who is used to being idle and takes little exercise
senses.definitionCN: 形容习惯于闲散、很少活动的人
senses.example: Years of desk work had made him slothful and overweight.
senses.exampleCN: 多年坐办公室让他变得懒散而超重。
senses.why: The animal sloth hangs still for most of the day, so the adjective can describe a whole way of life rather than one lazy act.
senses.whyCN: 树懒一天大部分时间挂着不动，所以这个形容词不只指一次偷懒，还能形容一整套闲散的生活方式。

senses.title: Slow to act or think
senses.definition: slow to respond, to speak, or to use the mind
senses.definitionCN: 反应、说话或思考迟缓的
senses.example: A slothful mind never asks the second question.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗懒于思考的头脑从不追问第二个问题。
senses.why: The delay is first bodily; by extension it moves inside, where thinking itself becomes sluggish.
senses.whyCN: 迟缓原本是身体的，再往下引申就进入头脑，于是连思考本身也变得迟钝。

senses.title: Neglected through idleness
senses.definition: used of a field, garden, or duty left untended out of laziness
senses.definitionCN: 形容田地、园子或职责因懒惰而无人照管
senses.example: The garden grew slothful under the weeds.
senses.exampleCN: 园子在杂草丛生中荒废了。
senses.why: The adjective can be transferred from the person to whatever the person has failed to care for.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从人身上移到人没照顾好事物上，于是园子、田地也会变得 slothful。

senses.title: Lazy in spirit
senses.definition: failing to make an effort in religion, art, or study out of lack of care
senses.definitionCN: 在信仰、艺术或学业上因为不上心而不肯努力
senses.example: His slothful prayers were repeated, not felt.
senses.exampleCN: 他的祈祷只是口头重复，心里并未投入。
senses.why: Old religious writing treats sloth as a disease of the soul, and the adjective carries that sense into modern talk about spirit and effort.
senses.whyCN: 古代宗教文献把 sloth 看成灵魂的病症，形容词把这个意义带进现代关于精神与努力的说法。

senses.title: Acerbic for lazy
senses.definition: used in a sharper or slightly comic way in place of lazy
senses.definitionCN: 比 lazy 更带挖苦意味或一点戏谑的用法
senses.example: The paper called the council slothful and wasteful.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸称该地方议会懒惰又浪费。
senses.why: Because the word comes from a moral sin, slothful sounds sharper and more judgemental than the ordinary lazy.
senses.whyCN: 因为词源带着「罪」的分量，slothful 听起来比普通的 lazy 更尖刻、更爱下判断。

intro.en: Slothful is sloth plus the suffix -ful; sloth itself is the noun of the adjective slow, a Germanic word for sluggish.
intro.cn: slothful 是 sloth 加后缀 -ful 构成；sloth 本身是形容词 slow 的名词，slow 是表示迟钝的日耳曼语词。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to slide or slip lies behind the Germanic family of slow.
items.cn: 一般认为，表示滑或溜走的重构词根是 slow 一族日耳曼词的源头，具体形式仍有争议。

items.en: Slaw means slow or sluggish, and the noun slæwð names slowness of mind.
items.cn: 古英语 slaw 意为缓慢、迟钝，名词 slæwð 指心思迟钝。

items.en: The noun settles as slouthe, later sloth, and names laziness as a sin.
items.cn: 名词定形为 slouthe，后来成为 sloth，用作七宗罪之一的名字。

items.en: The animal of Central and South America takes the name sloth because it moves so little.
items.cn: 中美洲与南美洲那种行动极少的动物被命名为 sloth，正是因为它动得太少。

items.en: Slothful forms from sloth with -ful and replaces older words for lazy in written English.
items.cn: slothful 由 sloth 加 -ful 构成，在书面英语中逐渐取代更老的「懒」的说法。

note.en: Slothful belongs to the sloth family and sits beside ordinary words for lazy and idle people.
note.cn: slothful 属于 sloth 词族，与表示懒、闲的常见词相邻。

entries.definition: laziness, or a slow tree dwelling animal
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰；树懒

entries.definition: in a lazy way
entries.definitionCN: 懒散地

entries.definition: the quality of being lazy
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰；懒散

entries.definition: moving without much speed
entries.definitionCN: 慢的；迟缓的；与 sloth 同源

entries.definition: unwilling to work and preferring to rest
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰的；不愿干活的；最日常的说法

entries.definition: habitually lazy but without the sharp moral edge
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰的；懒得动但语气比 slothful 温和

entries.definition: not working or not in use
entries.definitionCN: 空闲的；闲着的；强调没在做事

normalIntro.en: Slothful is sloth made into an adjective: the still animal, the deadly sin, both in one word.
normalIntro.cn: slothful 就是把 sloth 变成形容词：安静不动的动物、七宗罪里的懒惰，合成一个词。

normal.en: Sloth plus -ful means full of sloth, just as hopeful is full of hope.
normal.cn: sloth 加 -ful 表示满是懒惰，就像 hopeful 表示满是希望。

normal.en: The animal sloth was named after the sin, not the other way round.
normal.cn: 树懒的名字取自「懒惰」这个罪，而不是倒过来。

normal.en: Slow and sloth share a root, and a slothful person is literally slow to start.
normal.cn: slow 与 sloth 同源，slothful 的人就是开始得很慢的人。

normal.en: Use a slothful worker or slothful habits when the laziness is a routine rather than a moment.
normal.cn: 用 a slothful worker 或 slothful habits 指长期的懒，而不是一时偷懒。

normal.en: Compare lazy: lazy is neutral and everyday, while slothful carries the old moral judgement.
normal.cn: 对比 lazy：lazy 中性而日常，slothful 带着古老的道德评判。

abstract.en: Picture a uniform on a hook and the owner stretched on a bench all morning.
abstract.cn: 想象制服挂在钩子上，主人整个上午摊在长椅上。

abstract.en: See an unmade bed and three unwashed cups as a weekly routine.
abstract.cn: 想象没叠的床和三只没洗的杯子，每周都是这样。

abstract.en: Imagine a brain with its gears covered in dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗齿轮落满灰尘的脑子。

examples.en: He was too slothful to walk to the corner shop.
examples.cn: 他懒得连街角小店都不肯走去。

examples.en: The essay criticises a slothful government that postpones every reform.
examples.cn: 这篇文章批评一个懈怠的政府，把每项改革都往后拖。

examples.en: Their slothful habits cost the club a place in the final.
examples.cn: 他们懒散的习惯让俱乐部丢掉了决赛名额。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死了服了」——一进被窝「死了」一样不动，还「服了」自己这份懒；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 slaw（缓慢的）→ 名词 slæwð 与中古英语 slouthe → sloth（懒惰；树懒）→ sloth + -ful → slothful；核心义「不肯动、不肯努力」。

sensesIntro.en: Slothful begins as the adjective of a moral sin, then spreads to a whole idle way of life, to slow thinking, and to whatever idleness ruins.
sensesIntro.cn: slothful 先是一个道德之罪的形容词，再延伸到整套闲散的生活方式、迟钝的思考，以及因懒而荒废的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sloth hanging from a branch, not moving for a whole day.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只树懒挂在树枝上，一整天都不动一下。

branches.en: Refusing the work that should be done is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 拒绝做本该做的事，是最古老的义项。

branches.en: A settled idle life turns the adjective into a description of character.
branches.cn: 长期的闲散生活让这个形容词成为性格描写。

branches.en: Bodily stillness passes inward and makes the mind slow.
branches.cn: 身体的静止转向内部，使头脑迟钝。

branches.en: What a lazy person neglects becomes slothful in turn.
branches.cn: 懒人不管的东西，最后也带上了懒的印记。

branches.en: The religious sense gives the word its sharp, judging tone in modern use.
branches.cn: 宗教义项赋予它今天那副尖锐、爱评判的语气。

intro.en: Slothful is a Germanic word built on sloth, with -ful and -ly and -ness making the usual family.
intro.cn: slothful 是以 sloth 为词干的日耳曼语词，配 -ful、-ly 与 -ness 组成常见词族。

latinIntro.en: Slothful has no Latin ancestor; its root is the Old English adjective slaw.
latinIntro.cn: slothful 没有拉丁语祖先，词根是古英语形容词 slaw。

items.example: Sloth is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sloth 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ful turns sloth into slothful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 把 sloth 变成 slothful。

items.example: Slothful describes a person who will not work.
items.exampleCN: slothful 形容不肯干活的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms slothfully.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 slothfully。

items.example: Slothfully describes how an action is done.
items.exampleCN: slothfully 描述动作的方式。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms slothfulness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 slothfulness。

items.example: Slothfulness names the habit itself.
items.exampleCN: slothfulness 指这种习惯本身。

items.example: Slow is the close relative of sloth.
items.exampleCN: slow 是 sloth 的近亲。

items.meaning: a slow animal of the tropical forests
items.example: Sloth also names a slow climbing animal.
items.exampleCN: sloth 也指一种行动缓慢的动物。

definition_zh: 没精打采地坐或站；耷拉；无精打采的样子；懒散的人
definition_en: to sit or stand with the shoulders and head bent forward in a loose, lazy way
core_image: 坐在沙发上，肩膀垮下去，脑袋往前垂，整个人像泄了气的布偶
scene: 面试官走进来，候选人却靠着椅背、肩膀垮着，下巴几乎碰到胸口。He sat in a permanent slouch through the whole interview, which did not help his chances.
sceneCN: 这里 slouch 是「没精打采地坐」（第 1 个义项：塌肩驼背地坐或站）；句意：他整场面试都塌着肩膀，这对他很不利。

pos.zh: 没精打采地坐；无精打采地走；耷拉着
无精打采的姿势；懒散的人

collocations.zh: 不是笨手笨脚的人；相当能干

derivatives.zh: 加 -y 构成，义为「松松垮垮的；无精打采的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「弯腰驼背的」
加 -er 构成，义为「弯腰驼背的人」

senses.title: To sit with a bent back
senses.definition: to sit or stand with the body bent forward and the shoulders dropped, in a loose way
senses.definitionCN: 身体前倾、肩膀下沉、松松垮垮地坐着或站着
senses.example: Please do not slouch in your chair during the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试时请不要瘫坐在椅子上。
senses.why: The word seems to copy the shape of a heavy, sagging body, and this bent posture is the picture at the centre of every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词像是在模仿沉重身体往下塌的形状，这种驼背姿势就是其他所有义项的中心画面。

senses.title: To walk or stand heavily
senses.definition: to move or stand with the head down and the body loose, as if tired or discouraged
senses.definitionCN: 低着头、身体松垮地走或站，像是累了或很泄气
senses.example: He slouched out of the room after the bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到坏消息后，他垂着头走出了房间。
senses.why: A person who has lost energy lets the shoulders fall, so sagging posture becomes a way of walking as well.
senses.whyCN: 精力一失，肩膀就落下来，于是垮着的姿势也变成一种走路的样子。

senses.title: To hang down loosely
senses.definition: used of a hat brim, a coat, or a piece of cloth hanging down in a heavy, loose way
senses.definitionCN: 形容帽檐、外套或布片沉甸甸地松垂下来
senses.example: A wide brim slouched low over her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 一顶宽帽檐低低地压在她眼睛上方。
senses.why: When a thing cannot hold its shape, it sags just as a tired body does, so the word moves from people to clothes.
senses.whyCN: 东西撑不住形状就会往下坠，和累了的身体一样，于是这个词从人身上移到了衣物上。

senses.title: The lazy posture
senses.definition: a posture of dropped shoulders and a bent back, used like a short description of laziness
senses.definitionCN: 肩膀下沉、背部弯曲的姿势，常被当作懒惰的代名词
senses.example: She stood with a slight slouch that annoyed her teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她微微塌着肩站着，让老师很不满。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun naming the posture itself, so a single slouch can stand for how a person carries himself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词，指的就是这个姿势本身，于是一个 slouch 就能代表一个人的站相坐相。

senses.title: A lazy person
senses.definition: a slow, idle, and untidy person, mostly used in older or humorous English
senses.definitionCN: 迟缓、懒散而邋遢的人，多用于较老或带点戏谑的英语
senses.example: The manager called him a slouch for missing three shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 他缺了三次班，被经理叫作懒虫。
senses.why: From the posture, English shifts the word onto the person who walks about in that slack shape.
senses.whyCN: 从姿势出发，英语把词义移到总以这种松垮样子走路的人身上。

senses.title: No slouch, meaning capable
senses.definition: in the phrase be no slouch, used to say that someone is in fact very good at something
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定说法 be no slouch，表示某人其实相当在行
senses.example: She is no slouch at mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 她在数学上可是把好手。
senses.why: Saying someone is no slouch denies the lazy image, so the phrase works as a modest way of praising skill.
senses.whyCN: 说某人不是 slouch，就是否掉了「懒」的印象，于是这个短语成了一种含蓄的夸奖。
