senses.title: A drooping hat
senses.definition: used of a hat, especially a slouch hat, whose brim and crown hang soft and loose
senses.definitionCN: 形容帽檐与帽顶松软下垂的帽子，尤指软边宽檐帽
senses.example: The soldier folded his slouch hat under his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵把软边帽夹在胳膊下。
senses.why: Military English kept the hanging sense in the name of a soft felt hat worn by colonial troops.
senses.whyCN: 军事英语把这个「下垂」义保留在殖民地部队所戴软呢帽的名字里。

intro.en: Slouch is thought to come from Old Norse, where slokr names a lazy fellow; it is not related to slightly similar words like slow.
intro.cn: 一般认为 slouch 来自古诺斯语，slokr 指懒汉；它与发音相近的 slow 并不同源。

items.en: Slokr means a lazy and untidy fellow, and nearby forms describe hanging down loosely.
items.cn: slokr 意为懒散邋遢的家伙，相邻的词形则表示松散地垂挂。

items.en: The word enters northern English, where it describes a person who moves in a heavy, lazy way.
items.cn: 这个词进入英格兰北部，用来形容动作沉重、懒散的人。

items.en: Slouch beats slouchy and similar spellings and starts to name the bent posture itself.
items.cn: slouch 在拼写上胜过 slouchy 等写法，开始指驼背的姿势本身。

items.en: A slouch hat names the soft felt hat with a hanging brim, connected with colonial and military dress.
items.cn: slouch hat 指帽檐下垂的软呢帽，与殖民地与军队服饰有关。

items.en: Modern English uses slouch for posture, for lazy movement, and in the phrase no slouch for praise.
items.cn: 现代英语用 slouch 表示姿势、懒散的动作，并用 no slouch 表示称赞。

note.en: Slouch is a posture word that drifted into lazy behaviour; its family and neighbours show both.
note.cn: slouch 本是姿势词，后来滑向懒散的行为；它的词族与近邻两头都有。

entries.definitionCN: slouch 的三单与复数形式

entries.definition: sat or walked with a bent back
entries.definitionCN: 驼着背坐过或走过

entries.definition: bending the shoulders forward
entries.definitionCN: 弯腰塌肩的

entries.definition: loose, shapeless, and tending to sag
entries.definitionCN: 松垮的；无型的

entries.definition: to bend the head and shoulders forward
entries.definitionCN: 低头弯腰；强调身体向前的弯度

entries.definition: to raise and round the shoulders, often from cold or worry
entries.definitionCN: 弓起背；耸肩缩颈

entries.definition: to stand or sit in a relaxed and careless way
entries.definitionCN: 懒洋洋地倚靠；闲荡

normalIntro.en: Slouch is the body giving up its shape: shoulders down, head forward, clothes hanging loose.
normalIntro.cn: slouch 就是身体放弃了自己的形状：肩往下、头往前、衣物松松垂着。

normal.en: The ending -ch in slouch matches couch, and you slouch on a couch.
normal.cn: slouch 结尾的 -ch 让人想到 couch，而人正是在沙发的 couch 上 slouch。

normal.en: The past tense slouched and the plural slouches both keep the ch sound.
normal.cn: 过去式 slouched 与复数 slouches 都保留了末尾的 ch 音。

normal.en: Be no slouch is a double negative style compliment: not a lazy person, so a capable one.
normal.cn: be no slouch 是绕个弯的夸奖：不是懒人，也就是能干的人。

normal.en: The adjective slouchy describes loose, shapeless clothes as well as lazy bodies.
normal.cn: 形容词 slouchy 既形容松垮无型的衣服，也形容懒散的身体。

normal.en: Compare stoop: stoop is the forward bend, slouch adds the slack, lazy shoulders.
normal.cn: 对比 stoop：stoop 只是向前弯，slouch 还多了松垮、懒得撑起来的肩膀。

abstract.en: Picture a puppet on strings after the strings go slack.
abstract.cn: 想象提线木偶的线一松，整个人就往下塌。

abstract.en: See a backpack that has lost its stiff frame and folds in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没了硬支架的背包，从中间折下去。

abstract.en: Imagine a shirt that could not hold its shape and sags on the hanger.
abstract.cn: 想象一件撑不起形状的衬衫，软软地挂在衣架上。

examples.en: Students often slouch when they are bored.
examples.cn: 学生无聊时常常瘫坐在椅子上。

examples.en: A slouch is easier to fix than a bad habit of skipping work.
examples.cn: 驼背的坐姿比逃避工作的坏习惯更容易改。

examples.en: The coach is no slouch at reading a game.
examples.cn: 这位教练在阅读比赛方面可是把好手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死搂着」——死搂着沙发不起来，肩膀一垮就成了 slouch；这里的「死搂着」只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自古诺斯语 slokr（懒汉）及其表示「松散垂挂」的相关词形 → 中古英语北部方言 slouch → 现代英语 slouch；核心义「身体松垮下塌」。

sensesIntro.en: Slouch starts as a bent, slack posture, moves to lazy walking and drooping clothes, and finally names the posture, the lazy person, and even a soft hat.
sensesIntro.cn: slouch 先是松垮弯曲的姿势，再指懒散的走法、下垂的衣物，最后指这种姿势本身、懒散的人，乃至一种软边帽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoulders dropping forward like a puppet whose strings have gone slack.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩膀往前塌，像提线一松的木偶。

branches.en: The bent sitting posture is the root picture.
branches.cn: 弯腰的坐姿是根源画面。

branches.en: The same slack body carries itself when it walks.
branches.cn: 同一副松垮的身体走起路来仍是那个样子。

branches.en: Clothes and hat brims droop the way a tired body does.
branches.cn: 衣物与帽檐下垂的样子，正如疲惫的身体。

branches.en: The posture becomes a noun and then the person who owns it.
branches.cn: 姿势先变成名词，再指拥有这副姿势的人。

branches.en: A negation of the lazy image becomes praise, while the hanging sense survives in the hat.
branches.cn: 对「懒」的否认变成夸奖，而「下垂」义则活在软边帽里。

intro.en: Slouch is a short Norse loan that grew a small family: slouches, slouched, slouching, slouchy, and sloucher.
intro.cn: slouch 是一个短小的诺斯语借词，却长出了一个词族：slouches、slouched、slouching、slouchy 与 sloucher。

latinIntro.en: Slouch has no Latin source; it comes from Old Norse and is unrelated to Latin based slow.
latinIntro.cn: slouch 没有拉丁语来源，出自古诺斯语，与源自拉丁语的 slow 无关。

items.meaning: to sit or stand with a bent back
items.example: Slouch is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: slouch 是这个词族的基础。

items.meaning: third person singular and plural marker
items.example: The suffix -es forms slouches.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 构成 slouches。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms slouched.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 slouched。

items.example: Slouching works as an adjective too.
items.exampleCN: slouching 也可以作形容词。

items.example: The suffix -y forms slouchy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 slouchy。

items.example: Slouchy describes loose clothes and lazy bodies.
items.exampleCN: slouchy 形容松垮的衣物与懒散的身体。

items.example: The suffix -er forms sloucher.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 sloucher。

items.example: Sloucher names the person.
items.exampleCN: sloucher 指这样的人。

items.example: No in no slouch turns the word into praise.
items.exampleCN: no slouch 中的 no 让这个词变成夸奖。

definition_zh: 邋遢的；不修边幅的；马虎草率的
definition_en: untidy in dress or appearance, and careless in ordinary actions
core_image: 衬衫没扣好、头发乱翘的人站在满地杂物的房间里
scene: 合租的室友把脏碗堆到水槽外，衣服散在沙发上，垃圾袋一直没扔。The students were told that slovenly rooms would cost them their deposit.
sceneCN: 这里 slovenly 是「邋遢的、不整洁的」（第 1 个义项：外表或居所不整洁）；句意：学生们被告知，邋遢的房间会让押金被扣掉。

pos.zh: 邋遢的；不修边幅的；马虎草率的
邋遢地；马虎地

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「邋遢；草率」
基础名词，义为「邋遢的人」，也是 slovenly 的词干
疑似同族词，义为「泔水、剩汤」，保留着「脏而乱」的古义

senses.title: Untidy in appearance
senses.definition: careless and untidy about dress, hair, and personal cleanliness
senses.definitionCN: 穿着、头发与个人卫生上随意而不整洁的
senses.example: He arrived in a slovenly jacket that had not been brushed for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着件几周没刷过的外套来了，邋里邋遢。
senses.why: Slovenly comes from sloven, a person who is untidy, and the adjective keeps that picture of a person who will not tidy himself.
senses.whyCN: slovenly 来自名词 sloven（邋遢的人），形容词保留了这个画面：一个不肯把自己收拾利落的人。

senses.title: Careless and untidy in work
senses.definition: done without care, order, or neatness
senses.definitionCN: 做得不仔细、没有条理、不整洁的
senses.example: The notes were slovenly, full of crossed out lines.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记写得潦草，到处是划掉的字迹。
senses.why: If a person is slovenly at home, the same looseness appears in what the person makes, so the word moves from the body to the work.
senses.whyCN: 一个人在家里邋遢，他做出来的东西也一样松散，于是这个词从身体移到了工作成果上。

senses.title: Untidy in language or thought
senses.definition: used of speech, writing, or argument that is loose and badly organised
senses.definitionCN: 形容言辞、写作或论证松散、缺乏组织
senses.example: She refused to accept such slovenly reasoning.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒绝接受这么混乱的论证。
senses.why: Mill mentions the word exactly for this: he admits hasty, slovenly speech as the price of freedom of thought.
senses.whyCN: 密尔正是这样用这个词的：他把仓促、草率的言说当作思想自由的代价。

senses.title: Of a place left messy
senses.definition: describing a room, kitchen, or street that is dirty and disorderly
senses.definitionCN: 形容房间、厨房或街道又脏又乱
senses.example: The kitchen was slovenly, with unwashed pans on every surface.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房乱糟糟的，每个台面上都有没洗的锅。
senses.why: The adjective spreads from the person to the space the person has failed to keep.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从人身上扩展到人没能保持整洁的空间。

senses.title: In a careless manner
senses.definition: the adverb use: done in an untidy or careless way
senses.definitionCN: 副词用法：以不整洁或粗心的方式
senses.example: The report was slovenly written but the data were sound.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告写得潦草，但数据是可靠的。
senses.why: Because the same form serves as an adverb, English can describe the manner of an action as easily as the person.
senses.whyCN: 由于同一个词形也作副词，英语既能形容人，也能描述做事的方式。

senses.title: Sloppy, the everyday word
senses.definition: often replaced in speech by sloppy, which is milder and more common
senses.definitionCN: 口语中常被更温和、更常用的 sloppy 替代
senses.example: His slovenly, slipshod habits annoyed the whole lab.
senses.exampleCN: 他那种马虎草率的习惯让整个实验室都不满。
senses.why: Slovenly keeps an older, sharper judgement, so speakers who want to sound milder switch to sloppy for the same picture.
senses.whyCN: slovenly 保留着更老、更尖锐的评判，想说得温和些的人会用 sloppy 来指同一个画面。

intro.en: Slovenly is sloven plus -ly; sloven is a person who is lazy and dirty. Scholars often link it to slop, but the older source is uncertain, and it is not related to slave or to sloth.
intro.cn: slovenly 是 sloven 加 -ly 构成；sloven 指又懒又脏的人。学者常把它与 slop 联系起来，但更早的来源存疑，且与 slave、sloth 都不同源。

items.en: The earlier source of sloven is disputed; many scholars relate it to slop, words for liquid waste or a splashing mess, but no link is certain.
items.cn: sloven 的更早来源存疑；不少学者把它与 slop（泔水、泼洒的脏东西）一类词联系起来，但并无确证。

items.en: Sloven is recorded in the fifteenth century as a name for a lazy, dirty, and untidy person, often in moral writing.
items.cn: sloven 在十五世纪已有记载，指懒惰、肮脏、不整洁的人，多见于道德文本。

items.en: The adjective slovenly is attested in the sixteenth century and at first describes the manners of a sloven.
items.cn: 形容词 slovenly 于十六世纪见诸文字，最初形容一个 sloven 的做派。

items.en: The word widens from the person to work, writing, reasoning, and places.
items.cn: 这个词从人扩展到工作、写作、论证与场所。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective and the adverb, both rather formal and slightly old fashioned.
items.cn: 现代英语保留它的形容词与副词用法，两者都偏正式，也略有点老派。

note.en: Slovenly is the -ly adjective of sloven, standing beside the sloppy and untidy words of everyday English.
note.cn: slovenly 是 sloven 加 -ly 构成的形容词，与日常英语里的 sloppy、untidy 一类词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who is lazy and untidy
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰邋遢的人

entries.definition: the state of being untidy
entries.definitionCN: 邋遢；草率

entries.definition: lazy, with no sense of being dirty
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰的；与 slovenly 开头相近但词源不同，且不强调脏乱

entries.definition: not arranged neatly
entries.definitionCN: 不整洁的；最中性的说法

entries.definition: dirty and in disorder
entries.definitionCN: 凌乱的；乱糟糟的

entries.definition: not taking enough care
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的；只强调不在乎，不涉及整洁

entries.definition: with hair and clothes in disorder
entries.definitionCN: 衣衫不整、头发凌乱的

normalIntro.en: Slovenly is sloven made into an adjective: a person who will not tidy himself, and the things he leaves behind.
normalIntro.cn: slovenly 就是把 sloven 变成形容词：不肯把自己收拾利落的人，以及他留下的一团乱。

normal.en: The stem is sloven, and the -ly makes it a description of style rather than a person.
normal.cn: 词干是 sloven，加上 -ly 就变成对风格的描述，而不直指某个人。

normal.en: The noun is slovenliness, the adjective is slovenly, and the same adjective form also serves directly as an adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 slovenliness，形容词是 slovenly；同一个形容词形式还能直接当副词用。

normal.en: The word does not mean sleepy: it combines untidiness with carelessness, not tiredness.
normal.cn: 这个词并不表示困倦：它把「不整洁」和「粗心」合在一起，并不表示疲劳。

normal.en: It has no link with slave or sloth, even though the letters are close; its likeliest relative is slop.
normal.cn: 虽然字母很像，它与 slave 和 sloth 都没有词源关系，最可能的近亲是 slop。

normal.en: Compare untidy: untidy is neutral, slovenly adds judgement about the person behind the mess.
normal.cn: 对比 untidy：untidy 中性，slovenly 还对造成乱象的人下判断。

abstract.en: Picture a shirt with the buttons done up the wrong way.
abstract.cn: 想象一件扣子扣错了位置的衬衫。

abstract.en: See papers sliding off a desk into a pile on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象文件从桌上滑下去，在地板上堆成一摞。

abstract.en: Imagine a lecture full of half finished sentences that never add up.
abstract.cn: 想象一场满是半截话、怎么也对不上的讲座。

examples.en: His slovenly room was a warning to every flatmate.
examples.cn: 他邋遢的房间对每个室友都是一个警告。

examples.en: The agency blamed slovenly work for the delay.
examples.cn: 机构把延误归咎于马虎粗糙的工作。

examples.en: She thought it unfair to judge a scholar for slovenly shoes.
examples.cn: 她觉得仅凭一双邋遢的鞋来评判一位学者并不公平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死滥了」——衣服脏乱「死滥了」，东西摊了一地；这里的「死滥了」只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源存疑的中古英语名词 sloven（懒散邋遢的人），一般认为与 slop（泔水、泼洒）一类词同源 + 形容词词尾 -ly → slovenly；核心义「不收拾、不讲究」。

sensesIntro.en: Slovenly begins with the untidy person, then passes to the work, the language, and the place that person leaves loose and messy.
sensesIntro.cn: slovenly 始于不整洁的人，再传递到这个人留下的松散马虎的工作、语言与场所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbuttoned person in a cluttered room.
core.cn: 核心意象：钮扣没扣好的人，站在堆满杂物的房间里。

branches.en: The untidy body and dress are the origin of the image.
branches.cn: 不整洁的身体与穿着是意象的起点。

branches.en: A careless person produces careless work.
branches.cn: 粗心的人做出的活儿也粗心。

branches.en: The loosest thing of all can be an argument that will not hold together.
branches.cn: 最松散的东西，可以是一段组织不起来的论证。

branches.en: The room is a mirror of the person who never tidied.
branches.cn: 房间是从不收拾之人的镜子。

branches.en: The adverb marks careless actions, while sloppy takes over the milder everyday sense.
branches.cn: 副词标记马虎的动作，而更温和的日常义则由 sloppy 承担。

intro.en: Slovenly is built on the noun sloven, with -ness making slovenliness; slop and sloppy are close relatives.
intro.cn: slovenly 以名词 sloven 为词干，加 -ness 得 slovenliness；slop 与 sloppy 是它的近亲。

latinIntro.en: Slovenly has no Latin ancestor; sloven appears in Middle English and is probably related to slop.
latinIntro.cn: slovenly 没有拉丁语祖先；sloven 见于中古英语，一般认为与 slop 有关。

items.exampleCN: sloven 是这个词族的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns sloven into slovenly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 sloven 变成 slovenly。

items.example: Slovenly describes the untidy person.

items.exampleCN: slovenliness 指这种习惯。

items.example: The same form also works as an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 同一词形也作副词。

items.example: Slop is a likely relative of sloven.
items.exampleCN: slop 是 sloven 可能的近亲。

items.example: The verb slop shares the dirty, disorderly image.
items.exampleCN: 动词 slop 共享「脏而乱」的意象。

items.example: Slops keeps the oldest everyday form.
items.exampleCN: slops 保留了最古老的日常形式。

items.example: Sloppy is the milder everyday cousin.
items.exampleCN: sloppy 是更温和的日常近亲。

definition_zh: 贫民窟；简陋破旧的住房；极度脏乱拥挤的处境；过穷日子；屈尊下就
definition_en: a crowded and run-down part of a city where poor people live, or an extremely dirty and disordered place
core_image: 城市边缘一片歪斜拥挤的低矮屋棚，雨水从破屋顶滴下
scene: 城市边缘的坡地上，铁皮屋顶挨着铁皮屋顶，晾衣绳把小巷割成细条。Families in the slum still carry water up six flights of stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 slum 是「贫民窟」（第 1 个义项：城市中贫穷拥挤、房屋破败的居住区）；句意：贫民窟里的家庭仍要把水拎上六层楼。画面里能辨认的物件有铁皮屋顶、晾衣绳和湿漉漉的水桶。

pos.zh: 名词：贫民窟；简陋破旧的住房；极度脏乱拥挤的处境
动词：过穷日子；屈尊去寒酸的地方；使显得寒酸

collocations.zh: 贫民窟式住房；破旧住房
（口语）将就过穷日子；住简陋地方

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「贫民窟的；破旧脏乱的」
由本词加 like「像……一样」构成，义为「像贫民窟的」
形近误认词：义为「睡眠」，来自另一词根；与贫民窟义毫无关系，只提醒别拼混

senses.title: A poor crowded district
senses.definition: a thickly populated, run-down neighborhood of a city, with poor housing and few services
senses.definitionCN: 城市中人口稠密、房屋破败、公共设施匮乏的穷困住区
senses.example: The children were raised in a slum beside the old canal.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孩子是在老运河边的贫民窟里长大的。
senses.why: The word is first recorded in the early nineteenth century, apparently from a slang word for a room; the core image is a dense cluster of cramped dwellings, not a clean grid of streets.
senses.whyCN: 这个词十九世纪初才见于文字，一般认为来自指「房间」的俚语，所以核心意象是一簇簇拥挤狭小的住处，而不是整齐的街道。

senses.title: A badly maintained house
senses.definition: a single dwelling that is dirty, cramped, and in a dilapidated condition
senses.definitionCN: 一间脏乱、狭窄、破败失修的房子
senses.example: Their flat was a slum, with one tap for the whole floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们那套公寓破败不堪，整层楼只有一只水龙头。
senses.why: Before the word named a district, it could name one bad room or building, so the part always carries the whole image of neglect.
senses.whyCN: 在指整片街区之前，这个词先能指一间破屋；局部始终带着「被疏于照料」的整体印象，于是单间住房的义项自然存在。

senses.title: Any squalid crowded place
senses.definition: a place, or a setting, that is extremely dirty, crowded, and disordered
senses.definitionCN: 极其脏乱拥挤、缺乏秩序的地方或环境
senses.example: The dormitory after the game was a complete slum.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛后的宿舍简直像个贫民窟，脏乱不堪。
senses.why: Once the image is lodged, it travels to any space that is packed, messy, and unloved, from dormitories to kitchens.
senses.whyCN: 意象一旦成形，就会迁移到任何拥挤、凌乱、无人打理的空间，从宿舍到厨房都是如此。

senses.title: A slum area as a legal object
senses.titleCN: 需要整治的贫民窟地段
senses.definition: an area officially classed as unfit for habitation and scheduled for repair or demolition
senses.definitionCN: 被官方认定为不宜居住、须修复或拆除的地段
senses.example: The council declared the riverbank slum a clearance area.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会宣布河岸那片贫民窟为拆除整治区。
senses.why: Town planning turned the image into a category: a district marked on a map as unfit, to be cleared or rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 城市规划把这个意象变成了分类：地图上被标为「不宜居住」、须清理或重建的街区，于是长出了规划与法律层面的义项。

senses.title: To live very cheaply
senses.definition: to live in very poor or uncomfortable conditions, often out of choice for a while
senses.definitionCN: （口语）过十分简朴或艰苦的日子，常指出于某种选择而短期为之
senses.example: We slummed it in a cheap hostel for the whole trip.
senses.exampleCN: 整趟旅行我们都住廉价旅社，过得挺将就。
senses.why: The verb slum it takes the district image as a temporary condition a well-off person chooses to endure.
senses.whyCN: 动词搭配 slum it 把贫民窟当成一种临时处境，由条件宽裕的人主动选择去忍受，于是长出「将就过日子」的动词义。

senses.title: To visit poorer places out of curiosity
senses.titleCN: 屈尊造访；下到偏僻之地
senses.definition: to visit poor districts or cheap places, usually from a position of comfort and curiosity
senses.definitionCN: 出于好奇从优越处境到贫穷地区或廉价场所去看看
senses.example: The reporters slummed through the back streets for a story.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们到后街的穷巷里转了一圈，想找点素材。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century visitors famously toured slums as spectacles, so the verb kept a trace of slumming as sightseeing from above.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的访客曾把贫民窟当作景观去参观，动词里因此残留「居高临下地看热闹」的意味。

senses.title: The slum as a literary symbol
senses.definition: a setting associated with poverty, neglect, and social injustice in novels and reports
senses.definitionCN: 在小说和报道里象征贫穷、冷落与社会不公的场景
senses.example: Novels of the period took the slum as their moral center.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时期的小说常把贫民窟当作道德关怀的中心。
senses.why: Social writers turned the physical district into a moral image, so slum could stand for neglect as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 社会派作家把具体的街区提升为道德意象，slum 因此能整体代表「被社会遗忘」这件事。

senses.title: Squalor as a quality
senses.definition: the quality of being squalid, cramped, and uncared for, especially in housing
senses.definitionCN: 破败、拥挤、无人打理的品质，尤指住房条件
senses.example: Critics attacked the slum conditions in the new workers blocks.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击新建工人公寓里的贫民窟式条件。
senses.why: In compounds such as slum conditions, the noun works as a modifier for the quality itself rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 在 slum conditions 这类复合结构里，名词不再指地点，而是修饰「条件」本身，于是抽象地表示破败脏乱的品质。

intro.en: Slum appears in 1812 apparently from a slang word for a room, possibly related to the cant term slum meaning a trick; the deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: slum 于一八一二年出现，一般认为来自指「房间」的俚语，可能与黑话中表示「花招」的 slum 有关，更早的词源不确定。

items.en: The cant form slum is recorded with a sense such as a trick or a low room, though which sense came first is uncertain.
items.cn: 黑话形式 slum 有「花招」或「低下的房间」等义，哪一义在前并不确定。

items.en: Slum is first attested as a back alley, a room, or a low lodging place, and some sources connect it with the Irish term for a crowd or heap.
items.cn: slum 最早指后巷、房间或低级寄宿处；也有资料把它与爱尔兰语里表示「人群、堆」的词联系起来。

items.en: The modern sense, a run-down district of a city, is recorded by the 1820s in London writing.
items.cn: 现代的「城市破败街区」义在十九世纪二十年代伦敦的文字里已有记录。

items.en: The verb to slum appears, and slumming names well-off people touring poor districts.
items.cn: 动词 to slum 出现，slumming 指条件优渥者到贫穷街区游逛。

items.en: Reformers and novelists made the slum a fixed image of urban poverty.
items.cn: 改革者与小说家把贫民窟固化为城市贫困的典型意象。

items.en: The word extends to any squalid place and to compounds such as slum clearance and slum dweller.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何脏乱之处，并进入 slum clearance 与 slum dweller 等复合结构。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short sl- words that share only sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for bad housing and poverty with different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收了一批只共享读音的短词；近义组收了与糟糕住房、贫困有关的词，彼此范围不同。

entries.definition: A literary word for sleep or a state of rest; it merely looks similar and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「睡眠、安睡」，属文学用语；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sudden fall in prices or a period of poor trade; it merely looks similar and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「暴跌、萧条」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning like a slum, dirty and badly kept; formed from slum plus the suffix -y.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「贫民窟式的、破旧脏乱的」，由本词加后缀 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A poor crowded district that people belong to because of their class or background.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贫民聚居区」，指因阶层或背景而聚居的穷困街区。

entries.definition: An area of roughly built huts or sheds, often on the edge of a city.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「棚户区」，指城市边缘用简陋材料搭建的住区。

entries.definition: A small dirty house or hut; it names one dwelling rather than a whole district.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「破旧的陋屋」，只指一栋房子，不指整片街区。

entries.definition: A Brazilian term for an informal settlement on the edge of a large city.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（巴西的）贫民区」，指大城市边缘的非正式聚居地，多作专名。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real phrase patterns of slum and the words it commonly stands beside.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 slum 真实的搭配模式，以及它常见的搭配词。

normal.en: Slum is a noun for a district and a verb for living cheaply, and the noun is far more common.
normal.cn: slum 作名词指街区，作动词指将就过穷日子，名词用法要常见得多。

normal.en: Slum clearance is the official phrase for pulling run-down housing down.
normal.cn: slum clearance 是「清理贫民窟」的官方说法。

normal.en: Slum it is informal and means putting up with poor conditions for a while.
normal.cn: slum it 属口语，指将就着过一段艰苦日子。

normal.en: The plural slums is used in the same way as any other countable district noun.
normal.cn: 复数 slums 与其它可数地点名词用法相同。

normal.en: Do not confuse slum with slump: a slump is an economic fall, not a poor district.
normal.cn: 不要把 slum 和 slump 弄混：slump 是经济下跌，不是穷街区。

abstract.en: Picture a single broken window with a shirt drying on the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇破窗，窗框上晾着一件衬衫。

abstract.en: Imagine a row of shacks packed so tightly that no sun reaches the lane.
abstract.cn: 想象一排板棚挤得太紧，阳光照不进小巷。

abstract.en: Think of a rich tourist stepping carefully over a dirty puddle out of curiosity.
abstract.cn: 想象一位富裕的游客出于好奇，小心地跨过一滩脏水。

examples.en: The city finally cleared the slum beside the station.
examples.cn: 这座城市终于清理了车站旁的贫民窟。

examples.en: He slummed it in a friend of a friend flat for three weeks.
examples.cn: 他在朋友的朋友的一套公寓里将就住了三个星期。

examples.en: The report describes the slum as unfit for families with children.
examples.cn: 报告称那片贫民窟不适合有孩子的家庭居住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「湿烂木」——雨一淋，木屋又湿又烂，挤成一片片的穷街区；这只是读音联想，不是词源。

root: 来源不确定：slum 最早见于一八一二年，一般认为来自指「房间」或「后巷」的俚语，也可能与黑话中表示「花招」的词或爱尔兰语里「人群、堆」的词有关；词根并无可靠的拉丁语或古英语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one dense, neglected district and move outward to a single dwelling, any squalid place, an official planning category, the act of living cheaply or touring poor streets, a literary symbol, and finally the quality of squalor itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一片拥挤破败的街区出发，向外扩展：单间陋屋、任何脏乱之处、规划与法律上的地块类别、将就过日子的动作、到穷街游逛的动作，再到文学象征，最后是脏乱破败这一性质本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tight cluster of low, patched roofs at the edge of a city, with rainwater dripping from a broken edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：城市边缘一片低矮、打着补丁的屋顶紧紧相挨，破屋檐上滴着雨水。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the district of poverty is the everyday sense and the anchor of the family.
branches.cn: 地点线：贫穷街区是最常用的义项，也是整个词族的锚点。

branches.en: THE SCALE: one shabby dwelling and any squalid space are the same image at smaller and larger sizes.
branches.cn: 尺度线：一栋破屋与任何脏乱之处，是同一意象在大小不同尺度上的呈现。

branches.en: THE ADMINISTRATION: planned removal and the abstract quality both treat the image as a category to be measured.
branches.cn: 管理线：拆除规划与抽象品质都把这一意象当作可测量、可分类的对象。

branches.en: THE ACT: living cheaply and touring poor streets turn the district into something one does.
branches.cn: 动作线：将就过活与到穷街游逛，把街区变成了人去做的事情。

branches.en: THE IMAGE: literature makes the district a symbol of neglect and injustice.
branches.cn: 意象线：文学把街区升华成冷落与不公的象征。

intro.en: Slum is a short opaque word: English builds its family with the suffix -y and the combining form -like rather than with Latin pieces.
intro.cn: slum 是一个词根不透明的短词；英语只靠后缀 -y 和构词成分 -like 扩展词族，没有拉丁语部件。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor or cognate is recorded for slum, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: slum 没有可考的拉丁语来源或同源词，因此拉丁同源词表留空。

items.example: The noun is the center of the family.
items.exampleCN: 名词是整个词族的中心。

items.example: The plural follows the ordinary -s pattern.
items.exampleCN: 复数按常规加 -s 构成。

items.meaning: to live cheaply, to tour poor places
items.meaningCN: 将就过活；到穷地方游逛
items.example: The verb appears mostly in informal English.
items.exampleCN: 动词用法多出现在口语中。

items.meaning: the act of living or touring in this way
items.meaningCN: （现在分词或动名词）如此过活或游逛
items.example: Slumming names the act, not the place.
items.exampleCN: slumming 指的是行为，不是地点。

items.example: The suffix -y forms slummy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 slummy。

items.example: The form -like gives slumlike.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -like 构成 slumlike。

items.example: The compound comes from town planning.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词来自城市规划领域。

items.meaning: a person living in a slum
items.example: Dweller names the person living there.
items.exampleCN: dweller 指住在其中的人。

items.meaning: to put up with rough conditions
items.example: Slum it is a fixed informal phrase.
items.exampleCN: slum it 是固定的口语短语。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「贫民窟式的、破旧脏乱的」
由本词加 -like「像……一样」构成，义为「像贫民窟的」
